mcqs.subject: Anatomy
mcqs.question: A neuroanatomist examines a section of a dorsal root ganglion from a patient with herpes zoster. Which type of neuron is found there. [Prof 25. HITEC 26. WMC 25]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Sensory ganglia (DRG, cranial sensory ganglia) contain pseudounipolar neurons with satellite cells. Bipolar: retina, olfactory epithelium, spiral and vestibular ganglia. Multipolar: motor neurons, autonomic ganglia.

mcqs.subject: Anatomy
mcqs.question: A man's radial nerve is cut in a knife injury and is repaired surgically; function slowly recovers over months. Which cells guide axonal regrowth? [Prof 25]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Peripheral nerve regeneration: Schwann cells proliferate to form bands of Bungner that guide sprouting axons (~1 mm/day). CNS axons do not regenerate well: oligodendrocyte inhibitors + astrocytic glial scar.

mcqs.subject: Anatomy
mcqs.question: A 28-year-old woman with multiple sclerosis has demyelinating plaques in the brain. Which cells normally form myelin in the CNS? [Prof 25. BWP 26. MUL 25]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Oligodendrocytes myelinate CNS axons (one cell 4 many internodes); destroyed in MS. Schwann cells myelinate PNS axons (one cell 4 one internode); affected in Guillain-Barre.

mcqs.subject: Anatomy
mcqs.question: A 14-year-old boy has headaches and ataxia; MRI shows a cystic cerebellar tumour with a mural nodule arising from glial cells. What is the most likely neuroglial tumour. [LHR 25]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Astrocytomas are the commonest gliomas; pilocytic astrocytoma (GFAP+. Rosenthal fibres) is the commonest childhood brain tumour, usually cerebellar. Schwannoma is not a glioma.

mcqs.subject: Anatomy
mcqs.question: A surgeon repairing a crushed peripheral nerve notes that recovery is good when the connective-tissue tubes around each fibre are intact. Regeneration of axons requires the integrity of which sheath? [LHR 25]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Endoneurial tubes (with Schwann cells) guide regenerating axons." axonotmesis (tubes intact) recovers well. neurotmesis (nerve cut) needs surgical repair. Perineurium forms the blood-nerve barrier.

mcqs.subject: Anatomy
mcqs.question: A patient with Guillain-Barré syndrome has demyelination of peripheral nerves. What is the function of Schwann cells? [CKMC 25]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Schwann cells (neural crest) myelinate one internode of one PNS axon or ensheath many unmyelinated axons," they also support regeneration. Tumour = schwannoma (s-iocik).

mcqs.subject: Anatomy
mcqs.question: A pathologist examines anterior horn cells in a spinal cord section from a patient with ALS. What type of neurons are they? [HITEC 25]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Anterior horn cells are large multipolar neurons with prominent Nissl substance (RER) and many dendrites; ALS destroys them along with corticospinal neurons (UMN + LMN signs).

mcqs.subject: Anatomy
mcqs.question: A 60-year-old man with Parkinson disease dies; histology of the substantia nigra shows loss of a specific pigmented neuron. Which neurons are most affected? [QIMS 25]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Substantia nigra pars compacta and locus coeruleus neurons contain neuromelanin (catecholamine by-product). Lipofuscin = "wear and tear" pigment accumulating with age.

mcqs.subject: Anatomy
mcqs.question: Histology of brain tissue days after a stroke shows cells engulfing debris and lipid. Which cell type is responsible. [QIMS 25]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Microglia (mesodermal, monocyte-macrophage lineage, yolk-sac origin) are the CNS phagocytes; become lipid-laden "gitter cells" after infarction and are HIV reservoirs (multinucleated giant cells).

mcqs.subject: Anatomy
mcqs.question: A histologist identifies giant pyramidal neurons in layer V of the precentral gyrus whose axons form part of the corticospinal tract. What are these cells called? [AMC 26. BWP 26]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Betz cells." largest neurons of the cerebral cortex, layer V of area 4; contribute ~3¥0 of CST fibres. Purkinje cells are the output neurons of the cerebellar cortex.

mcqs.subject: Anatomy
mcqs.question: A neuropathologist examines the lining of the lateral ventricle in a patient with ventriculitis. Which cells line the ventricles. [AMC 26]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Ependymal cells: ciliated cuboidal/columnar glia lining ventricles and central canal; modified ependyma forms choroid epithelium," tanycytes in the third ventricle floor. Tumour: ependymoma (perivascular pseudorosettes).

mcqs.subject: Anatomy
mcqs.question: A neuropathologist explains that microglia behave like macrophages. From which tissue are microglia derived? [LHR 26]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: All other CNS glia (astrocytes, oligodendrocytes, ependyma) are neuroectodermal; microglia derive from mesodermal (yolk-sac) myeloid precursors.

mcqs.subject: Anatomy
mcqs.question: A pathologist looks for Nissl granules in a section containing the spinal nerve roots. Which structure contains neuronal cell bodies with Nissl granules. [CKMC 26]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Nissl bodies = RER in neuronal cell bodies and dendrites (absent from axon and axon hillock). Roots and nerves contain only axons," DRG contains pseudounipolar cell bodies. Chromatolysis follows axon injury.

mcqs.subject: Anatomy
mcqs.question: A neuropathologist explains how CSF is propelled through the ventricles. Which histological feature of the ventricular lining helps move CSF? [HITEC 26]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Ependymal cells bear cilia and microvilli; ciliary beating helps CSF flow. Choroid plexus epithelium (modified ependyma) has tight junctions forming the blood-CSF barrier.

mcqs.subject: Anatomy
mcqs.question: After an ischaemic stroke, glial cells around the infarct buffer potassium, take up glutamate and form a scar. Which CNS cells provide metabolic and structural support to neurons. [BWP 26]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Astrocytes (GFAP+): K. buffering, glutamate reuptake, glycogen store/lactate shuttle. BBB induction (end-feet), glial scar (gliosis). Tumour: astrocytoma/glioblastoma.

mcqs.subject: Anatomy
mcqs.question: A newborn has a lumbar sac covered by thin membrane containing meninges and spinal cord tissue, with paralysis of the legs. Defective development of which structure causes this? [Prof 25 . HITEC 26. KIMS 26. BWP 25]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Meningomyelocele = failure of caudal neural tube closure (posterior neuropore, day 28) with protrusion of meninges + cord. Raised maternal AFP; prevented by periconceptional folic acid.

mcqs.subject: Anatomy
mcqs.question: An infant has a lumbosacral swelling; imaging shows the central canal of the cord within the sac is dilated (syringomyelocele). With which condition is this associated? [Prof 25]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Syringomyelocele = meningomyelocele in which the herniated cord has a dilated central canal (syringomyelia/hydromyelia). Spina bifida cystica types: meningocele, meningomyelocele, myeloschisis.

mcqs.subject: Anatomy
mcqs.question: A stillborn fetus has a completely open spinal cord exposed along the back with no covering of meninges or skin. Failure of the neural folds to elevate and fuse results in which condition. [AMC 25]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Rachischisis = neural folds never fuse ￿ open neural plate. Cranially = anencephaly (craniorachischisis if total). Meningocele/meningomyelocele = closed tube herniating through a vertebral defect.

mcqs.subject: Anatomy
mcqs.question: An infant has a long, narrow, boat-shaped skull. X-ray shows premature f usion of one suture. Early closure of which suture causes scaphocephaly. [AMC 26. BWP 26. AMC 25]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Sagittal ￿ scaphocephaly (commonest); bilateral coronal ￿ brachycephaly/oxycephaly (turricephaly); unilateral coronal/lambdoid ￿ plagiocephaly; metopic 4 trigonocephaly.

mcqs.subject: Anatomy
mcqs.question: A school child is noted to have a tuft of hair and a dimple over the lower back; neurological examination is normal. What does this suggest? [LHR 25 . MUL 25]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Spina bifida occulta: failure of vertebral arch fvsion (usually L5/SI) covered by skin. often with hair tuft. dimple, lipoma or naevus," usually asymptomatic," AFP normal.

mcqs.subject: Anatomy
mcqs.question: A newborn has a skin-covered lumbar sac that transilluminates; it contains only meninges and CSF, with normal leg movement. What is the basic defect in meningocele. [BWP 26. CKMC 25. KIMS 25]

options.B: Failure of vertebral arches to fuse

mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Spina bifida = failure of fusion of vertebral arches (sclerotome); meningocele = meninges herniate through it; meningomyelocele adds cord tissue (neural tube involvement).

mcqs.subject: Anatomy
mcqs.question: A 2-year-old has a still-open anterior fontanelle and a large skull because of defective ossification of the cranial vault. From which tissue does the neurocranium (cranial vault) develop? [CKMC 25. BWP 25]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Neurocranium: membranous vault (frontal. parietal) from neural crest and paraxial mesoderm: chondrocranium (base) from paraxial mesoderm (occipital sclerotomes) and neural crest. Anterior fontanelle closes- 18 months; delayed in rickets. hypothyroidism, hydrocephalus.

mcqs.subject: Anatomy
mcqs.question: An embryology student traces the derivatives of the five secondary brain vesicles. Which structure develops from the telencephalon. [MUL 25]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Telencephalon 4 cerebral hemispheres (cortex incl. hippocampus, basal nuclei, lateral ventricles). Diencephalon 4 thalamus, hypothalamus, retina, posterior pituitary, pineal. Mesencephalon ￿ midbrain.

mcqs.subject: Anatomy
mcqs.question: A woman asks when the lower end of the fetal spinal cord closes, as she started folic acid late. On which day does the posterior (caudal) neuropore close? [MUL 25]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Neural tube closure starts at day 22 (cervical region); anterior (cranial) neuropore closes day 25-26, posterior (caudal) neuropore day 27-28. Failure anencephaly and spina bifida respectively.

mcqs.subject: Anatomy
mcqs.question: An infant has an abnormally shaped skull because a suture closed before birth. What is premature closure of a cranial suture called? [MUL 25]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Craniosynostosis = premature suture fusion; skull grows parallel to the fvsed suture (sagittal 4 scaphocephaly). Associated with FGFR mutations (Crouzon, Apert). Cranioschisis = failure of skull vault to form (anencephaly).

mcqs.subject: Anatomy
mcqs.question: An embryology lecturer explains that the sensory (dorsal) part of the neural tube forms most of the diencephalon. From which part do the thalamus and hypothalamus develop. [MUL 25]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: The diencephalon develops only from alar and roof plates (no basal plate): thalamus, hypothalamus from alar; choroid plexus and pineal from roof plate.

mcqs.subject: Anatomy
mcqs.question: An MRI of a child shows absence of the largest non-olfactory commissure that normally appears around the 10th week. Which commissure is this. [WMC 25]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Langman: anterior commissure forms first (olfactory bulb + temporal lobe fibres), then hippocampal (fornix) commissure; corpus callosum (non-olfactory neocortical) appears by the 10th week in the lamina terminalis. Key note: source keyed anterior commissure.

mcqs.subject: Anatomy
mcqs.question: A child with a cerebellopontine angle mass has vestibular symptoms. The nerve supplying the macula of the saccule and utricle attaches to the [WMC 25] brainstem in a region derived from which vesicle.
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Metencephalon 4 pons and cerebellum (CN V-vlll nuclei largely); myelencephalon 4 medulla (IX-XII). CN Vlll enters at the pontomedullaryjunction.

mcqs.subject: Anatomy
mcqs.question: A routine 16-week ultrasound shows absence of the cranial vault and forebrain; maternal AFP is very high. Failure of closure of which structure causes anencephaly? [WMC 26. HITEC 26. BWP 26. KIMS 26. WMC 25 . QIMS 25]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Anencephaly: anterior neuropore fails to close (day 25) 4 exposed degenerated brain, no calvaria; polyhydramnios (no swallowing). Prevent with 0.4 mg folic acid (4 mg if previous NTD).

mcqs.subject: Anatomy
mcqs.question: An embryologist explains which part of the neural tube forms anterior horn cells. From which plate are motor neurons derived? [BWP 25]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Sulcus limitans divides the tube: basal plate (ventral) ￿ motor neurons (anterior and lateral horns); alar plate (dorsal) ￿ sensory/association neurons (posterior horn).

mcqs.subject: Anatomy
mcqs.question: A newborn with lumbosacral meningomyelocele also has hydrocephalus; MRI shows the cerebellar vermis and medulla herniated through the foramen magnum. With which developmental failure is Chiari11 malformation associated? [BWP 25]

options.A: Failure of caudal neuropore closure (open spinal defect)

mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Chiari11: CSF leak through an open spinal NTD 4 small posterior fossa 4 hindbrain herniation, aqueductal stenosis, hydrocephalus. Chiari l." tonsils only, adults, syringomyelia. Key note: source keyed cranial neuropore.

mcqs.subject: Anatomy
mcqs.question: A neonate's skull X-ray shows wide sutures between the frontal and parietal bones. How do the flat bones of the skull vault develop? [BWP 25]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Membranous neurocranium (vault: frontal, parietal, squamous temporal and occipital) ossifies in membrane: chondrocranium (skull base) by endochondral ossification.

mcqs.subject: Anatomy
mcqs.question: A newborn has dilated lateral and third ventricles but a normal fourth ventricle; MRI shows aqueductal obstruction. Which developmental process was disrupted? [QIMS 25]

options.C: Canalization of the mesencephalic part of the neural tube

mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: The mesencephalon cavity becomes the cerebral aqueduct; congenital aqueductal stenosis (X-linked LICAM, infections like toxoplasmosis) is the commonest cause of congenital hydrocephalus.

mcqs.subject: Anatomy
mcqs.question: A 3-year-old girl has conductive deafness; CT shows a poorly developed middle ear cavity. Malformation of which pharyngeal pouch is responsible. [KIMS 25]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: First pouch 4 tubotympanic recess (middle ear cavity, auditory tube, inner layer of tympanic membrane). Second 4 palatine tonsil; third 4 inferior parathyroid, thymus; fourth 4 superior parathyroid.

mcqs.subject: Anatomy
mcqs.question: During the 5th week, the forebrain vesicle subdivides. Into which parts does the prosencephalon differentiate. [KIMS 25]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: 3-vesicle stage (4th week): prosencephalon, mesencephalon, rhombencephalon. 5-vesicle stage (5th week): telencephalon, diencephalon, mesencephalon, metencephalon, myelencephalon.

mcqs.subject: Anatomy
mcqs.question: A newborn has flaccid paralysis of both legs and a lumbosacral open neural tube defect. Failure of closure of which structure is responsible. [AMC 26. CKMC 26]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Caudal (posterior) neuropore closes-day 28,. failure 4 spina bifida aperta (meningomyelocele, myeloschisis). Rostral neuropore failure anencephaly.

mcqs.subject: Anatomy
mcqs.question: An infant with scaphocephaly has premature fusion of a suture of the skull vault. Premature fusion within which part of the skull causes scaphocephaly. [CKMC 26]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Sutures lie between flat membrane bones of the vault (membranous neurocranium): sagittal suture synostosis ￿ scaphocephaly.

mcqs.subject: Anatomy
mcqs.question: An embryology student identifies three brain flexures in a 6-week embryo. Between which regions does the pontine flexure lie. [MUL 26]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Flexures: cephalic (mesencephalic) and cervical flexures are ventral; pontine flexure is dorsal, between metencephalon and myelencephalon. thinning the roof of the fourth ventricle.

mcqs.subject: Anatomy
mcqs.question: A mother asks when her baby's soft spot on top of the head will close. At about what age does the anterior fontanelle close. [BWP 26]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Anterior fontanelle (diamond. at bregma) closes by~ 18 months," posterior fontanelle (triangular, lambda) by 2~3 months; sphenoid -6 months; mastoid 6-18 months.

mcqs.subject: Anatomy
mcqs.question: An embryology question shows a cross-section of the developing medulla with the sulcus limitans marked. Which medullary cranial nerve nucleus develops from the basal plate. [HITEC 26]

options.A: Spinal nucleus of the trigeminal nerve

mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Stem created: the source recall was incomplete (the original used an image "black arrow"). Basal plate (medial to sulcus limitans) 4 motor nuclei (Xll, nucleus ambiguus, dorsal vagal),. alar plate (lateral) 4 sensory nuclei (vestibular, cochlear, spinal V, solitary).

mcqs.subject: Anatomy
mcqs.question: A woman with vitamin B12 deficiency loses vibration and position sense in both legs. A medulla section shows degeneration of the second-order neurons. Where do the first-order neurons of the DCML pathway synapse? [Prof 24]

options.B: Dorsal horn of the spinal cord

mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: DCML.. 1st order = DRG 4 ascend ipsilaterally in fasciculus gracilis/cuneatus ￿ synapse in nucleus gracilis/cuneatus (lower medulla) 4 internal arcuate fibres cross 4 medial lemniscus 4 VPL ￿ postcentral gyrus.

mcqs.subject: Anatomy
mcqs.question: A 30-year-old man has a cape-like loss of pain and temperature over both shoulders and arms, with preserved touch and vibration. He has painless burns on his hands. What is the diagnosis. [Prof 25]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Syringomyelia (cervical cyst around central canal) first damages crossing spinothalamic fibres in the anterior white commissure 4 bilateral, segmental (cape) loss of pain/temperature with dissociated sensory loss. Enlarging syrinx 4 LMN wasting of hands.

mcqs.subject: Anatomy
mcqs.question: A man stabbed in the back has loss of pain and temperature on the left side of the body starting two segments below the level of the lesion. Which tract is damaged? [Prof 25]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: The lateral spinothalamic tract carries pain/temperature from the CONTRALATERAL body (fibres cross 1~2 segments above entry). Left-sided loss = right tract lesion.

mcqs.subject: Anatomy
mcqs.question: After a hyperextension neck injury, an elderly man has weakness of both arms much more than legs, with variable sensory loss. What is the diagnosis. [Prof 25]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Central cord syndrome: hyperextension in a spondylotic neck 4 central grey matter and medial (cervical) corticospinal fibres damaged 4 upper limbs > lower limbs, often with sacral sparing.

mcqs.subject: Anatomy
mcqs.question: A child with poliomyelitis has a flaccid, wasted leg with absent reflexes but normal sensation. Damage to which structure causes this lower motor neuron palsy. [Prof 25]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Poliovirus destroys anterior horn (a motor) cells 4 LMN signs: flaccid paralysis, atrophy. fasciculations, areflexia; sensation is intact.

mcqs.subject: Anatomy
mcqs.question: On a coronal MRI of a patient with hydrocephalus, the radiologist traces the walls of the dilated lateral ventricle. Which structure forms boundary of both the body and the inferior horn of the lateral ventricle? [AMC 25]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Caudate nucleus follows the C-shape of the ventricle." head/body in the floor-lateral wall of anterior horn and body, tail in the roof of the inferior horn. Key note: source keyed thalamus, which floors only the body.

mcqs.subject: Anatomy
mcqs.question: A man stabbed in the back has a right hemisection of the cord at TIO. Which signs occur at the level of the lesion? [AMC 26. AMC 25]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Brown-sequard." at the level - ipsilateral LMN palsy and band of anaesthesia," below - ipsilateral UMN paralysis + loss of DC sensation, contralateral loss of pain/temperature (from 1-2 segments below).

mcqs.subject: Anatomy
mcqs.question: A young man is stabbed in the back and has a hemisection of the spinal cord. Which sensation is lost on the same side below the lesion. [LHR 25]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Ipsilateral below lesion: dorsal column loss (proprioception, vibration. fine touch) + UMN paralysis. Contralateral: pain and temperature loss.

mcqs.subject: Anatomy
mcqs.question: A 50-year-old man with a thoracic cord tumour cannot move his legs, which are spastic with brisk reflexes. Which tract is involved? [HITEC 26. LHR 25 . CKMC 25. QIMS 25]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Lateral corticospinal tract: crossed fibres in the lateral funiculus, laminated with sacral fibres lateral and cervical medial; supplies all limb muscles. The anterior CST (uncrossed) supplies axial muscles.

mcqs.subject: Anatomy
mcqs.question: A child with Friedreich ataxia has an unsteady gait due to loss of unconscious proprioceptive input to the cerebellum. Which tract carries unconscious proprioception? [LHR 25]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Spinocerebellar tracts (dorsal, ventral, cuneocerebellar) carry unconscious proprioception to the ipsilateral cerebellum. Conscious proprioception travels in the dorsal columns.

mcqs.subject: Anatomy
mcqs.question: A child with Friedreich ataxia has degeneration of the nucleus dorsalis (Clarke column) in the thoracic cord. Which tract arises from Clarke column. [CKMC 25]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Clarke nucleus (C8-L3, lamina Vll) ￿ uncrossed dorsal spinocerebellar tract 4 inferior cerebellar peduncle. Above C8 the equivalent is the accessory cuneate nucleus ￿ cuneocerebellar tract.

mcqs.subject: Anatomy
mcqs.question: A patient in decerebrate posture has marked extensor rigidity of all limbs. Which descending tract mainly facilitates extensor (antigravity) muscles. [CKMC 25. WMC 25]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Lateral vestibulospinal (and pontine reticulospinal) tracts excite extensor antigravity motor neurons," rubrospinal and corticospinal favour flexors. Decerebration releases vestibular/pontine extensor drive.

mcqs.subject: Anatomy
mcqs.question: A stroke patient loses skilled finger movements of the opposite hand. Which is the major tract controlling skilled upper-limb movement? [CKMC 25]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Lateral CST synapses (some directly) on motor neurons of distal limb muscles," it is essential for fractionated finger movements. Rubrospinal tract in humans is small, aiding flexor tone of upper limb.

mcqs.subject: Anatomy
mcqs.question: A patient with a cervical syrinx has cape-like loss of pain and temperature with preserved touch. Which fibres are damaged first? [CKMC 25]

options.A: Decussating fibres in the anterior white commissure

mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: A central cavity first interrupts second-order pain/temperature fibres crossing in the anterior white commissure 4 bilateral segmental loss. Spinothalamic fibres from lower levels (already in the tract) are spared.

mcqs.subject: Anatomy
mcqs.question: Before a lumbar puncture in an adult, a student is asked where the spinal cord ends. At which vertebral level does the conus medullaris end in adults: [MUL 25]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Cord ends at lower border Ll/upper L2 in adults (L3 in newborns); dural sac ends at S2. LP is done at L3-L4/L4-L5 (line joining iliac crests at L4).

mcqs.subject: Anatomy
mcqs.question: A patient with an anterolateral cord lesion loses pain, temperature and crude touch on the opposite side of the body below the lesion. Which tracts are involved? [WMC 25]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: The anterolateral system (lateral + anterior spinothalamic) carries pain. temperature and crude touch from the contralateral side. Source stem said "same side"; spinothalamic loss is contralateral to the lesion.

mcqs.subject: Anatomy
mcqs.question: A man with a C5-C7 cervical radiculopathy has weakness of the shoulder and pectoral muscles but normal sensation. Lesion of which structures causes pure motor weakness. [WMC 25]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Ventral roots contain motor (and preganglionic autonomic) fibres," dorsal roots carry sensory fibres from DRG cells (Bell-magendie law).

mcqs.subject: Anatomy
mcqs.question: A man with tabes dorsalis sways and falls when he closes his eyes while standing with feet together, but is steady with eyes open. A positive Romberg sign indicates a lesion of which pathway. [WMC 25]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Romberg positive = sensory ataxia (dorsal columns, large-fibre neuropathy) compensated by vision. Cerebellar ataxia is present with eyes open as well (Romberg negative).

mcqs.subject: Anatomy
mcqs.question: A neuroanatomy student studies how f ibres are arranged in the dorsal columns at the cervical level. Where are new incoming fibres added in the dorsal column. [HITEC 25]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Dorsal columns: sacral fibres most medial, cervical most lateral (new fibres added laterally) - gracilis (lower body) medial to cuneatus (upper body).

mcqs.subject: Anatomy
mcqs.question: A neurosurgeon performing cordotomy notes that sacral fibres lie superficially in the spinothalamic tract. Where are new incoming fibres added in the spinothalamic tract? [HITEC 25]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Spinothalamic and lateral corticospinal tracts: sacral fibres lateral (superficial), cervical medial new fibres are added medially. Intramedullary tumours spare sacral sensation (sacral sparing).

mcqs.subject: Anatomy
mcqs.question: A man with a knife wound to the left side of the thoracic cord is examined. Which findings characterize Brown-sequard syndrome. [AMC 26. CKMC 26. KIMS 26. MUL 25. HITEC 25. BWP 25. KIMS 25]

options.D: Ipsilateral paralysis and proprioception loss; contralateral pain and temperature loss

mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Hemisection: ipsilateral UMN paralysis (CST) + DC loss; contralateral spinothalamic loss beginning 1-2 segments below; ipsilateral LMN/anaesthetic band at the level.

mcqs.subject: Anatomy
mcqs.question: A 45-year-old man has loss of pain and temperature on the right side below the umbilicus and paralysis of the left leg. Which tract is involved on the side of the lesion. [QIMS 25]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Left hemisection at ~T8: left CST (left paralysis), left spinothalamic (right pain/temp loss), left DC (left proprioception loss).

mcqs.subject: Anatomy
mcqs.question: A man with untreated syphilis has lightning pains, loss of vibration and position sense in both legs, a stamping gait and positive Romberg. Which condition is this. [QIMS 25]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Tabes dorsalis (tertiary syphilis): degeneration of dorsal roots and dorsal columns ￿ sensory ataxia, Argyll Robertson pupils, Charcot joints, absent reflexes.

mcqs.subject: Anatomy
mcqs.question: A loud noise at a building site makes pedestrians reflexly turn their heads towards it. Which tract mediates this reflex. [KIMS 26. KIMS 25]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Tectospinal tract (superior colliculus," inferior colliculus input for sound) crosses in the dorsal tegmental decussation 4 cervical cord ￿ reflex head turning to visual and auditory stimuli.

mcqs.subject: Anatomy
mcqs.question: A partial spinal cord lesion at T6 damages the dorsal columns on one side only. Which finding is expected below the lesion. [AMC 26]

options.A: Bilateral loss of pain and temperature
options.C: Ipsilateral loss of fine touch, vibration and position sense

mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Dorsal column fibres ascend ipsilaterally until they synapse in the medulla, so cord lesions give same-side DC Ioss.

mcqs.subject: Anatomy
mcqs.question: A cervical cord lesion damages the anterior horn cells and corticospinal tract at one segment. Which pattern of signs occurs. [AMC 26]

options.A: UMN signs at the level and LMN below
options.C: LMN signs at the level and UMN signs below
options.D: UMN signs only above the lesion

mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: At the level: anterior horn/root damage 4 LMN signs (wasting, areflexia). Below." interrupted CST 4 UMN signs (spasticity, hyperreflexia, Babinski).

mcqs.subject: Anatomy
mcqs.question: A neuroanatomy student lists descending tracts and their functions. Which descending tract is most important for maintaining posture and balance. [CKMC 26]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Lateral vestibulospinal (uncrossed, whole cord) ￿ antigravity extensor tone,. medial vestibulospinal (MLF) 4 head/neck position. Both are "medial system" tracts for posture.

mcqs.subject: Anatomy
mcqs.question: A student is asked which tract is essential for writing and buttoning a shirt. Which descending tract is primarily involved in skilled voluntary movement? [CKMC 26. KIMS 26]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Corticospinal (pyramidal) tract: fractionated, skilled distal movements; lesion causes loss of fine finger movements that seldom recover fully.

mcqs.subject: Anatomy
mcqs.question: A man with burns on his hand feels no pain because of a cord lesion. Which tract carries pain and temperature sensation? [CKMC 26]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Lateral spinothalamic tract (anterolateral system): pain and temperature from the contralateral body, crossing in the anterior white commissure.

mcqs.subject: Anatomy
mcqs.question: A man has impaired vibration and joint sense in both legs, positive Romberg sign and normal power. Which tract is most likely affected? [HITEC 26]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Fasciculus gracilis carries DC modalities from the lower limbs and lower trunk (below T6)," cuneatus from upper limbs and upper trunk (above T6). so it exists only in upper thoracic and cervical cord.

mcqs.subject: Anatomy
mcqs.question: A man has a right spinal cord hemisection from a knife wound. Which sensation is lost on the contralateral side below the lesion. [BWP 26]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Spinothalamic fibres have already crossed, so the hemisection cuts fibres from the opposite side ￿ contralateral pain and temperature loss.

mcqs.subject: Anatomy
mcqs.question: A man with loss of vibration and position sense in his legs walks with a high-stepping, stamping gait and watches his feet. Which additional finding is associated? [BWP 26]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Dorsal column loss 4 sensory ataxia (worse in dark/eyes closed, positive Romberg). pseudoathetosis of the outstretched hands.

mcqs.subject: Anatomy
mcqs.question: A man falls from a height and injures his spine at TIO. He has paralysis of both legs and loss of pain, temperature, f ine touch and proprioception below the umbilicus. Which cord lesion explains this? [KIMS 26]

options.B: Complete transection of the spinal cord

mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Stem created: the source recall was incomplete (the KIMS item was vague." "anterior/lateral column/horn"). Loss of all modalities + bilateral paralysis = complete transection; anterior cord syndrome spares dorsal columns; central cord affects arms more than legs.

mcqs.subject: Anatomy
mcqs.question: A midbrain lesion at the interpeduncular fossa causes ptosis, a dilated pupil and a "down and out" eye. Which cranial nerve emerges here. [Prof 25]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: CN111 emerges from the interpeduncular fossa, passes between PCA and superior cerebellar artery (Pcomm aneurysm compresses it 4 pupil involved first, as parasympathetic fibres are superficial).

mcqs.subject: Anatomy
mcqs.question: A 60~year-old man has a left oculomotor palsy with an involuntary tremor and ataxia of the right limbs. Where is the lesion. [Prof 25 . LHR 25 . HITEC 25]

options.A: Red nucleus in the midbrain tegmentum (Benedikt)

mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Benedikt syndrome: tegmental midbrain lesion (PCA branches) ￿ ipsilateral CN111 palsy + contralateral tremor/ataxia (red nucleus, superior cerebellar peduncle fibres). Weber: crus cerebri 4 CN111 + contralateral hemiplegia.

mcqs.subject: Anatomy
mcqs.question: A patient has an infarct of the right ventral (basilar) pons involving the corticospinal fibres. On which side does the limb weakness occur? [Prof 25]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Corticospinal fibres cross at the pyramidal decussation (lower medulla), so any lesion above it causes CONTRALATERAL hemiplegia. Medial pontine syndrome adds ipsilateral CN Vl palsy.

mcqs.subject: Anatomy
mcqs.question: A 60~year-old man has vertigo, hoarseness, ipsilateral facial pain/temperature loss, Horner syndrome and contralateral body pain/temperature loss. Occlusion of which artery causes this lateral medullary syndrome. [BWP 26. LHR 25. BWP 25]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Wallenberg: PICA/vertebral 4 spinal V nucleus (ipsilateral face), spinothalamic (contralateral body), nucleus ambiguus (dysphagia), vestibular nuclei, descending sympathetics (Horner), inferior cerebellar peduncle (ataxia).

mcqs.subject: Anatomy
mcqs.question: A patient with a pineal tumour compressing the dorsal midbrain loses visual ref lexes such as turning the eyes to a sudden f lash. Which nerve provides the main afferent input to the superior colliculus. [LHR 25]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Superior colliculus receives retinal fibres (via brachium of superior colliculus) and visual cortex input; it mediates visual reflexes and orienting eye/head movements (tectospinal tract).

mcqs.subject: Anatomy
mcqs.question: A patient with neurosyphilis has pupils that constrict on accommodation but not to light (Argyll Robertson pupils). Lesion of which midbrain structure impairs the light reflex but spares accommodation? [LHR 25]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Light reflex: retina 4 optic nerve/tract -> pretectal nucleus 4 both EW nuclei 4 CN1114 ciliary ganglion 4 sphincter pupillae. Accommodation bypasses the pretectum. Key note: source keyed EW (whose lesion abolishes both reflexes).

mcqs.subject: Anatomy
mcqs.question: A man has vertigo, nausea and horizontal nystagmus after a small infarct of the dorsolateral pons-medulla junction. Damage to which structure causes these? [LHR 25]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Vestibular nuclei (floor of the fourth ventricle) connect with the MLF (eye movements), cerebellum and spinal cord,. lesion 4 vertigo, nystagmus, imbalance, vomiting.

mcqs.subject: Anatomy
mcqs.question: A teenager with a pineal tumour cannot look upward and has pupils that react poorly to light. Damage to which region causes this upward gaze palsy. [CKMC 25]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Parinaud (dorsal midbrain) syndrome: compression of superior colliculus/pretectum and posterior commissure 4 upward gaze palsy, light-near dissociation, convergence-retraction nystagmus, lid retraction.

mcqs.subject: Anatomy
mcqs.question: A child with a brainstem tumour has impaired hearing. The ascending auditory fibres from the cochlear nuclei and superior olive are involved. Which tract forms the major auditory pathway in the brainstem? [CKMC 25]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Auditory path: cochlear nuclei 4 trapezoid body/superior olive 4 lateral lemniscus 4 inferior colliculus 4 MGB 4 areas 41/42. Bilateral representation ￿ unilateral cortical lesion causes no deafness.

mcqs.subject: Anatomy
mcqs.question: A child with a lower pontine tumour has weakness of all the muscles of one side of the face. Lesion of which nucleus causes this. [CKMC 25]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Facial motor nucleus lies in the caudal pontine tegmentum; its fibres loop around the abducens nucleus forming the facial colliculus. Lesion = LMN facial palsy (whole half of face).

mcqs.subject: Anatomy
mcqs.question: A man has left hemiplegia, left loss of vibration and position sense and deviation of the tongue to the right on protrusion. Where is the lesion. [CKMC 26. KIMS 26 . CKMC 25 . HITEC 25]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Medial medullary (Dejerine) syndrome - anterior spinal/vertebral artery: pyramid (contralateral hemiplegia), medial lemniscus (contralateral DC loss), Xll nucleus/fibres (ipsilateral tongue palsy).

mcqs.subject: Anatomy
mcqs.question: A 60-year-old man has a left dilated pupil, ptosis and "down and out" eye with right-sided hemiplegia. Which syndrome is this. [AMC 26. MUL25. HITEC 25 . QIMS 25]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Weber." crus cerebri + CN111 fibres (PCA paramedian branches) 4 ipsilateral111 palsy + contralateral hemiplegia. Claude: 111 + contralateral ataxia (dorsal tegmentum). Benedikt."111 + tremor/ataxia (red nucleus).

mcqs.subject: Anatomy
mcqs.question: A man with sudden vertigo and dysphagia is diagnosed with lateral medullary syndrome. Which feature is characteristic. [AMC 26. MUL 25]

options.A: Loss of proprioception in the body
options.D: Ipsilateral loss of pain and temperature on the face

mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Wallenberg: crossed sensory loss - IPSILATERAL face (spinal V tract/nucleus) and CONTRALATERAL body (spinothalamic). No hemiplegia (pyramids are medial) and no tongue palsy (Xll is medial).

mcqs.subject: Anatomy
mcqs.question: A neuroanatomy student studies the transverse f ibres in the ventral pontine tegmentum that carry auditory signals across the midline. With which nucleus is the trapezoid body closely related? [MUL 25]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Ventral cochlear nucleus fibres form the trapezoid body and synapse in the superior olivary complex (incl. nucleus of trapezoid body) - the first site of binaural sound localization. Key note: source keyed cochlear nucleus (origin of fibres).

mcqs.subject: Anatomy
mcqs.question: A neuroanatomy student traces f ibres from the pontine nuclei that cross the midline in the basal pons. What are these fibres and where do they go: [WMC 25]

options.A: Transverse pontine fibres to the opposite cerebellum (middle
options.B: Corticopontine fibres to the medulla peduncle)

mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Cortex 4 corticopontine fibres 4 pontine nuclei 4 transverse pontocerebellar fibres cross 4 middle cerebellar peduncle ￿ contralateral cerebrocerebellum. Source stem said "to medulla"; corrected.

mcqs.subject: Anatomy
mcqs.question: A patient with an optic tract lesion has impaired visual reflex orientation of the eyes in addition to f ield loss. Which brainstem structure receives fibres directly from the optic tract? [WMC 25]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Optic tract fibres end mainly in the LGB, with others reaching the superior colliculus (visual reflexes), pretectal nucleus (light reflex) and SCN (circadian rhythm).

mcqs.subject: Anatomy
mcqs.question: In a pontine lesion, a patient loses vibration and position sense on the opposite side. As what does the DCML pathway ascend through the brainstem. [CKMC 26. HITEC 25. QIMS 25]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: After crossing (internal arcuate fibres, sensory decussation) the second-order fibres ascend as the medial lemniscus - vertical in the medulla, horizontal in the pons - to VPL.

mcqs.subject: Anatomy
mcqs.question: A midbrain infarct causes ipsilateral third nerve palsy, contralateral tremor and contralateral loss of position sense. Which structures are involved in Benedikt syndrome. [HITEC 25]

options.A: Substantia nigra and crus cerebri only
options.D: Red nucleus and medial lemniscus (with CN111 fibres)

mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Benedikt = tegmental midbrain." CN111 fascicles + red nucleus/superior cerebellar peduncle (tremor, ataxia) + medial lemniscus (contralateral sensory loss).

mcqs.subject: Anatomy
mcqs.question: A man has a right lower motor neuron facial palsy, right lateral rectus palsy and left hemiplegia. Where is the lesion. [BWP 25]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Millard-Gubler syndrome: ventral caudal pons - CN VI/VII fascicles (ipsilateral) + corticospinal tract (contralateral hemiplegia). Key note: source keyed left caudal pons; cranial nerve signs localize the lesion to the SAME side.

mcqs.subject: Anatomy
mcqs.question: A patient has a left oculomotor palsy and right-sided limb weakness. Alternating (crossed) hemiplegia indicates a lesion of which region. [BWP 25]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Crossed signs (ipsilateral cranial nerve LMN palsy + contralateral hemiplegia) localize to the brainstem: midbrain (111- Weber), pons (Vl/VII - Millard-Gubler), medulla (Xll - medial medullary).

mcqs.subject: Anatomy
mcqs.question: A patient has left facial paralysis including the forehead, loss of the left corneal reflex blink and left lateral gaze palsy after a small pontine infarct. Which brainstem structure is involved? [QIMS 25]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Facial colliculus (floor of fourth ventricle) = abducens nucleus + looping facial fibres 4 ipsilateral LMN Vll palsy + horizontal gaze palsy. Corneal reflex efferent limb is Vll.

mcqs.subject: Anatomy
mcqs.question: A man after basilar artery thrombosis is quadriplegic and mute, has pinpoint pupils, but is fully conscious and blinks/moves his eyes vertically to communicate. Which structure is damaged? [QIMS 25]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Locked-in syndrome: bilateral ventral pontine infarction (corticospinal + corticobulbar) with preserved tegmentum (reticular activating system consciousness) and midbrain vertical gaze centres.

mcqs.subject: Anatomy
mcqs.question: A man has diplopia and cannot move his right eye laterally; other eye movements are normal. Which cranial nerve nucleus is affected? [KIMS 26. QIMS 25]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Isolated abduction failure = CN VI. A lesion of the abducens NUCLEUS gives a horizontal gaze palsy (it contains interneurons to the opposite MLF), often with facial palsy.

mcqs.subject: Anatomy
mcqs.question: A medullary tumour causes dysphagia, hoarseness, shoulder weakness and tongue wasting. Which cranial nerves arise from the medulla oblongata. [KIMS 25]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Midbrain:111. IV. Pons: V; pontomedullary junction: Vl, Vll, Vlll. Medulla: IX, X, Xl (cranial root), Xll. (Xl spinal root from Cl~C5.)

mcqs.subject: Anatomy
mcqs.question: A motorcyclist has dorsal midbrain injury at the level of the superior colliculus. Which nucleus is located at this level? [KIMS 25]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Superior colliculus level: oculomotor nucleus, Edinger-westphal, red nucleus, substantia nigra. crus. Inferior colliculus level.. trochlear nucleus, decussation of superior cerebellar peduncles.

mcqs.subject: Anatomy
mcqs.question: A neuroanatomy student traces motor fibres that loop around the abducens nucleus forming a bulge in the floor of the fourth ventricle. Which fibres wind around the abducens nucleus. [WMC 26. KIMS 25]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Internal genu of the facial nerve loops dorsally over the abducens nucleus 4 facial colliculus; lesion 4 ipsilateral facial palsy + lateral gaze palsy.

mcqs.subject: Anatomy
mcqs.question: A 12-year-old boy has vertical diplopia when reading or going downstairs. MRI shows a dorsal midbrain glioma at the level of the inferior colliculus. Which nucleus is involved? [KIMS 25]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Trochlear nucleus lies at the level of the inferior colliculus in the periaqueductal grey; its fibres cross in the superior medullary velum and emerge dorsally.

mcqs.subject: Anatomy
mcqs.question: A neuroanatomist traces the spinal nucleus and tract of the trigeminal nerve upward from the substantia gelatinosa of C2. Up to which level does it extend? [KIMS 26. KIMS 25]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Trigeminal nuclei: mesencephalic (midbrain, proprioception), chief sensory (pons, touch), spinal (pons to C2, pain/temperature - continuous with substantia gelatinosa). Key note: source keyed medulla; the spinal nucleus extends into the pons.

mcqs.subject: Anatomy
mcqs.question: A neurologist localizes a lesion causing hemiplegia relative to the pyramidal decussation. Which statement about the corticospinal tract is correct? [AMC 26]

options.B: It is ipsilateral in the pons, and most fibres decussate in the caudal medulla
options.D: It remains ipsilateral throughout the cord

mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: CST: corona radiata ￿ posterior limb of internal capsule ￿ middle 3/5 of crus ￿ basilar pons (scattered) 4 pyramids ￿ 85-90% cross at the pyramidal decussation (lateral CST); IOA uncrossed (anterior CST).

mcqs.subject: Anatomy
mcqs.question: On the ventral surface of the medulla, an oval swelling is seen lateral to the pyramid. Which nuclei form this swelling. [LHR 26]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Olive (inferior olivary nucleus) lies between the pyramid and the inferior cerebellar peduncle: Xll emerges between pyramid and olive, IK/X/XI behind the olive. Gracile/cuneate tubercles are dorsal.

mcqs.subject: Anatomy
mcqs.question: A neuroanatomy student locates the red nucleus on a cross-section of the midbrain. In which part of the midbrain is it located? [CKMC 26]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Midbrain: tectum (colliculi) dorsal to the aqueduct; tegmentum (red nucleus, CN III/IV nuclei, MLF, medial lemniscus) in the middle," basis (substantia nigra + crus) ventral.

mcqs.subject: Anatomy
mcqs.question: A patient with a midbrain lesion has a dilated pupil that does not react to light or near, with normal eye movements. Which nucleus provides parasympathetic fibres to the eye through CN111? [MUL 26]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: EW nucleus 4 CNI11￿ ciliary ganglion ￿ short ciliary nerves ￿ sphincter pupillae and ciliary muscle (pupillary constriction, accommodation).

mcqs.subject: Anatomy
mcqs.question: A neuroanatomy student examines the elevation in the floor of the fourth ventricle at the level of the lower pons. Which nucleus underlies the facial colliculus. [WMC 26]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Facial colliculus = abducens nucleus covered by the internal genu of the facial nerve. Hypoglossal trigone and vagal trigone lie in the medullary floor.

mcqs.subject: Anatomy
mcqs.question: A woman has hoarseness from vocal cord paralysis after a brainstem infarct. Which CNS structure is involved? [BWP 26]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Nucleus ambiguus ￿ vagus (recurrent laryngeal nerve) 4 all intrinsic laryngeal muscles except cricothyroid (superior laryngeal nerve).

mcqs.subject: Anatomy
mcqs.question: On the ventral surface of the midbrain, two large bundles of descending f ibres diverge from the cerebral hemispheres. What are they. [KIMS 26]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Crus cerebri carries corticospinal and corticobulbar fibres (middle 3/5), frontopontine (medial 1/5) and parieto-temporo-occipitopontine (lateral 1/5) fibres," the interpeduncular fossa lies between.

mcqs.subject: Anatomy
mcqs.question: A hypertensive man suddenly becomes comatose with quadriplegia, facial weakness and pinpoint pupils. What is the likely site of haemorrhage. [KIMS 26]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Pontine haemorrhage: pinpoint (but reactive) pupils from loss of descending sympathetic fibres, quadriplegia, coma, hyperthermia; poor prognosis.

mcqs.subject: Anatomy
mcqs.question: A child with a midline cerebellar tumour has a wide-based gait, truncal sway and nystagmus. The flocculonodular lobe belongs to which functional division? [Prof 25 . AMC 26. WMC 26 . HITEC 25]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Vestibulocerebellum (archicerebellum) = flocculonodular lobe ￿ equilibrium, eye movements," lesion (medulloblastoma) 4 truncal ataxia, nystagmus. Spinocerebellum = vermis + paravermis. Cerebrocerebellum = lateral hemispheres.

mcqs.subject: Anatomy
mcqs.question: A pianist with a lateral cerebellar hemisphere lesion has difficulty planning and timing rapid skilled finger movements. What is the main function of the cerebrocerebellum. [Prof 25]

options.C: Planning and coordination of skilled voluntary movements

mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Cerebrocerebellum (neocerebellum," lateral hemispheres 4 dentate 4 thalamus VL 4 cortex) plans and times sequential skilled movements." lesions dysmetria, intention tremor, dysdiadochokinesia.

mcqs.subject: Anatomy
mcqs.question: A man with a superior cerebellar peduncle lesion has ipsilateral intention tremor. Which tract passes through the superior cerebellar peduncle. [AMC 25]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Superior peduncle = main OUTPUT (dentatothalamic, dentatorubral) + ventral spinocerebellar input. Middle = pontocerebellar. Inferior = dorsal spinocerebellar, cuneocerebellar, olivocerebellar; fastigial efferents leave via the juxtarestiform body.

mcqs.subject: Anatomy
mcqs.question: A neuroanatomy student traces proprioceptive f ibres from Clarke nucleus into the cerebellum. Through which peduncle does the dorsal spinocerebellar tract enter. [CKMC 25]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Inferior peduncle: dorsal spinocerebellar, cuneocerebellar, olivocerebellar (climbing fibres), vestibulocerebellar. Ventral spinocerebellar enters via the superior peduncle (crosses twice).

mcqs.subject: Anatomy
mcqs.question: A 50-year-old man with a right cerebellar hemisphere metastasis has clumsiness of the right arm and leg. What does a cerebellar hemisphere [HITEC 26. CKMC 25] lesion produce.
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Cerebellar signs are IPSILATERAL (double crossing: dentatothalamic fibres cross, then corticospinal fibres cross back). Vermis lesion ￿ truncal ataxia; hemisphere 4 limb ataxia, intention tremor.

mcqs.subject: Anatomy
mcqs.question: On a sagittal MRI, the student identif ies the largest part of the cerebellum. Which is the largest part of the cerebellum? [HITEC 25]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Posterior lobe (neocerebellum, cerebrocerebellum) forms most of the hemispheres and is phylogenetically newest," connected with cerebral cortex via pontine nuclei.

mcqs.subject: Anatomy
mcqs.question: A neuroscientist traces afferents ending as rosettes on granule cells in the cerebellar cortex. From where do mossy fibres arise? [HITEC 25]

options.B: Pontine nuclei, spinal cord and vestibular nuclei (all except olive)

mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: All cerebellar afferents are mossy fibres (4 granule cells ￿ parallel fibres) EXCEPT olivocerebellar fibres, which are climbing fibres ending directly on Purkinje dendrites.

mcqs.subject: Anatomy
mcqs.question: An infant has an enlarged posterior fossa, a cystic fourth ventricle, hydrocephalus and absent cerebellar vermis. Which part of the cerebellum is hypoplastic in Dandy-walker malformation. [BWP 25]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Dandy-walker: vermian agenesis/hypoplasia + cystic dilatation of the fourth ventricle (atresia of Magendie/Luschka) + enlarged posterior fossa. Source stem mentioned facial anomalies (syndromic association).

mcqs.subject: Anatomy
mcqs.question: A neuroanatomist stains GABAergic interneurons whose axons form baskets" around Purkinje cell bodies. In which layer do basket cell axons terminate. [BWP 25]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Basket and stellate cell bodies lie in the molecular layer. but basket cell axons descend to synapse on Purkinje cell bodies (Purkinje layer). Key note: source keyed molecular layer (location of basket cell bodies).

mcqs.subject: Anatomy
mcqs.question: A neuroanatomy slide shows T-shaped axons of granule cells running along the folia. In which layer are parallel f ibres located? [BWP 25]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Granule cell axons ascend to the molecular layer, bifurcate into parallel fibres and excite Purkinje dendrites (each Purkinje cell receives ~200 000).

mcqs.subject: Anatomy
mcqs.question: A 55-year-old man cannot sit or stand without swaying; limb coordination is normal. Which part of the cerebellum is involved? [KIMS 26 . QIMS 25]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Vermis (spinocerebellum. fastigial nucleus 4 vestibulospinal/reticulospinal) controls axial muscles," lesion ￿ truncal ataxia, titubation.

mcqs.subject: Anatomy
mcqs.question: A 60-year-old alcoholic has a broad-based gait and frequent falls; arms are relatively normal. MRI shows cerebellar atrophy. Which part of the cerebellum is most affected? [QIMS 25]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Alcoholic cerebellar degeneration selectively affects the anterior lobe and superior vermis 4 gait (leg) ataxia with relative sparing of arms, speech and eyes.

mcqs.subject: Anatomy
mcqs.question: A 54-year-old man with gait instability has selective loss of large flask-shaped neurons in the middle layer of the cerebellar cortex. Which cells are involved? [KIMS 25]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Purkinje cells (middle layer, single row) are the only output of the cerebellar cortex GABAergic inhibition of deep nuclei. Lost in alcoholic and paraneoplastic (anti-yo) degeneration.

mcqs.subject: Anatomy
mcqs.question: A 55-year-old man has slurred speech, a wide-based gait, falls to the right and an intention tremor. Which structure is affected? [KIMS 26 . KIMS 25]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Ipsilateral cerebellar lesion: ataxia. falling towards the side of the lesion, intention tremor, scanning dysarthria, nystagmus, hypotonia.

mcqs.subject: Anatomy
mcqs.question: A child with a midline cerebellar tumour has truncal instability. Which deep cerebellar nucleus is most involved in postural adjustments and axial movements? [AMC 26]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Deep nuclei (lateral -> medial, "Don't Eat Greasy Food").. dentate (cerebrocerebellum, planning), emboliform + globose (interposed, limb), fastigial (vermis, axial/vestibular).

mcqs.subject: Anatomy
mcqs.question: A neuroanatomy student traces the ventral spinocerebellar tract into the cerebellum. How many times do its fibres decussate? [CKMC 26]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: VSCT crosses in the anterior white commissure, ascends, enters via the SUPERIOR peduncle and crosses back in the cerebellum - so cerebellar input remains ipsilateral. DSCT never crosses.

mcqs.subject: Anatomy
mcqs.question: A histology slide of cerebellar cortex shows three layers. Which is the innermost layer. [CKMC 26]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Cerebellar cortex from outside in: molecular (stellate, basket, parallel fibres, Purkinje dendrites) 4 Purkinje layer 4 granular (granule cells, Golgi cells, mossy fibre rosettes/glomeruli).

mcqs.subject: Anatomy
mcqs.question: A man presents with a wide-based, staggering gait and ataxia. Which structure is most likely affected? [CKMC 26]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Wide-based "drunken" gait = cerebellar (vermis/anterior lobe) ataxia; parkinsonian gait is narrow-based and shuffling; sensory ataxia is stamping with positive Romberg.

mcqs.subject: Anatomy
mcqs.question: A neurosurgeon explains that a lesion of the largest deep cerebellar nucleus impaired planning of limb movements. Which deep nucleus coordinates voluntary limb movements through connections with the cerebral cortex. [HITEC 26]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Dentate nucleus receives the lateral hemisphere and projects via the superior peduncle to the contralateral red nucleus and VL thalamus motor/premotor cortex.

mcqs.subject: Anatomy
mcqs.question: A patient with a flocculonodular lobe lesion has imbalance and frequent falls. Which structure provides the main input to this lobe. [HITEC 26]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Flocculonodular lobe receives primary vestibular fibres (directly from the vestibular nerve - the only primary afferents reaching the cerebellum) and secondary fibres from vestibular nuclei.

mcqs.subject: Anatomy
mcqs.question: A neuroscientist describes a cerebellar region that works with premotor cortex and basal ganglia in cognitive planning of movement. Which region is this. [HITEC 26]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Cerebrocerebellum (lateral hemispheres) receives cortical input via pontine nuclei and returns to cortex via dentate-VL; it plans timing and sequence of movements and contributes to cognition.

mcqs.subject: Anatomy
mcqs.question: A neuroanatomist traces mossy fibre rosettes within cerebellar glomeruli. With which cerebellar cells do mossy fibres synapse. [KIMS 26]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Glomerulus = mossy fibre rosette + granule cell dendrites + Golgi cell axon. Climbing fibres synapse directly on Purkinje dendrites.

mcqs.subject: Anatomy
mcqs.question: After a stroke, a man speaks fluently but his speech makes no sense, and he cannot understand spoken commands. Which lobe contains the damaged area? [Prof 24. AMC 26. HITEC 26. QIMS 25]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Wernicke area (area 22) = posterior part of superior temporal gyrus of the dominant hemisphere 4 fluent, meaningless speech with poor comprehension. Broca area (44, 45) = inferior frontal gyrus ￿ non~fluent, effortful speech.

mcqs.subject: Anatomy
mcqs.question: A 45-year-old woman has headaches, galactorrhoea and loss of the outer halves of both visual fields. MRI shows a pituitary macroadenoma. At which site is the lesion. [Prof 24. Prof 25. KIMS 26. KIMS 25]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Bitemporal hemianopia = compression of crossing nasal fibres in the optic chiasma (pituitary adenoma, craniopharyngioma). Optic tract lesion contralateral homonymous hemianopia.

mcqs.subject: Anatomy
mcqs.question: During a craniotomy for epilepsy, the surgeon maps the central sulcus with cortical stimulation. Which lobes does the central sulcus separate. [Prof 25]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Central sulcus separates frontal (precentral gyrus, area 4) from parietal (postcentral gyrus, 3, 1,2). Lateral sulcus separates frontal/parietal from temporal," parieto-occipital sulcus is on the medial surface.

mcqs.subject: Anatomy
mcqs.question: On an axial MRI, a thin white-matter lamina is seen between the insular cortex and the claustrum. What is it? [Prof 25]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Lateral ￿ medial: insula - extreme capsule - claustrum - external capsule - putamen - globus pallidus - internal capsule - thalamus/caudate.

mcqs.subject: Anatomy
mcqs.question: A histologist compares Brodmann areas and notes one with a very thin layer IV and large pyramidal cells. Which area has agranular cortex? [Prof 25]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Agranular (motor) cortex: areas 4 and 6 (primary motor and premotor) - few granular cells, prominent pyramidal (Betz cells in 4). Granular (koniocortex): areas 17, 41, 3, 1,2.

mcqs.subject: Anatomy
mcqs.question: An MRI shows a thin lamina of white matter between the claustrum and the putamen. What is it? [Prof 25]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: External capsule lies between putamen and claustrum; extreme capsule between claustrum and insula; internal capsule between lentiform nucleus (lateral) and caudate/thalamus (medial).

mcqs.subject: Anatomy
mcqs.question: A right-handed man has a stroke affecting the right cerebral hemisphere including the internal capsule. Which motor deficit will he have. [Prof 25]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Each hemisphere controls the opposite half of the body (pyramidal decussation). Right non-dominant parietal lesions also cause left hemineglect.

mcqs.subject: Anatomy
mcqs.question: A patient with a tumour in the superior parietal lobule cannot recognize objects placed in his hand and has poor spatial awareness. In which function is this area involved? [Prof 25 . MUL 25 . WMC 25]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Superior parietal lobule (areas 5, 7) = somatosensory association 4 stereognosis and body image. Lesion ￿ astereognosis, tactile agnosia, contralateral neglect.

mcqs.subject: Anatomy
mcqs.question: An MRI of a patient with a lacunar stroke shows the internal capsule. Which structures form the medial boundary of the internal capsule. [AMC 25]

options.A: Head of caudate nucleus and thalamus

mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Internal capsule: medial = caudate head (anterior limb) and thalamus (posterior limb),. lateral = lentiform nucleus (putamen + globus pallidus). Key note: source keyed globus pallidus. which lies L4TERAL to the capsule.

mcqs.subject: Anatomy
mcqs.question: A patient speaks fluently and understands well, but cannot repeat a sentence spoken to him. Which fibres connecting Broca and Wernicke areas are damaged? [LHR 25]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Arcuate fasciculus (part of superior longitudinal fasciculus) links Wernicke to Broca,. lesion ￿ conduction aphasia (poor repetition with fluent speech and good comprehension).

mcqs.subject: Anatomy
mcqs.question: A 60-year-old woman with a left posterior temporal infarct speaks fluently in jargon. What is the main deficit with a lesion of Wernicke area. [BWP 26. CKMC 25]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Wernicke (receptive) aphasia: fluent, paraphasic speech, P¢X)r comprehension and repetition, patient unaware. Broca: non-fluent, telegraphic speech, comprehension preserved, patient frustrated.

mcqs.subject: Anatomy
mcqs.question: A man understands commands but speaks slowly, with great effort and few words. Which type of aphasia results from a lesion of Broca area. [MUL 26. KIMS 26. CKMC 25. QIMS 25. KIMS 25]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Broca area (areas 44, 45. inferior frontal gyrus of the dominant hemisphere) programmes speech.. lesion 4 expressive aphasia, often with right face/arm weakness (MCA superior division).

mcqs.subject: Anatomy
mcqs.question: A woman can feel the texture of a key in her hand with eyes closed but cannot name the object. A lesion of which area causes this tactile agnosia. [HITEC 26. BWP 26. CKMC 25. KIMS 25]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Primary somatosensory cortex (3, 1,2) detects; association cortex (5,7) interprets. Lesion ￿ astereognosis with intact primary sensation.

mcqs.subject: Anatomy
mcqs.question: A man speaks fluently but cannot understand what is said to him after a stroke. Damage to which gyrus is most likely. [MUL 25]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Posterior superior temporal gyrus (area 22, Wernicke) is the language-comprehension area: inferior frontal gyrus (44, 45) is Broca area. Source stem was garbled ("speech intact")," comprehension loss with intact fluency fits the key.

mcqs.subject: Anatomy
mcqs.question: A patient with a tumour of the posterior corpus callosum cannot read words presented to his left visual field (alexia without agraphia). Which part of the corpus callosum connects the occipital lobes. [MUL 25]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Splenium (forceps major) connects occipital lobes." genu (forceps minor) connects frontal lobes; body connects frontal/parietal; rostrum joins the lamina terminalis.

mcqs.subject: Anatomy
mcqs.question: A man with a left frontal infarct has non-fluent, effortful speech but good comprehension. Where is the expressive speech area. [AMC 26. HITEC 26 . MUL 25]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Broca area = pars opercularis (44) + pars triangularis (45) of the dominant inferior frontal gyrus,. supplied by the superior division of MCA.

mcqs.subject: Anatomy
mcqs.question: A tumour adjacent to the left optic tract causes a right homonymous hemianopia and right-sided hemiparesis. Which neighbouring structure is damaged to cause the weakness. [WMC 25]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: The optic tract winds around the lateral side of the crus cerebri, which carries corticospinal fibres above their decussation 4 contralateral (right) hemiparesis.

mcqs.subject: Anatomy
mcqs.question: After a stroke, a woman ignores the left side of her body and eats food from only the right side of her plate; power is normal. A lesion of which area causes hemineglect? [BWP 25]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Right (non-dominant) inferior parietal lobule attends to both halves of space: lesion 4 contralateral (left) neglect, anosognosia, dressing apraxia.

mcqs.subject: Anatomy
mcqs.question: A 65-year-old man has loss of touch and vibration on the left side of his body after a cortical infarct. Where is the lesion. [QIMS 25]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Postcentral gyrus (areas 3, 1,2) = primary somatosensory cortex receiving VPUVPM fibres," contralateral. somatotopic (leg medial, face lateral).

mcqs.subject: Anatomy
mcqs.question: A man cannot recognise his wife's face, though he knows her by her voice; vision and intelligence are normal. In which lobe is the lesion. [QIMS 25]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Prosopagnosia." bilateral (or right) lesions of the fusiform face area on the inferomedial occipitotemporal surface, often PCA territory.

mcqs.subject: Anatomy
mcqs.question: A neuroanatomy student classifies white-matter fibres passing from cortex to brainstem through the internal capsule. Which category are they. [KIMS 25]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Projection fibres connect cortex with subcortical centres (corona radiata, internal capsule); association fibres join areas of the same hemisphere; commissural fibres cross (corpus callosum).

mcqs.subject: Anatomy
mcqs.question: A 42-year-old woman lacks motivation, initiative, emotional responsiveness and goal-directed behaviour. Which lobe is involved? [AMC 26. KIMS 26 . KIMS 25]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Prefrontal cortex: planning, judgment, personality, motivation. Dorsolateral lesion 4 apathy, poor executive function; orbitofrontal ￿ disinhibition (Phineas Gage).

mcqs.subject: Anatomy
mcqs.question: A 35-year-old with a lesion in the fibres connecting the two cerebral hemispheres has difficulty coordinating bimanual tasks. Which structure is affected? [KIMS 26. KIMS 25]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Corpus callosum (largest commissure) coordinates the hemispheres; callosotomy 4 disconnection syndrome (left-hand apraxia, inability to name objects in the left hand).

mcqs.subject: Anatomy
mcqs.question: A woman with a parasagittal meningioma has spastic weakness of the contralateral leg and urinary incontinence. Where is the cortical motor area for the leg? [AMC 26 . HITEC 26]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Paracentral lobule (medial surface, ACA territory) contains leg/foot motor and sensory areas and the cortical centre for micturition. Parasagittal meningioma can cause bilateral leg weakness.

mcqs.subject: Anatomy
mcqs.question: A student is asked which cortical area interprets spoken and written language. Which area is primarily responsible for language comprehension. [CKMC 26. WMC 26]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Wernicke area (22) - comprehension," Broca (44, 45) - expression: arcuate fasciculus - repetition; angular gyrus (39) - reading/writing.

mcqs.subject: Anatomy
mcqs.question: A patient with a right frontal infarct has both eyes deviated to the right and cannot look voluntarily to the left. Brodmann area 8 (frontal eye field) controls which function. [CKMC 26]

options.D: Voluntary horizontal conjugate eye movements (saccades) to the opposite side

mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: FEF drives contralateral saccades via the PPRF,. destructive lesion 4 eyes deviate TOWARDS the lesion," irritative (seizure) 4 away from it.

mcqs.subject: Anatomy
mcqs.question: A student explains why a pituitary tumour causes loss of the temporal fields. Where do fibres from the nasal halves of the retina cross. [WMC 26]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Nasal retinal fibres (temporal visual fields) decussate in the chiasma; temporal retinal fibres remain uncrossed. Each optic tract therefore carries the contralateral visual field.

mcqs.subject: Anatomy
mcqs.question: A patient is unable to read, write or understand spoken language, though he can speak f luently. Which cortical area is most likely defective. [BWP 26]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Wernicke area (with angular gyrus) is Guyton's "general interpretative area" for both auditory and visual language; isolated angular gyrus lesions spare auditory comprehension. Source gave no definite key.

mcqs.subject: Anatomy
mcqs.question: A woman has amenorrhoea, galactorrhoea, raised prolactin and bitemporal hemianopia. Where is the lesion. [BWP 26]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Prolactinoma is the commonest functioning pituitary adenoma; macroadenomas grow upward to compress the chiasma from below ￿ superior bitemporal quadrantanopia first.

mcqs.subject: Anatomy
mcqs.question: A student classif ies the fibres of the corpus callosum. Of which fibre type is the corpus callosum mainly composed? [BWP 26]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Commissures: corpus callosum, anterior, posterior, habenular, hippocampal commissures. Association." arcuate fasciculus, cingulum, uncinate. longitudinal fasciculi. Projection." internal capsule, fornix.

mcqs.subject: Anatomy
mcqs.question: A patient with a right parietal lesion ignores the left side of space and objects. Amorphosynthesis is associated with a lesion of which area. [BWP 26]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Amorphosynthesis (Guyton): loss of ability to synthesize the form of objects/body on the opposite side - posterior parietal association cortex, especially non-dominant (neglect).

mcqs.subject: Anatomy
mcqs.question: A histologist notes that areas 3, 17 and 41 have a thick internal granular layer (koniocortex). What function is performed by granular cortex. [KIMS 26]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Granular (koniocortex) = primary sensory areas receiving thalamic input in layer IV," agranular = motor areas with large layer V pyramidal cells.

mcqs.subject: Anatomy
mcqs.question: A hypertensive man has a pure motor hemiplegia of the face, arm and leg on the left side with no sensory or cortical signs. Which part of the internal capsule is most likely involved? [HITEC 26]

options.A: Posterior limb of the right internal capsule
options.B: Anterior limb of the left internal capsule
options.C: Retrolentiform part of the right internal capsule
options.D: Genu of the left internal capsule

mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Stem created: the source recall was incomplete (HITEC 26 Anatomy Q20, between corticospinal and Parkinson questions). Posterior limb: corticospinal (arm, leg) + thalamocortical sensory fibres," genu: corticobulbar; retro/sublentiform." optic and auditory radiations.

mcqs.subject: Anatomy
mcqs.question: A patient with a colloid cyst compressing the fornix develops anterograde amnesia. Fibres from the hippocampus to the mammillary body pass through which structure? [AMC 25]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Papez circuit: hippocampus 4 fornix 4 mammillary body ￿ mammillothalamic tract ￿ anterior thalamic nucleus 4 cingulate gyrus ￿ hippocampus. Key note: source stem said amygdala; amygdala 4 hypothalamus runs in the stria terminalis.

mcqs.subject: Anatomy
mcqs.question: A man who recovered from herpes simplex encephalitis puts objects in his mouth, shows no fear, overeats and is hypersexual. Which syndrome is this. [CKMC 25]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Bilateral amygdala/anterior temporal destruction 4 Kluver-Bucy." placidity, hyperorality, hypersexuality, visual agnosia. hypermetamorphosis. HSV encephalitis targets temporal lobes.

mcqs.subject: Anatomy
mcqs.question: A man with a temporal lobe tumour shows episodes of rage, fear and aggression. Which nucleus is chief ly involved in these emotional (defence) behaviours. [MUL 26. MUL 25]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Amygdala (limbic system) attaches emotional significance, especially fear and aggression; stimulation 4 rage/fear, bilateral lesion ￿ placidity (Kluver-Bucy).

mcqs.subject: Anatomy
mcqs.question: A student traces the major efferent bundle of the hippocampus. Which structure connects the hippocampus to the hypothalamus (mammillary body)? [BWP 26]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Hippocampus ￿ alveus 4 fimbria 4 crus 4 body ￿ columns of fornix ￿ mammillary bodies. Stria terminalis connects amygdala to hypothalamus.

mcqs.subject: Anatomy
mcqs.question: A man after bilateral temporal lobectomy places inedible objects in his mouth and has lost fear. Which is a characteristic feature of Kluver-Bucy syndrome. [BWP 26]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Kluver-Bucy: hyperorality, hypersexuality. placidity, visual agnosia (psychic blindness). hypermetamorphosis, dietary change - bilateral amygdala/anterior temporal lesions.

mcqs.subject: Anatomy
mcqs.question: A 40-year-old man has jerky, purposeless, dance-like movements, personality change and a family history of early dementia. Which of the following is a hyperkinetic movement disorder? [Prof 25]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Hyperkinetic disorders: Huntington chorea, hemiballismus, athetosis, tics. Hypokinetic: Parkinson disease (bradykinesia, rigidity). Huntington = CAG repeat on chromosome 4, loss of striatal (caudate) GABA neurons.

mcqs.subject: Anatomy
mcqs.question: A 65-year-old man has a resting pill-rolling tremor, cogwheel rigidity and a shuffling gait. Pathology shows loss of pigmented midbrain neurons. Damage to which structure causes this. [Prof 25. HITEC 26. KIMS 26. LHR 25. CKMC 25. BWP 25. QIMS 25. KIMS 25]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Parkinson disease = degeneration of dopaminergic neurons of substantia nigra pars compacta (neuromelanin) ￿ loss of nigrostriatal dopamine. TRAP: Tremor, Rigidity, Akinesia, Postural instability.

mcqs.subject: Anatomy
mcqs.question: A 42-year-old man has chorea, irritability and memory loss; his father had the same illness. MRI shows "box-car" lateral ventricles. Which part of the basal ganglia is primarily affected among the following. [AMC 26. AMC 25]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Huntington disease destroys GABAergic/enkephalin neurons of the striatum - caudate head first (ventricular widening) then putamen. Key note.. source keyed lentiform,. the striatum (caudate + putamen) is the site.

mcqs.subject: Anatomy
mcqs.question: A neuroanatomy lecturer describes the phylogenetically newer part of the basal ganglia that receives cortical input. Which structures form the neostriatum (striatum)? [LHR 25]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Striatum (neostriatum) = caudate + putamen (input nuclei). Paleostriatum = globus pallidus (output). Lentiform nucleus = putamen + globus pallidus. Corpus striatum = caudate + lentiform.

mcqs.subject: Anatomy
mcqs.question: A hypertensive woman develops sudden violent flinging movements of her right arm and leg. A lesion of which structure causes this? [AMC 26. BWP 26. CKMC 25 . QIMS 25]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Hemiballismus = lacunar infarct of the CONTRALATERAL subthalamic nucleus 4 loss of excitation of GPI 4 disinhibited thalamus. Source asked "left STN lesion causes?•l (answer: right hemiballismus).

mcqs.subject: Anatomy
mcqs.question: A neurosurgeon targets the main output nucleus of the basal ganglia in deep brain stimulation for Parkinson disease. Through which structure does basal ganglia output leave. [AMC 26. CKMC 26. CKMC 25]

options.A: Globus pallidus (internal segment) and substantia nigra reticulata

mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Input: striatum. Output: GPI + SNr (GABAergic inhibition of VAIVL thalamus via ansa and lenticular fasciculus). STN is an intrinsic (indirect pathway) nucleus.

mcqs.subject: Anatomy
mcqs.question: A neurosurgeon places a stimulator in the only glutamatergic (excitatory) nucleus of the basal ganglia circuit. Which nucleus is excitatory. [WMC 25]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: STN uses glutamate to excite GPi/SNr (indirect pathway). All other intrinsic basal ganglia projections are GABAergic; nigrostriatal fibres are dopaminergic. STN is a DBS target in Parkinson disease.

mcqs.subject: Anatomy
mcqs.question: A patient with long-standing Parkinson disease has a hand posture with the wrist pronated and f lexed, MCP joints flexed and IP joints extended. A lesion of which structure produces this posture? [WMC 25]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: This "striatal hand" (dystonic posture) occurs in basal ganglia disease. A similar carpal spasm (main d'accoucheur) occurs in hypocalcaemic tetany.

mcqs.subject: Anatomy
mcqs.question: A patient has involuntary, large-amplitude movements of the proximal limb muscles at rest. A lesion of which system causes this. [WMC 25]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Involuntary movements (ballism, chorea, athetosis, tremor at rest) = basal ganglia disease; cerebellar lesions cause incoordination of voluntary movement, not involuntary movements at rest.

mcqs.subject: Anatomy
mcqs.question: A 45-year-old man has involuntary, jerky, non-repetitive movements of limbs and head, dysarthria and dysphagia; his paternal uncle died of the same illness. Which part of the basal ganglia is affected? [KIMS 26. KIMS 25]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Familial chorea = Huntington disease (AD) 4 degeneration of the striatum, especially caudate head. Key note: source keyed subthalamic nucleus (causes hemiballismus, not familial chorea).

mcqs.subject: Anatomy
mcqs.question: A patient with Parkinson disease has dopamine deficiency. Which dopaminergic pathway is affected? [MUL 26]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Nigrostriatal (SNC 4 striatum): movement - loss in PD, blocked by antipsychotics (EPS). Mesolimbic/mesocortical (VTA): reward, psychosis. Tuberoinfundibular: inhibits prolactin.

mcqs.subject: Anatomy
mcqs.question: A man has dysphagia, hoarseness and a deviated uvula after a lateral medullary infarct involving the nucleus ambiguus. Which cranial nerves receive motor fibres from this nucleus? [Prof 24]

options.B: Glossopharyngeal, vagus and cranial part of accessory

mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Nucleus ambiguus (special visceral efferent) ￿ IX (stylopharyngeus), X and cranial Xl (muscles of palate, pharynx. larynx). Lesion: dysphagia, hoarseness, uvula deviates to the opposite (healthy) side.

mcqs.subject: Anatomy
mcqs.question: A 50-year-old man with a fourth nerve palsy has difficulty walking downstairs and reading. Which is a main action of the superior oblique muscle. [Prof 25]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Superior oblique: intorsion. depression (best in adduction). abduction. Patients tilt the head AWAY from the affected side to compensate for extorsion. S04, LR6, rest 3"

mcqs.subject: Anatomy
mcqs.question: A man with vertical diplopia tilts his head to the side opposite the weak eye; the affected eye cannot look down and in. Which nerve supplies the paralysed muscle. [Prof 25]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Trochlear nerve: only nerve emerging from the dorsal brainstem, decussates completely (nucleus supplies contralateral SO), longest intracranial course. Palsy 4 vertical diplopia worse on looking down.

mcqs.subject: Anatomy
mcqs.question: After a fracture of the floor of the orbit, a man has numbness of the upper lip, cheek and side of the nose. Which nerve division supplies this area. [Prof 25]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Infraorbital nerve (terminal branch of V2) supplies lower eyelid, cheek, side of nose and upper lip; it is injured in orbital floor (blow-out) fractures.

mcqs.subject: Anatomy
mcqs.question: A diabetic woman has ptosis and her right eye rests "down and out" with the pupil spared. Which nerve is affected? [HITEC 26. KIMS 26. LHR 25. BWP 25]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: CN111 palsy: ptosis (levator), down-and-out eye (unopposed LR and SO), dilated pupil (compressive). Diabetic (ischaemic) palsy spares the pupil because the peripheral parasympathetic fibres survive.

mcqs.subject: Anatomy
mcqs.question: A 30-year-old woman wakes up unable to close her right eye, wrinkle her forehead or smile on the right side. What does paralysis of both upper and lower face on one side indicate? [LHR 25 . HITEC 25]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: UMN (cortical/capsular) lesions spare the forehead because the upper face receives bilateral corticobulbar input. LMN (nucleus or nerve) lesion paralyses the whole half of the face.

mcqs.subject: Anatomy
mcqs.question: A 70-year-old diabetic has dysarthria; his tongue is wasted and fasciculating on one side and deviates to that side on protrusion. Which nerve is damaged? [HITEC 26. LHR 25. HITEC 25]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: LMN Xll lesion." ipsilateral wasting + fasciculation, tongue deviates TOWARDS the lesion (unopposed opposite genioglossus). UMN lesion: deviation to the side opposite the cortical lesion, no wasting.

mcqs.subject: Anatomy
