mcqs.question: A woman develops a weak voice, nasal regurgitation and an absent gag reflex on one side after a jugular foramen tumour. Damage to which nerve causes loss of the gag reflex motor limb and hoarseness. [CKMC 25]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Gag reflex." afferent IX, efferent X. Vagus supplies palate, pharynx, larynx (via recurrenL/superior laryngeal nerves) ￿ hoarseness, dysphagia, uvula to the opposite side.

mcqs.subject: Anatomy
mcqs.question: A man with raised intracranial pressure develops horizontal diplopia worse on looking to the left; his left eye cannot move outward. What is the action of the muscle supplied by CN VI? [MUL 25]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: CN Vl 4 lateral rectus (abduction). It has a long intracranial course over the petrous apex, so it is often stretched by raised ICP (false localizing sign).

mcqs.subject: Anatomy
mcqs.question: A man's tongue deviates to the right on protrusion and the right half is wasted. Which nerve is damaged? [CKMC 26. MUL 25]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: The intact left genioglossus pushes the tongue toward the paralysed right side. Wasting/fasciculation = LMN lesion of the right nerve or nucleus.

mcqs.subject: Anatomy
mcqs.question: A patient cannot clench his teeth firmly on one side; the masseter and temporalis do not bulge. Which nerve supplies these muscles. [WMC 25]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: All muscles of mastication (masseter, temporalis, pterygoids) + mylohyoid, anterior digastric, tensor tympani, tensor veli palatini are supplied by V3 (first pharyngeal arch).

mcqs.subject: Anatomy
mcqs.question: A woman has double vision only when looking up and to the right; the right eye fails to elevate in abduction. Which muscle is weak? [BWP 25]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Superior rectus is the pure elevator in abduction: inferior oblique elevates in adduction. Clinical testing: "H" pattern of gaze.

mcqs.subject: Anatomy
mcqs.question: A child does not gag when the posterior pharyngeal wall is touched on one side. Which nerves form the gag reflex arc. [BWP 25]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Gag reflex." afferent IX (pharyngeal sensation), centre in medulla (nucleus solitarius -> nucleus ambiguus), efferent X (pharyngeal constrictors).

mcqs.subject: Anatomy
mcqs.question: A 45-year-old man with an acoustic neuroma cannot close his right eye; the angle of the mouth droops and hearing is reduced on the same side. Where is the nerve affected? IQIMS 25]

options.B: Facial nerve in the internal acoustic meatus

mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: CN Vll and Vlll run together through the IAM," vestibular schwannoma causes hearing loss, tinnitus, vertigo, then facial weakness and loss of corneal reflex (V).

mcqs.subject: Anatomy
mcqs.question: A patient has hoarseness and his uvula deviates to the right on saying ah Which cranial nerve and nucleus are affected? IQIMS 25 . KIMS 25]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Uvula deviates AWAY from the paralysed side (pulled by intact levator palati): deviation to the right = left vagus/nucleus ambiguus lesion.

mcqs.subject: Anatomy
mcqs.question: A patient loses taste over the posterior one-third of the tongue and has an absent gag reflex on one side after a jugular foramen lesion. Which cranial nerve (with its motor nucleus) is affected? [QIMS 25]

options.B: Glossopharyngeal nerve - inferior salivatory nucleus only

mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: CN IX: taste and general sensation of posterior 1/3 tongue (4 nucleus solitarius/spinal V), gag afferent, motor to stylopharyngeus (nucleus ambiguus), parotid secretion (inferior salivatory nucleus).

mcqs.subject: Anatomy
mcqs.question: A child with vertical diplopia habitually tilts his head to the right. Which nerve and muscle are most likely affected? [AMC 26]

options.A: Left trochlear nerve, left superior oblique
options.B: Right oculomotor nerve, right inferior rectus
options.C: Right trochlear nerve, right superior oblique
options.D: Left abducens nerve, left lateral rectus

mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: In SO palsy the affected eye is extorted; tilting the head to the OPPOSITE shoulder reduces diplopia. Bielschowsky test: diplopia worsens on tilting towards the affected side.

mcqs.subject: Anatomy
mcqs.question: A patient with a lesion of the lateral lemniscus has impaired hearing. Which cranial nerve carries the auditory information that ascends in the lateral lemniscus? [AMC 26]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Spiral ganglion (bipolar) ￿ cochlear nerve 4 cochlear nuclei ￿ superior olive 4 lateral lemniscus ￿ inferior colliculus ￿ MGB.

mcqs.subject: Anatomy
mcqs.question: A woman has ptosis and double vision; her eye is turned down and out. Which cranial nerve is affected? [CKMC 26]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: CN111 supplies levator palpebrae superioris (ptosis when paralysed), SR, IR, MR, 10. sphincter pupillae and ciliary muscle. Partial ptosis from Muller muscle = Horner syndrome.

mcqs.subject: Anatomy
mcqs.question: After a stroke, a woman has weakness of the lower half of the right side of her face but can wrinkle her forehead normally on both sides. Where is the lesion. [CKMC 26]

options.A: Left facial nerve at the stylomastoid foramen
options.B: Right facial nerve in the facial canal

mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Stem created: the source recall was incomplete ("facial problem"). The part of the facial nucleus supplying the forehead receives bilateral corticobulbar fibres, so a UMN lesion spares the forehead and affects the CONTRALATERAL lower face; LMN (Bell) palsy affects the whole ipsilateral face.

mcqs.subject: Anatomy
mcqs.question: A man cannot turn his chin to the left against resistance and his right shoulder droops after a posterior triangle lymph node biopsy. Which nerve is injured? [HITEC 26]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Stem created: the source recall was incomplete (head-rotation question was incomplete). The sternocleidomastoid turns the chin to the OPPOSITE side, so weak rotation to the left = right SCM (right CN XI); trapezius weakness causes shoulder droop.

mcqs.subject: Anatomy
mcqs.question: A 70-year-old man has a stroke and loses pain and temperature sensation over the entire left side of the body including the face. What is the most likely site of the lesion? [Prof 25]

options.D: Left half of the spinal cord

mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: VPL (body) and VPM (face) relay all contralateral somatic sensation; a thalamic lesion causes hemianaesthesia of the opposite side and may be followed by thalamic (Dejerine-Roussy) pain.

mcqs.subject: Anatomy
mcqs.question: A man with a small thalamic infarct has difficulty locating sounds. The auditory relay nucleus is involved. In which thalamic nucleus do auditory fibres relay. [LHR 25. MUL 25]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: "M for Music, L for Light": MGB (from inferior colliculus) 4 auditory radiation (sublentiform part of internal capsule) 4 areas 41, 42. LGB ￿ optic radiation ￿ area 17.

mcqs.subject: Anatomy
mcqs.question: A hypertensive man has a thalamic haemorrhage and loses proprioception, light touch and vibration on the opposite side of the body (face spared). Which thalamic nucleus is involved? [KIMS 26. LHR 25 . KIMS 25]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: VPL receives medial lemniscus and spinothalamic tracts (body)," VPM receives trigeminothalamic and taste (face). Both project to the postcentral gyrus via the posterior limb of the internal capsule.

mcqs.subject: Anatomy
mcqs.question: A patient with Wernicke-Korsakoff syndrome has severe recent memory loss with lesions in the Papez circuit. Which thalamic nucleus is concerned with recent memory. [MUL 25]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Anterior nucleus (receives mammillothalamic tract. projects to cingulate gyrus) is part of the Papez circuit; dorsomedial nucleus also serves memory and affect. Korsakoff: mammillary bodies and dorsomedial thalamus.

mcqs.subject: Anatomy
mcqs.question: A 48-year-old man who had a stroke months ago now has severe, burning, spontaneous pain on the left side of his body with normal power. Which thalamic nucleus is involved in thalamic pain syndrome. [QIMS 25]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Dejerine-Roussy syndrome." infarct of VP nuclei (thalamogeniculate branches of PCA) 4 contralateral hemianaesthesia followed by intractable central pain, allodynia.

mcqs.subject: Anatomy
mcqs.question: A neuroanatomy student matches thalamic relay nuclei with their inputs. Which nuclei relay somatic sensation from the body and the face, respectively. [AMC 26. MUL 26]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: VPL: medial lemniscus + spinothalamic (body). VPM: trigeminothalamic tracts (face) + taste (solitary nucleus). Both 4 postcentral gyrus.

mcqs.subject: Anatomy
mcqs.question: A thalamic lacune involves only the ventral posterolateral nucleus. Which deficit results? [CKMC 26]

options.A: Contralateral loss of body sensation with the face spared

mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: VPL = body (spinothalamic + medial lemniscus); VPM = face (trigeminothalamic). A lesion of VPL alone spares facial sensation.

mcqs.subject: Anatomy
mcqs.question: A patient develops dangerous hyperthermia from a tumour destroying the preoptic and anterior hypothalamus. This region is mainly concerned with which function. [Prof 25 . QIMS 25]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Anterior (preoptic) hypothalamus = heat-loss centre (sweating, vasodilation): lesion 4 hyperthermia. Posterior hypothalamus = heat-gain/conservation (shivering); lesion 4 poikilothermia/hypothermia. "A/C = Anterior Cooling"

mcqs.subject: Anatomy
mcqs.question: A night-shift worker has disturbed sleep-wake rhythm. Retinal input reaches a hypothalamic biological clock Which nucleus controls circadian rhythm: [MUL 25]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: SCN receives the retinohypothalamic tract (melanopsin ganglion cells) and drives the pineal (via sympathetic chain) to secrete melatonin at night.

mcqs.subject: Anatomy
mcqs.question: A man develops central diabetes insipidus after a head injury damaging the hypothalamus. Which nucleus mainly synthesizes ADH? [MUL 25]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: ADH: mainly supraoptic (5/6)," oxytocin: mainly paraventricular. Both are carried by the hypothalamohypophyseal tract (bound to neurophysins) to the posterior pituitary (Herring bodies).

mcqs.subject: Anatomy
mcqs.question: A cat stimulated electrically in a specif ic hypothalamic region shows fear, hissing and avoidance behaviour. Where is the "punishment" (aversion) centre located? [HITEC 25]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Guyton: punishment centres - central grey around the aqueduct extending into periventricular zones of hypothalamus and thalamus; reward centres - medial forebrain bundle, lateral and ventromedial hypothalamus, septum.

mcqs.subject: Anatomy
mcqs.question: A man with lateral medullary syndrome has ptosis, miosis and anhidrosis on the same side. Where do the descending sympathetic fibres involved in Horner syndrome originate. [AMC 26]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Oculosympathetic path.. hypothalamus 4 descends uncrossed in lateral brainstem 4 ciliospinal centre (C8-T2) 4 superior cervical ganglion 4 along ICA ￿ dilator pupillae and Muller muscle.

mcqs.subject: Anatomy
mcqs.question: A CT venogram shows thrombus in the sinus running along the junction of the falx cerebri and tentorium cerebelli. Where does the straight sinus drain? [Prof 25]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Straight sinus = inferior sagittal sinus + great cerebral vein (Galen) 4 confluence of sinuses (torcular Herophili) ￿ transverse ￿ sigmoid 4 IJV.

mcqs.subject: Anatomy
mcqs.question: An elderly alcoholic man with fluctuating confusion after a minor fall has a crescent~shaped hypodense collection crossing suture lines on CT. What is the diagnosis. [CKMC 25]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Subdural = torn bridging veins 4 crescentic, crosses sutures, not falx. Epidural = middle meningeal artery ￿ biconvex (lentiform), limited by sutures, lucid interval. Key note." source keyed epidural.

mcqs.subject: Anatomy
mcqs.question: A 40-year-old woman has a sudden "thunderclap" headache, neck stiffness and vomiting. The "worst headache of life" is typical of which condition. [CKMC 26. CKMC 25. BWP 25. KIMS 25]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: SAH: ruptured berry aneurysm (commonly Acom) 4 thunderclap headache. meningism." CT shows blood in cisterns." xanthochromic CSF if CT negative.

mcqs.subject: Anatomy
mcqs.question: A neonate has high-output heart failure from a vein of Galen malformation. Into which sinus does the great cerebral vein drain? [CKMC 25]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Internal cerebral veins + basal veins ￿ great cerebral vein (Galen) ￿ joins inferior sagittal sinus to form the straight sinus.

mcqs.subject: Anatomy
mcqs.question: A neurosurgeon approaching the pineal region enters the CSF space between the splenium of the corpus callosum and the superior surface of the cerebellum. Which cistern is this. [MUL 25]

options.A: Cistern of the great cerebral vein (quadrigeminal/superior cistern)

mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Superior (quadrigeminal) cistern contains the great cerebral vein and pineal gland. Interpeduncular cistern contains the circle of Willis; cisterna magna lies between cerebellum and medulla.

mcqs.subject: Anatomy
mcqs.question: A boy hit on the side of the head is lucid for an hour then becomes drowsy with a dilated pupil. CT shows a biconvex hyperdensity. Rupture of the middle meningeal artery causes which haemorrhage. [KIMS 26. MUL 25. HITEC 25. KIMS 25]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Pterion fracture 4 middle meningeal artery 4 extradural haematoma (lentiform, does not cross sutures), lucid interval, uncal herniation. Treat with urgent burr-hole evacuation.

mcqs.subject: Anatomy
mcqs.question: A melanoma deposit is found in the dura along the arachnoid granulations at the vertex. Into which sinus do tumour cells spreading via arachnoid villi most commonly enter. [WMC 25]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Arachnoid villi are concentrated in the lateral lacunae of the superior sagittal sinus. Melanoma commonly metastasizes to the brain and meninges.

mcqs.subject: Anatomy
mcqs.question: A man with an expanding temporal haematoma develops a fixed dilated pupil and then hemiparesis. Which part of the brainstem is compressed in uncal herniation. [WMC 25]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Uncus herniates through the tentorial notch 4 compresses CN111 (dilated pupil), cerebral peduncle (contralateral, or ipsilateral via Kernohan notch), PCA (occipital infarct), Duret haemorrhages in the midbrain/pons.

mcqs.subject: Anatomy
mcqs.question: During spinal surgery, the surgeon sees tooth-like lateral bands anchoring the cord to the dura between nerve roots. Denticulate ligaments are extensions of which layer. [KIMS 26. HITEC 25 . KIMS 25]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: 21 pairs of denticulate ligaments (pial) stabilise the cord in the dural sac; filum terminale internum is also pial, continuing from the conus to the coccyx (filum externum = dural).

mcqs.subject: Anatomy
mcqs.question: A child with a tethered cord has a thickened f ibrous strand running from the conus medullaris to the coccyx. What is this extension of the
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Filum terminale = pia mater continuation from the conus (Ll-L2), passing through the dural sac (ends S2) and attaching to the coccyx. Cauda equina lumbar and sacral nerve roots.

mcqs.subject: Anatomy
mcqs.question: A young man with a temporal bone fracture deteriorates after a lucid interval. What is the shape of an epidural haematoma on CT? [HITEC 25]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: EDH: biconvex, limited by sutures (dura is adherent there), may cross the falx/tentorium. SDH: crescent, crosses sutures. SAH: blood in sulci/cisterns.

mcqs.subject: Anatomy
mcqs.question: A neuroradiologist identifies the vein formed beneath the splenium of the corpus callosum. How is the great cerebral vein (of Galen) formed? [HITEC 25]

options.B: Union of two internal cerebral veins

mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Internal cerebral veins (formed at foramen of Monro by thalamostriate + choroidal veins) unite 4 great cerebral vein. which receives the basal veins and drains into the straight sinus.

mcqs.subject: Anatomy
mcqs.question: A boxer is struck on the side of the head where the frontal, parietal, temporal and sphenoid bones meet. Which artery may be damaged? [AMC 26 . MUL 26]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: The anterior branch of the middle meningeal artery grooves the inner surface at the pterion (thinnest part of the skull) 4 extradural haematoma.

mcqs.subject: Anatomy
mcqs.question: A man with a cervical disc prolapse has posterolateral herniation that compresses a nerve root. Which ligament resists direct posterior herniation of intervertebral discs. [AMC 26]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: The posterior longitudinal ligament (narrow, strongest in the midline) deflects herniations posterolaterally, where they compress the root exiting below (e.g. C5/6 disc ￿ C6 root; L4/5 disc 4 L5 root).

mcqs.subject: Anatomy
mcqs.question: A boy squeezes a boil on his upper lip and days later develops proptosis, chemosis and ophthalmoplegia. Thrombosis of which sinus has occurred? [CKMC 26. HITEC 26]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Danger triangle (nose-upper lip) drains via facial vein 4 ophthalmic veins (valveless) ￿ cavernous sinus; CN111, IV, VI, V2, Vl and ICA are affected (Vl first, lying free in the sinus).

mcqs.subject: Anatomy
mcqs.question: A patient with a cavernous sinus lesion has ophthalmoplegia with a small pupil. Compression of the sympathetic fibres around the ICA in the cavernous sinus causes which pupillary sign. [MUL 26]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Postganglionic sympathetic plexus on the ICA ￿ dilator pupillae,. injury 4 miosis (Horner). Combined111 + sympathetic lesion may leave a mid-sized fixed pupil.

mcqs.subject: Anatomy
mcqs.question: A man with a supratentorial meningioma has headache referred to the forehead. Pain from structures above the tentorium cerebelli is carried by which nerve. [MUL 26]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Supratentorial dura/vessels ￿ trigeminal (mainly Vl) 4 frontal/retro-orbital headache: infratentorial 4 upper cervical nerves (C2, C3) and vagus occipital/neck pain.

mcqs.subject: Anatomy
mcqs.question: A neurosurgeon explains venous drainage of the cavernous sinus. Into which sinus does the cavernous sinus drain posteriorly. [MUL 26]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Cavernous sinus receives ophthalmic veins, sphenoparietal sinus and superficial middle cerebral vein; drains via superior petrosal (- corrected direction. transverse/sigmoid) and inferior petrosal (4 IJV) sinuses. Source stem asked "which drains into"

mcqs.subject: Anatomy
mcqs.question: A patient with an infected stye develops proptosis and cavernous sinus thrombosis. Which vein directly connects the facial veins with the cavernous sinus. [HITEC 26]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Angular/facial vein fr> superior ophthalmic vein (valveless) 4 cavernous sinus." pterygoid plexus H inferior ophthalmic vein and emissary veins are other routes.

mcqs.subject: Anatomy
mcqs.question: A child with suspected meningitis undergoes lumbar puncture at L4-L5. From which space is CSF obtained? [BWP 26]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Needle passes skin ￿ supraspinous ￿ interspinous ligament ￿ ligamentum flavum (give) ￿ epidural space ￿ dura and arachnoid 4 subarachnoid space (lumbar cistern with cauda equina).

mcqs.subject: Anatomy
mcqs.question: During a neurosurgical approach to the third ventricle, the surgeon identifies the lamina terminalis forming its anterior wall. Which commissure lies within it? [Prof 24. KIMS 26]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Lamina terminalis = closed rostral end of the neural tube (anterior neuropore); contains the anterior commissure. Posterior commissure lies at the junction of third ventricle and aqueduct (posterior wall).

mcqs.subject: Anatomy
mcqs.question: A radiologist describes a dilated central canal of the spinal cord in syringomyelia. What does the normal central canal contain? [Prof 25]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: The central canal is lined by ependyma, continuous above with the fourth ventricle and contains CSF; it ends in the terminal ventricle in the conus medullaris.

mcqs.subject: Anatomy
mcqs.question: A child has hydrocephalus. The neurosurgeon explains where CSF is made and where it is absorbed. Which structure produces CSF? [Prof 25. WMC 26. CKMC 25. MUL 25]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Choroid plexus (ependyma-derived choroid epithelium, tight junctions = blood-CSF barrier) secretes-500 muday; total volume~150 ML." absorbed by arachnoid villi/granulations into the dural sinuses.

mcqs.subject: Anatomy
mcqs.question: A child with hydrocephalus has obstruction of the median aperture (foramen of Magendie) by a tumour. In the roof of which ventricle is this aperture located? [Prof 25]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: The fourth ventricle drains into the subarachnoid space through the median aperture (Magendie, into cisterna magna) and two lateral apertures (Luschka, into cerebellopontine angle). Dandy-walker: atresia of these foramina.

mcqs.subject: Anatomy
mcqs.question: A child has enlarged lateral, third and fourth ventricles with no obstructing mass on MRI. What causes this type of ventricular enlargement? [CKMC 25]

options.A: Overproduction or impaired absorption of CSF (communicating hydrocephalus)

mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Communicating hydrocephalus." CSF flows freely from ventricles to subarachnoid space but is not absorbed (meningitis, SAH) or is overproduced (choroid plexus papilloma). Non-communicating: obstruction within ventricles (aqueduct).

mcqs.subject: Anatomy
mcqs.question: In a patient with sagittal sinus thrombosis, CSF absorption fails and intracranial pressure rises. Into which sinus do most arachnoid villi drain CSF? [HITEC 26. MUL 25]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Arachnoid granulations are largest and most numerous along the superior sagittal sinus and its lateral lacunae; they calcify with age and indent the skull (granular foveolae).

mcqs.subject: Anatomy
mcqs.question: A child with headache has dilated lateral and third ventricles but a small fourth ventricle. Through which channel does the third ventricle communicate with the fourth? [HITEC 26. HITEC 25]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Lateral ventricles 4 foramina of Monro 4 third ventricle 4 cerebral aqueduct (narrowest part, commonest site of obstruction) ￿ fourth ventricle Magendie/Luschka 4 subarachnoid space.

mcqs.subject: Anatomy
mcqs.question: A radiologist describes the paired C-shaped cavities within the cerebral hemispheres on MRI. Which ventricles are these. [BWP 25]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Lateral ventricles curve (C-shape) following hemisphere growth: anterior horn (frontal), body. atrium/trigone, posterior horn (occipital), inferior horn (temporal).

mcqs.subject: Anatomy
mcqs.question: A man has headache and papilloedema; MRI shows dilatation of one lateral ventricle while the third ventricle is normal. Where is the likely obstruction. [AMC 26. KIMS 25]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Obstruction at the foramen of Monro (colloid cyst of third ventricle. tumour) dilates the lateral ventricle(s) proximal to it," aqueductal obstruction dilates both laterals and third.

mcqs.subject: Anatomy
mcqs.question: A child with aqueductal stenosis has large lateral and third ventricles. Which type of hydrocephalus does aqueductal stenosis cause. [WMC 26 . KIMS 26]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Obstruction within the ventricular system = non-communicating. NPH (wet, wobbly, wacky: incontinence, gait apraxia, dementia) is communicating; ex vacuo = atrophy (Alzheimer, Huntington).

mcqs.subject: Anatomy
mcqs.question: A neurosurgeon operating through the body of the lateral ventricle identifies the structure forming most of its floor. Which structure is this. [HITEC 26]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Body of lateral ventricle: roof = corpus callosum," medial wall = septum pellucidum and fornix; floor = thalamus (medially) and body of caudate (laterally) with the stria terminalis between.

mcqs.subject: Anatomy
mcqs.question: A 72~year-old man has a broad-based magnetic gait, urinary incontinence and progressive forgetfulness. CT shows enlarged ventricles with no obstruction and normal CSF opening pressure on lumbar puncture. What is the most likely diagnosis. [CKMC 26]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Stem created: the source recall was incomplete ("enlarged ventricles"). NPH = communicating hydrocephalus with impaired CSF absorption: "wet, wobbly, wacky"; improves after large-volume LP or VP shunt. Ex vacuo = ventricles enlarge from brain atrophy.

mcqs.subject: Anatomy
mcqs.topicName: Blood Supply of Brain & Spinal Cord
mcqs.question: A 68-year-old hypertensive man has sudden weakness of the left leg and foot, with relatively spared face and arm. Occlusion of which artery is most likely? [Prof 24. HITEC 26 . HITEC 25]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: ACA supplies the medial surface (paracentral lobule) = leg and foot area of the homunculus. MCA = face and arm > leg," PCA = visual cortex (contralateral homonymous hemianopia with macular sparing).

mcqs.subject: Anatomy
mcqs.topicName: Blood Supply of Brain & Spinal Cord
mcqs.question: A neurologist explains that drugs reach some brain regions easily because they lack a blood-brain barrier (circumventricular organs). Which structure has an intact blood-brain barrier. [Prof 24]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Circumventricular organs lacking BBB." area postrema (vomiting centre), median eminence, posterior pituitary, pineal, subfornical organ. OVLT. Deep nuclei like the corpus striatum have an intact BBB.

mcqs.subject: Anatomy
mcqs.topicName: Blood Supply of Brain & Spinal Cord
mcqs.question: A neurosurgeon dissecting the lateral sulcus identifies a vein draining the insula that joins the basal vein. What is it called? [Prof 25]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Deep middle cerebral vein drains insula 4 joins anterior cerebral vein to form the basal vein (of Rosenthal) 4 great cerebral vein. Superficial middle cerebral vein runs on the surface of the lateral sulcus to the cavernous sinus.

mcqs.subject: Anatomy
mcqs.topicName: Blood Supply of Brain & Spinal Cord
mcqs.question: A patient develops paraplegia after repair of a thoracoabdominal aortic aneurysm. Which artery, the largest anterior radicular artery supplying the lower cord, was probably compromised? [Prof 25. AMC 25]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Arteria radicularis magna (Adamkiewicz)." usually left side, T9-L2, a branch of a posterior intercostal/lumbar (segmental) artery," reinforces the anterior spinal artery to the lower two-thirds of the cord.

mcqs.subject: Anatomy
mcqs.topicName: Blood Supply of Brain & Spinal Cord
mcqs.question: A 70-year-old hypertensive man has a pure motor stroke from a lacunar infarct of the posterior limb of the internal capsule. Which arteries supply this deep territory of the middle cerebral artery. [Prof 25. MUL 26. LHR 25. WMC 25]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Lenticulostriate (lateral striate) arteries from MCA Ml = "arteries of cerebral haemorrhage" (Charcot); supply putamen. caudate, internal capsule. Charcot-Bouchard microaneurysms rupture in hypertension.

mcqs.subject: Anatomy
mcqs.topicName: Blood Supply of Brain & Spinal Cord
mcqs.question: A patient with a pontine vascular loop has a lateral rectus palsy; at operation the nerve is seen crossed by an artery as it ascends from the pontomedullary junction. Which artery is closely related to the abducens nerve here? [AMC 25]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: CN Vl emerges at the pontomedullary junction and ascends in the prepontine cistern, usually dorsal to the AICA, beside the basilar artery. Key note: source keyed basilar; AICA is the classic crossing relation.

mcqs.subject: Anatomy
mcqs.topicName: Blood Supply of Brain & Spinal Cord
mcqs.question: A patient has sudden monocular blindness from thrombosis of the internal carotid artery just after it leaves the cavernous sinus. Blood flow to which branch is blocked first? [AMC 25]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: The ophthalmic artery is the first branch of the ICA after it emerges from the cavernous sinus (medial to anterior clinoid). Amaurosis fugax = transient retinal ischaemia from carotid emboli.

mcqs.subject: Anatomy
mcqs.topicName: Blood Supply of Brain & Spinal Cord
mcqs.question: After aortic surgery, a patient has paraplegia and loss of pain and temperature below TIO, but vibration and joint sense are preserved. Occlusion of which artery causes this. [MUL 26. KIMS 26. LHR 25. QIMS 25. KIMS 25]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Anterior spinal artery supplies the anterior two-thirds of the cord (anterior horns, corticospinal and spinothalamic tracts); the dorsal columns (posterior spinal arteries) are spared.

mcqs.subject: Anatomy
mcqs.topicName: Blood Supply of Brain & Spinal Cord
mcqs.question: A woman has sudden severe headache with a painful, dilated pupil and ptosis on the left. An aneurysm of the posterior communicating artery compresses which nerve? [LHR 25]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: CN111 runs parallel and lateral to the Pcomm," aneurysm compresses the superficial pupillomotor fibres first 4 "surgical" third nerve palsy with a dilated pupil.

mcqs.subject: Anatomy
mcqs.topicName: Blood Supply of Brain & Spinal Cord
mcqs.question: A man suddenly cannot understand speech and speaks fluent jargon. Which artery supplies Wernicke area. [CKMC 25]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: MCA supplies the lateral surface: superior division 4 Broca area. motor/sensory face-arm; inferior division 4 Wernicke area, superior temporal gyrus, optic radiation (Meyer loop).

mcqs.subject: Anatomy
mcqs.topicName: Blood Supply of Brain & Spinal Cord
mcqs.question: A 65-year-old woman has a right homonymous hemianopia with macular sparing after a stroke. Which artery supplies the visual cortex. [KIMS 26. CKMC 25. KIMS 25]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: PCA (calcarine branch) supplies area 17. Macular sparing occurs because the occipital pole receives collateral MCA supply.

mcqs.subject: Anatomy
mcqs.topicName: Blood Supply of Brain & Spinal Cord
mcqs.question: An angiogram shows the circle of Willis. What does the posterior communicating artery connect? [HITEC 26 . HITEC 25]

options.A: Anterior cerebral artery with basilar artery
options.B: Basilar artery with anterior communicating artery
options.C: Internal carotid artery with posterior cerebral artery
options.D: Vertebral artery with middle cerebral artery

mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Circle of Willis." ACAS joined by Acom." ICA joined to PCA by Pcomm. Commonest aneurysm sites." Acom > PComm-ICA junction > MCA bifurcation.

mcqs.subject: Anatomy
mcqs.topicName: Blood Supply of Brain & Spinal Cord
mcqs.question: A man has a left CN111 palsy with right hemiplegia from a ventral midbrain infarct. Occlusion of which artery causes Weber syndrome? [HITEC 25]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Midbrain is supplied by PCA and basilar paramedian branches; Weber syndrome = PCA penetrating branches to the crus cerebri and CN111 fascicles.

mcqs.subject: Anatomy
mcqs.topicName: Blood Supply of Brain & Spinal Cord
mcqs.question: A 60-year-old woman has weakness and numbness of the right face and arm, with expressive aphasia; the leg is relatively spared. Occlusion of which artery causes this. [HITEC 25. BWP 25. KIMS 25]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: MCA (lateral convexity)." contralateral face/arm > leg weakness and sensory loss, homonymous hemianopia, aphasia (dominant) or neglect (non-dominant).

mcqs.subject: Anatomy
mcqs.topicName: Blood Supply of Brain & Spinal Cord
mcqs.question: A patient develops sudden loss of vibration and joint position sense in both legs with preserved strength. Occlusion of which artery causes this. [BWP 25]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Two posterior spinal arteries (from vertebral or PICA) supply the posterior one-third of the cord (dorsal columns, posterior horns). Infarction is rare because of good anastomoses.

mcqs.subject: Anatomy
mcqs.topicName: Blood Supply of Brain & Spinal Cord
mcqs.question: A 50-year-old hypertensive woman has sudden severe headache, vomiting and neck stiffness; CT shows blood in the basal cisterns. Which vessel has most likely ruptured? [QIMS 25]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Berry (saccular) aneurysms at branch points of the circle of Willis: Acom (~35%) > PComm/lCA > MCA. Risk: ADPKD, Ehlers-Danlos, Marfan, hypertension, smoking.

mcqs.subject: Anatomy
mcqs.topicName: Blood Supply of Brain & Spinal Cord
mcqs.question: A 72-year-old man suddenly becomes blind in both eyes but his pupils still react normally to light. Infarction in which arterial territory is most likely: [QIMS 25]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Cortical blindness with preserved light reflex (the reflex arc ends at the pretectum) = bilateral occipital (PCA/top-of-basilar) infarction." may deny blindness (Anton syndrome).

mcqs.subject: Anatomy
mcqs.topicName: Blood Supply of Brain & Spinal Cord
mcqs.question: A patient has loss of vibration and position sense on the left side of the body and his tongue deviates to the right after a medullary stroke. Which artery is most likely affected? [QIMS 25]

options.D: Posterior inferior cerebellar artery that would be lateral

mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Medial medullary syndrome = anterior spinal/vertebral paramedian branches. Source stem said "pain and temperature" medulla (PICA); medial lemniscus loss + Xll palsy fits the keyed ASA.

mcqs.subject: Anatomy
mcqs.topicName: Blood Supply of Brain & Spinal Cord
mcqs.question: An MRI shows infarction of the anterior part of the thoracic spinal cord. Which part of the cord does the anterior spinal artery supply. [CKMC 26. QIMS 25]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Single anterior spinal artery (from both vertebrals) 4 anterior two-thirds via sulcal arteries: paired posterior spinal arteries 4 posterior one-third. Watershed at T4 and Ll.

mcqs.subject: Anatomy
mcqs.topicName: Blood Supply of Brain & Spinal Cord
mcqs.question: A neuroradiologist traces the branches running over the insula deep in the lateral sulcus. Which artery supplies the insular cortex. [AMC 26]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: MCA M2 segments run over the insula (insular segment) before emerging onto the lateral surface (opercular/cortical segments).

mcqs.subject: Anatomy
mcqs.topicName: Blood Supply of Brain & Spinal Cord
mcqs.question: A patient with cavernous sinus thrombosis has engorged veins on the lateral surface of the brain. Which vein drains the lateral cerebral cortex along the lateral sulcus into the cavernous sinus. [LHR 26]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Superficial middle cerebral vein 4 cavernous/sphenoparietal sinus,. anastomoses: superior (Trolard) to SSS and inferior (Labbe) to transverse sinus.

mcqs.subject: Anatomy
mcqs.topicName: Blood Supply of Brain & Spinal Cord
mcqs.question: A woman develops non-fluent aphasia from an embolic stroke. Which artery primarily supplies Broca area. [CKMC 26]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: MCA superior division 4 frontal operculum (Broca area) and the face/arm motor cortex: inferior division 4 Wernicke area.

mcqs.subject: Anatomy
mcqs.topicName: Blood Supply of Brain & Spinal Cord
mcqs.question: A pontine infarct causes an internuclear ophthalmoplegia and contralateral hemiparesis. Which vessels supply the paramedian region of the pons. [CKMC 26]

options.D: Paramedian branches of the basilar artery

mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Pons: paramedian branches (medial - CST, medial lemniscus, MLF, VI), short and long circumferential branches + AICA/SCA (lateral pons).

mcqs.subject: Anatomy
mcqs.topicName: Blood Supply of Brain & Spinal Cord
mcqs.question: A right-handed man develops sudden weakness of his right leg; his face and arm are relatively spared. Which artery is most likely occluded? [CKMC 26. KIMS 26]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: The leg area (paracentral lobule) of the LEFT hemisphere. supplied by the left ACA, controls the right leg.

mcqs.subject: Anatomy
mcqs.topicName: Blood Supply of Brain & Spinal Cord
mcqs.question: A woman with an anterior cerebral artery infarct develops apathy and akinetic mutism. Which artery primarily supplies the cingulate gyrus. [BWP 26]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: ACA (callosomarginal and pericallosal branches) supplies the medial frontal and parietal cortex including the cingulate gyrus and anterior 4/5 of the corpus callosum," bilateral lesions 4 abulia/akinetic mutism.

mcqs.subject: Anatomy
mcqs.topicName: Blood Supply of Brain & Spinal Cord
mcqs.question: An angiogram is reviewed in a patient with a visual memory deficit. Which artery primarily supplies the inferior (and inferomedial) surface of the temporal lobe. [BWP 26]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: PCA temporal branches supply the inferior temporal surface, hippocampus and parahippocampal gyrus (and occipital lobe). MCA supplies the temporal pole and lateral (superior/middle) temporal gyri.

mcqs.subject: Anatomy
mcqs.topicName: Blood Supply of Brain & Spinal Cord
mcqs.question: A drug fails to enter the brain because of the blood-brain barrier. By which structure is the BBB primarily maintained? [BWP 26]

options.A: Tight junctions between capillary endothelial cells

mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: BBB: continuous non-fenestrated endothelium with tight junctions (claudins, occludin). basement membrane, astrocytic end-feet and pericytes," lipid-soluble molecules cross freely.

mcqs.subject: Anatomy
mcqs.topicName: Blood Supply of Brain & Spinal Cord
mcqs.question: A 60-year-old hypertensive diabetic develops sudden right hemiplegia and slurred speech. Which investigation is performed first? [BWP 26]

options.C: Non-contrast CT scan of the brain

mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Stem created: the source recall was incomplete (clinical scenario and options missing). Non-contrast CT first excludes haemorrhage before thrombolysis (within 4.5 h); early ischaemic changes may be invisible; diffusion MRI is most sensitive for infarction. PHYSIOLOGY

mcqs.subject: Physiology
mcqs.question: A man develops descending paralysis, ptosis and dilated pupils after eating home-canned food. What is the mechanism of botulinum toxin. [MUL 25]

options.C: Inhibits Ach release at the neuromuscular junction

mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Botulinum toxin cleaves SNARE proteins (SNAP-25. synaptobrevin, syntaxin) ￿ no vesicle fusion 4 no Ach release ￿ flaccid paralysis. Tetanus toxin blocks glycine/GABA release from Renshaw cells 4 spastic paralysis.

mcqs.subject: Physiology
mcqs.question: After thyroidectomy, a patient given succinylcholine remains apnoeic for several hours. Deficiency of which enzyme is responsible? [WMC 25]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Plasma (pseudo)cholinesterase hydrolyses succinylcholine and mivacurium; atypical (dibucaine-resistant) variant 4 prolonged apnoea ("scoline apnoea").

mcqs.subject: Physiology
mcqs.question: A neuroscientist records a small depolarization in a motor neuron after a single excitatory input. What is true about the excitatory postsynaptic potential? [QIMS 25]

options.A: It is due to opening of chloride channels
options.B: It is due to opening of ligand~gated Na. (cation) channels
options.C: It is graded and must summate to reach threshold
options.D: Develops with a single impulse to reach threshold always

mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: EPSP." transmitter opens cation (mainly Na.) channels 4 local depolarization (-+0.5- 1 mv per terminal): many must summate (spatial/temporal) to reach threshold (--45 mv) at the axon hillock.

mcqs.subject: Physiology
mcqs.question: Synaptic inputs on distant dendrites must spread to the soma of a motor neuron. By which process are signals transferred from dendrites to soma. [QIMS 25]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Most dendrites have few voltage-gated Na. channels, so potentials spread electrotonically with decrement; distal synapses are therefore less effective than those near the soma.

mcqs.subject: Physiology
mcqs.question: A 2-year-old with high fever is hyperventilating and has a febrile convulsion. What effect does hyperventilation have on neuronal activity. [QIMS 25]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Alkalosis (pH 7.8-8.0) increases neuronal excitability ￿ seizures; acidosis (pH <7.0) depresses ￿ coma. Hyperventilation is used during EEG to provoke absence seizures.

mcqs.subject: Physiology
mcqs.question: Cardiac muscle cells and some neurons communicate through gap junctions. Which property is specif ic to electrical synapses. [KIMS 25]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Electrical synapses (gap junctions, connexins): bidirectional, no delay, synchronize groups of cells. Chemical synapses." one-way, synaptic delay (~0.5 ms), fatigue.

mcqs.subject: Physiology
mcqs.question: A woman with myasthenia gravis is treated with neostigmine. On which receptor does the accumulated Ach act at the neuromuscular junction. [KIMS 25]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Neostigmine inhibits acetylcholinesterase ￿ t Ach at nicotinic receptors (antibodies in MG reduce their number). Quaternary - does not cross BBB.

mcqs.subject: Physiology
mcqs.question: A toxin blocks voltage-gated channels in presynaptic terminals and stops transmitter release (Lambert-Eaton). Influx of which ion triggers neurotransmitter release. [KIMS 25]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: AP opens P/Q-type Ca" channels at active zones ￿ Ca" binds synaptotagmin ￿ SNARE-mediated vesicle fusion. Lambert-Eaton: antibodies against these channels.

mcqs.subject: Physiology
mcqs.question: A woman on diuretics has a serum potassium of 2.5 mmol/L. Which neuromuscular effect commonly results. [LHR 26]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Hypokalaemia hyperpolarizes the membrane (more negative RMP) 4 reduced excitability 4 weakness, hyporeflexia, ileus, U waves. Tetany results from hypocalcaemia.

mcqs.subject: Physiology
mcqs.question: A neuron that has just received a subthreshold input responds more strongly to a second input. What does facilitation mean in synaptic physiology? [CKMC 26]

options.C: Increased postsynaptic excitability after prior or repeated stimulation

mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Facilitation." membrane brought closer to threshold (subthreshold EPSP) or post-tetanic potentiation from residual presynaptic Ca" 4 greater response to the next stimulus.

mcqs.subject: Physiology
mcqs.question: A drug (4-aminopyridine) blocks the K" channels that repolarize the presynaptic terminal. What is the likely effect on synaptic transmission. [BWP 26]

options.B: Shortened action potential and reduced release
options.D: Prolonged action potential and increased transmitter release

mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Delayed repolarization keeps voltage-gated Ca" channels open longer 4 more Ca" entry 4 more vesicle fusion; 4-AP is used in Lambert-Eaton and MS.

mcqs.subject: Physiology
mcqs.question: Stimulating the postsynaptic membrane of a chemical synapse produces no change in the presynaptic neuron. Which property explains this. [KIMS 26]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Chemical synapses conduct only from presynaptic (vesicles) to postsynaptic (receptors) - the "principle of one-way conduction" which gives direction to neural circuits.

mcqs.subject: Physiology
mcqs.question: Stimulating nerve A alone excites 10 motor neurons and nerve B alone excites 10; stimulating both together excites only 16. What is this property called? [MUL 25]
mcqs.explanation: Occlusion: overlapping discharge zones of two inputs ￿ combined response less than the sum. Opposite = subliminal fringe facilitation (combined response greater than the sum).

mcqs.subject: Physiology
mcqs.question: A gymnast lifts her leg; one pyramidal cell activates 2000 muscle fibres in the quadriceps. Which neuronal circuit is involved? [QIMS 25]
mcqs.explanation: Divergence (amplifying type): one input excites many output neurons (corticospinal ￿ many anterior horn cells). Convergence." many inputs to one neuron. Reverberating circuits prolong output.

mcqs.subject: Physiology
mcqs.question: After repeated high-frequency stimulation of a hippocampal pathway, synaptic strength remains increased for hours. What is this phenomenon. [KIMS 26]
mcqs.explanation: LTP: glutamate on NMDA receptors (Mg" block removed by depolarization) 4 Ca" entry 4 CaMKII 4 more AMPA receptors; cellular basis of memory. Source options lacked LTP." added.

mcqs.subject: Physiology
mcqs.question: After a brief sensory stimulus, a motor neuron keeps firing for several seconds because its output re-excites the same pool through collateral loops. Which neuronal circuit explains this prolonged after~discharge. [CKMC 26]
mcqs.explanation: I: Source note: this question slot was blank in the CKMC 26 recall," a high-yield question on the same block topic has been added. Reverberating circuits (positive feedback loops) prolong output after the input stops - basis of rhythmic activity (respiration) and short-term memory; they fatigue as synaptic transmitter is depleted. NEUROTRANSMirrERS

mcqs.subject: Physiology
mcqs.question: Acetylcholine excites skeletal muscle but slows the heart. What determines whether a neurotransmitter is excitatory or inhibitory. [QIMS 25]

options.A: The shape of its synaptic vesicle
options.B: The function of its postsynaptic receptor
options.D: The width of the synaptic cleft

mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: The receptor determines the response: Ach on nicotinic (cation channel) excites; on M2 (Gi, opens K. channels) inhibits the SA node.

mcqs.subject: Physiology
mcqs.question: GABA released at a synapse hyperpolarizes the postsynaptic neuron. What is the action of inhibitory neurotransmitters. [KIMS 25]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: IPSP: opening of Cl- channels (GABA-A, glycine) or K. channels (GABA-B, M2) 4 hyperpolarization (-70 4 -75 MV).

mcqs.subject: Physiology
mcqs.question: A student studying all night before exams feels hyper-alert despite fatigue. Increased wakefulness during stress is associated with increased release of which transmitter? [AMC 26]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Locus coeruleus NE (with Ach, histamine, orexin, serotonin) maintains arousal via the ascending reticular activating system," stress activates the LC.

mcqs.subject: Physiology
mcqs.question: A patient with epilepsy is given a drug that enhances the brain's main inhibitory transmitter. What is the major inhibitory neurotransmitter in the brain. [CKMC 26]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: GABA (from glutamate by glutamate decarboxylase, B6) - main inhibitory transmitter in brain," glycine in spinal cord and brainstem. Benzodiazepines and barbiturates enhance GABA-A.

mcqs.subject: Physiology
mcqs.question: A student is asked which transmitter may act as inhibitory in the CNS. Which of the following can act as an inhibitory neurotransmitter. [CKMC 26]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Dopamine is inhibitory at D2 receptors (indirect pathway, pituitary lactotrophs) and excitatory at DI. Inhibitory: GABA, glycine, dopamine (D2), enkephalins," excitatory: glutamate, aspartate, Ach (nicotinic), substance P.

mcqs.subject: Physiology
mcqs.question: A man with a posterior spinal cord lesion loses vibration sense and joint position sense below the lesion; pain and temperature are normal. Which tract is damaged? [Prof 24]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Dorsal columns (gracilis = lower limb, medial; cuneatus = upper limb, lateral, above T6) carry fine touch, vibration, conscious proprioception. Positive Romberg sign = sensory ataxia.

mcqs.subject: Physiology
mcqs.question: A diabetic with neuropathy cannot distinguish two points on his fingertips 3 mm apart and has lost vibration sense. Which pathway transmits two-point discrimination and vibration. [KIMS 26 . LHR 25 . CKMC 25 . MUL 25 . HITEC 25]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: DCML.. large AF fibres, high spatial resolution - fine touch, two-point discrimination, vibration, conscious proprioception, stereognosis. Anterolateral: pain, temperature, crude touch, itch, tickle.

mcqs.subject: Physiology
mcqs.question: A man with an anterior spinal cord lesion cannot feel a cotton wisp crudely touching his leg, though vibration and joint position are intact. Which tract carries crude touch and pressure. [MUL 25 . WMC 25 . HITEC 25]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Anterior spinothalamic tract." crude (light, poorly localized) touch and pressure; lateral spinothalamic." pain and temperature. Light touch is doubly represented (DC + anterior ST), so it is rarely lost completely.

mcqs.subject: Physiology
mcqs.question: After a stab wound, a man loses pain and temperature in his left leg. Which sensations are lost in his right leg. [MUL 25]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Left leg pain loss = right spinothalamic lesion 4 right hemisection 4 right dorsal columns also cut 4 right leg loses proprioception, vibration, fine touch (plus right UMN paralysis).

mcqs.subject: Physiology
mcqs.question: A man has a right hemisection of the spinal cord at C2 from a stab wound. Which sensations are lost below the lesion. [WMC 25]

options.A: Touch and temperature on the same side

mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Hemisection: ipsilateral loss of DC modalities (fine touch, vibration, proprioception) and contralateral loss of pain and temperature; at c2 there may also be phrenic involvement.

mcqs.subject: Physiology
mcqs.question: A patient with large-fibre neuropathy loses vibration and joint position sense. Which fibres carry vibration and proprioception. [BWP 25]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: AF (30-70 m/s): touch, pressure, vibration. joint position (and Aa/la, Ib from muscle). A6: fast pain, cold. C: slow pain. warmth, itch.

mcqs.subject: Physiology
mcqs.question: An 18-year-old skateboarder injures his spine and loses vibration sense in his left leg. Which tract is damaged? [KIMS 25]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Dorsal columns are uncrossed in the cord. so vibration loss in the left leg = left dorsal column lesion.

mcqs.subject: Physiology
mcqs.question: A physiologist compares conduction velocities of different ne￿e fibres. Which fibres conduct impulses fastest? [AMC 26]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Velocity diameter (myelinated, ~6 m/s per Hm) via saltatory conduction; Aa (12-20 um) 70-120 m/s. Unmyelinated velocity ddiameter.

mcqs.subject: Physiology
mcqs.question: A patient with an anterolateral cordotomy for pain notices he has also lost itch sensation below the lesion. Which pathway carries itch? [CKMC 261
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Itch: C fibres (histamine-sensitive and non-histaminergic) ￿ lamina l 4 anterolateral (spinothalamic) system, as for pain, temperature, tickle and crude touch.

mcqs.subject: Physiology
mcqs.question: A neurologist explains why a hemisection causes contralateral pain loss. At which level do the fibres of the anterolateral (spinothalamic) system decussate. [HITEC 26]

options.C: Spinal cord, within 1-2 segments of entry (anterior white

mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Spinothalamic second-order fibres cross in the anterior white commissure near their entry level,. DCML fibres cross in the medulla (internal arcuate fibres)," CST crosses at the pyramidal decussation.

mcqs.subject: Physiology
mcqs.question: A patient with large-f ibre neuropathy loses vibration and joint position sense. Which fibres mainly carry vibration and proprioception. [BWP 26]

options.A: Large myelinated Aa and AF fibres

mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Proprioception: Aa (la, Ib) from spindles and tendon organs, AF from joints: vibration." Afj from Pacinian/Meissner corpuscles.

mcqs.subject: Physiology
mcqs.question: A neurologist tests sensations carried by the dorsal column-medial lemniscus pathway. Which sensation is carried by this pathway. [HITEC 26]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Stem created: the source recall was incomplete (DCML question was incomplete). DCML: vibration. fine touch, two-point discrimination, conscious proprioception, stereognosis. Anterolateral." pain. temperature, itch, crude touch.

mcqs.subject: Physiology
mcqs.question: A man whose leg was amputated a year ago still feels pain in his missing foot. Which law explains phantom limb pain. [LHR 25]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Law of projection." wherever a sensory pathway is stimulated. the sensation is felt at the receptor location. Muller law (specific nerve energies): each pathway gives one modality (labelled line).

mcqs.subject: Physiology
mcqs.question: A sensory physiologist records from a Pacinian corpuscle; graded depolarization appears before any spike occurs. What is this subthreshold potential called? [LHR 25]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Receptor (generator) potential." graded, non-propagated, proportional to stimulus strength," when it exceeds threshold at the first node, action potentials fire at a rate proportional to its amplitude.

mcqs.subject: Physiology
mcqs.question: A physiologist finds a receptor that f ires only at the onset and offset of pressure and stops during constant pressure. Which is a rapidly adapting (phasic) receptor. [AMC 26. MUL 25. WMC 25]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Pacinian corpuscle: onion-like lamellae in deep dermis, detects vibration (30-800 Hz) and rapid indentation; adapts within milliseconds. Slowly adapting (tonic): Merkel discs, Ruffini endings, spindles, GTO. nociceptors.

mcqs.subject: Physiology
mcqs.question: A boy whose thumb has been in a plaster cast for weeks still feels its continuous pressure. Which receptor detects sustained pressure and stretch of the skin. [MUL 25. BWP 25. KIMS 25]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Ruffini endings: deep dermis and joint capsules, very slowly adapting, signal continuous deformation, heavy prolonged touch and joint position. Merkel discs: sustained light touch.

mcqs.subject: Physiology
mcqs.question: A man with a scarred, burned fingertip cannot feel light touch on the glabrous skin. Which receptor in the dermal papillae has been damaged? [WMC 25. BWP 25]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Meissner corpuscles: dermal papillae of glabrous skin (fingertips, lips), rapidly adapting, fine discriminative touch and low-frequency vibration (flutter). Merkel discs." epidermal base, slowly adapting.

mcqs.subject: Physiology
mcqs.question: A man has vivid sensations and pain in an arm amputated two years earlier. Which mechanism mainly explains phantom limb pain? [BWP 25]

options.D: Reorganization of the somatosensory cortex and CNS

mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Phantom limb." cortical remapping (face area invades hand area), central sensitization and neuroma activity; perceived in the missing limb by the law of projection.

mcqs.subject: Physiology
mcqs.question: A 10-year-old girl with type I diabetes develops a neuropathy limited to fibres ending as free nerve endings. Transmission of which sensation is affected? [QIMS 25]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Free nerve endings (A6 and C) detect pain, temperature, itch, crude touch. Fine touch, vibration and pressure use encapsulated/expanded endings (Meissner, Pacinian, Merkel, Ruffini).

mcqs.subject: Physiology
mcqs.question: A sensory physiologist examines how stimulus strength is coded. Which statement about sensory signalling is true. [QIMS 25]

options.B: In spatial summation, stronger signals are carried by progressively more fibres

mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Intensity is coded by spatial summation (recruiting more fibres) and temporal summation (higher firing frequency in each fibre).

mcqs.subject: Physiology
mcqs.question: A neurosurgeon picks up a scalpel, activating mechanoreceptors in her hand. What is the basis of sensory transduction. [QIMS 25]

options.A: Increased ion permeability of the receptor membrane
options.C: Activation of G proteins in all receptors

mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Stimuli deform/act on the receptor membrane 4 opening of ion (mainly Na'/cation) channels 4 receptor potential. Exception: photoreceptors hyperpolarize (closure of CGMP channels).

mcqs.subject: Physiology
mcqs.question: A cook chopping onions develops stinging eyes and tears. Which receptor types are involved? [AMC 26]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Onion releases syn-propanethial-s-oxide 4 activates TRPAI on corneal nociceptive/chemosensitive (trigeminal Vl) endings ￿ stinging and reflex lacrimation (Vll parasympathetic).

mcqs.subject: Physiology
mcqs.question: A student holding a pencil feels its continuous pressure on his fingertips. Which receptors are stimulated? [BWP 26]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Merkel discs (Iggo domes, epidermal base) - slowly adapting, continuous light touch and texture/shape; Ruffini - skin stretch and heavy sustained pressure.

mcqs.subject: Physiology
mcqs.question: A woman stabbed in the back has a right hemisection of the spinal cord. Which statement about Brown-séquard syndrome is correct? [QIMS 25]

options.A: Loss of tone and reflexes on the opposite side at the level
options.B: Upper motor neuron paralysis on the same side below the lesion
options.C: All sensation is lost on the same side below the lesion

mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Hemisection: ipsilateral spastic (UMN) paralysis below the lesion,. pain/temperature are lost on the OPPOSITE side. so not "all sensation" ipsilaterally.

mcqs.subject: Physiology
mcqs.question: A young man with complete transection of the thoracic cord has f laccid legs, absent reflexes and a flaccid bladder for the first two weeks; later the legs become spastic. What explains the initial phase. [CKMC 26]

options.A: Damage to all anterior horn cells
options.B: Spinal shock loss of tonic facilitation from higher centres

mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Source note: this question slot was blank in the CKMC 26 recall; a high-yield question on the same block topic has been added. Spinal shock: cord neurons lose descending facilitatory input 4 areflexia, hypotonia, fall in BP; reflexes return in days-weeks (first the bulbocavernosus/anal reflex), then hyperreflexia and mass reflex develop.

mcqs.subject: Physiology
mcqs.question: A woman with intractable pain in the left leg from pelvic malignancy is treated with anterolateral cordotomy in the thoracic cord. Which tract is cut? [Prof 24]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Pain fibres cross within 1-2 segments in the anterior white commissure, so pain from the left leg ascends in the RIGHT lateral spinothalamic tract. Cordotomy is done on the side opposite the pain.

mcqs.subject: Physiology
mcqs.question: A patient pricked with a pin feels a sharp pain, followed a second later by a dull, diffuse, burning pain. Which pathway carries the second pain. [Prof 24]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Fast pain: AS fibres (6-30 m/s) 4 lamina l 4 neospinothalamic 4 VPL; glutamate." well localized. Slow pain: C fibres (0.5-2 m/s) 4 laminae Il/lll paleospinothalamic 4 reticular formation, intralaminar nuclei," substance P," poorly localized.

mcqs.subject: Physiology
mcqs.question: A patient with a lung abscess deep in the parenchyma has no pain until the pleura is involved. Which structure does not transmit pain. [CKMC 25]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Lung parenchyma, visceral pleura and brain substance are insensitive to pain. Parietal pleura (intercostal/phrenic nerves) is highly sensitive.

mcqs.subject: Physiology
mcqs.question: A boy with appendicitis has periumbilical pain that later shifts to the right iliac fossa with guarding. The localized right iliac fossa pain is due to what? [CKMC 25]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Early visceral pain (TIO, umbilicus) is referred,. later inflammation of the parietal peritoneum (somatic nerves T12/LI) gives sharp, localized pain at McBurney point.

mcqs.subject: Physiology
mcqs.question: A researcher measures conduction in f ibres carrying slow, burning pain. What is the conduction velocity of C fibres? [CKMC 25]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: C fibres: 0.4-2 m/s (unmyelinated, 0.5-2 ym). A6: 5-30 m/s. AF.. 30-70 m/s. Aa: 70-120 m/s.

mcqs.subject: Physiology
mcqs.question: A child pricks his finger on a thorn and pulls back immediately. Which fibres carry the fast pricking pain that triggers this. [WMC 25 . QIMS 25]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: A6 fibres (thinly myelinated, 6-30 m/s) carry fast. sharp, localized pain from mechanical/thermal nociceptors; glutamate at the dorsal horn (lamina I, v).

mcqs.subject: Physiology
mcqs.question: A student classifies skin receptors. How are pain receptors typically classified? [QIMS 25]

options.C: The same type as position~sense receptors

mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Nociceptors are free nerve endings (mechanical, thermal. chemical/polymodal): they adapt very little and can become sensitized (hyperalgesia).

mcqs.subject: Physiology
mcqs.question: A patient has sharp, well-localized pain at the incision immediately after surgery. Which fibre-transmitter combination mediates this acute pain. [KIMS 25]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Fast pain: AS 4 glutamate (milliseconds). Slow chronic pain: C 4 glutamate + substance P (seconds to minutes, builds up).

mcqs.subject: Physiology
mcqs.question: After a painful burn, even light touch on the area feels painful. What is this phenomenon called? [MUL 26]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Sensitization (hyperalgesia/allodynia): inflammatory mediators (bradykinin, PGS) lower nociceptor threshold (peripheral) and dorsal horn neurons become hyperexcitable (central, NMDA "wind-up").

mcqs.subject: Physiology
mcqs.question: A patient with a burn has poorly localized, burning, long-lasting pain hours after the injury. Which fibres transmit this pain. [HITEC 26]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: C fibres: unmyelinated, 0.5-2 m/s, slow/second pain (burning, aching), release glutamate + substance P, terminate in laminae11-111 (substantia gelatinosa).

mcqs.subject: Physiology
mcqs.question: A man feels his amputated hand is clenched and painful. What is pain perceived in an amputated limb called? [BWP 26]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Phantom limb pain occurs in up to 80% of amputees; mechanisms include cortical reorganization and stump neuromas; mirror therapy may help.

mcqs.subject: Physiology
mcqs.question: A man with myocardial infarction has pain radiating to the left shoulder and inner arm. What type of pain is this. [KIMS 26]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Referred pain." visceral and somatic afferents converge on the same dorsal horn neurons (TI-T5 for the heart,. dermatomes of the inner arm). Source had no options.

mcqs.subject: Physiology
mcqs.question: A 10-year-old boy cuts his finger and presses it to reduce the pain. Which afferent fibres mediate inhibition of pain by tactile stimulation? [CKMC 26. QIMS 25]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Gate control theory (Melzack-wall): AF touch afferents excite inhibitory interneurons in substantia gelatinosa (lamina 11) that block pain transmission; basis for rubbing and TENS.

mcqs.subject: Physiology
mcqs.question: A 44-year-old woman with spinal metastases is given low-dose epidural morphine. What is the cellular action of morphine on dorsal horn neurons. [KIMS 25]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: y-opioid (Gi/0) receptors: postsynaptic K. channel opening (hyperpolarization) + presynaptic Ca" channel closure ( I substance P/glutamate release).

mcqs.subject: Physiology
mcqs.question: A marathon runner feels little pain despite injury ("runner's high ). Which endogenous opioid is a major mediator of analgesia. [AMC 26. CKMC 26]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Endogenous opioids." F-endorphin (POMC, hypothalamus/pituitary), met- and leu-enkephalin (PAG, raphe, dorsal horn), dynorphin. Substance P is a pain transmitter.

mcqs.subject: Physiology
mcqs.question: Electrical stimulation of the periaqueductal grey produces profound analgesia in a patient with intractable pain. Which neurotransmitter mainly mediates this analgesia at the spinal level? [HITEC 26]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Analgesia system: PAG (enkephalin) ￿ nucleus raphe magnus (serotonin) ￿ dorsal horn enkephalinergic interneurons ￿ presynaptic inhibition of C/AS terminals (I substance P release).

mcqs.subject: Physiology
mcqs.question: A muscle is held stretched at a constant length while recording spindle afferents; firing stays high as long as the stretch lasts. Which receptor detects sustained muscle stretch? [AMC 26. AMC 25]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Static response (length): nuclear chain + static bag2 fibres, secondary (11) and primary (la) endings. Dynamic response (rate of stretch): nuclear bagl fibres, la endings only.

mcqs.subject: Physiology
mcqs.question: A physiologist records from a receptor in series with muscle fibres at the musculotendinous junction; it fires in proportion to the force of contraction. Which receptor detects muscle tension. [CKMC 25]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Golgi tendon organ: in series with extrafusal fibres, Ib afferents, signals tension (force) 4 autogenic inhibition. Spindle (in parallel) signals length. Key note: source keyed Ruffini endings.

mcqs.subject: Physiology
mcqs.question: During a voluntary contraction, the spindle continues to fire because intrafusal fibres shorten along with extrafusal fibres. What is this called? [CKMC 25]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Alpha-gamma co-activation keeps spindles taut during shortening so they can still signal length and damp unwanted variations (servo-assist).

mcqs.subject: Physiology
mcqs.question: A weightlifter tries to lift an excessive load; suddenly his biceps relaxes and he drops the weight. Which reflex is responsible. [KIMS 26. MUL 25. KIMS 25]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Excess tension ￿ GTO 4 Ib afferents ￿ inhibitory interneurons 4 autogenic inhibition of the same muscle (lengthening reaction), protecting tendon and muscle from tearing.

mcqs.subject: Physiology
mcqs.question: During stretching exercises at the gym, a man's hamstrings are suddenly lengthened. Which afferent fibres are activated first? [MUL 25]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Primary (annulospiral) endings 4 la fibres (fastest sensory, 70- 120 m/s) 4 monosynaptic stretch reflex. Secondary (flower-spray) ￿ type11 fibres.

mcqs.subject: Physiology
mcqs.question: A patient blindfolded can tell the position of his fingers. Position sense involves muscle spindles and which other receptors. [QIMS 25]

options.D: Deep receptors in joint capsules only

mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Guyton: position sense uses spindles (most important in mid-range), joint-capsule (Ruffini, Pacinian-like) receptors at extremes of angle, and skin tactile receptors.

mcqs.subject: Physiology
mcqs.question: A blindfolded patient can tell whether his knee is bent or straight. Which receptor provides the main proprioceptive information from the legs. [AMC 26]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Muscle spindles (with joint receptors) signal limb position and movement; conscious proprioception reaches cortex via the dorsal columns, unconscious via spinocerebellar tracts.

mcqs.subject: Physiology
mcqs.question: A physiologist asks which receptor most directly signals both limb position and muscle stretch. Which receptor is it? [CKMC 26]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Muscle spindle (intrafusal fibres, in parallel with extrafusal) ￿ length and rate of change of length; GTO (in series) 4 tension.

mcqs.subject: Physiology
mcqs.question: A physiologist records spindle afferents during a rapid stretch of muscle. Which afferents mainly transmit dynamic changes in muscle stretch? [HITEC 26]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Primary (la) endings respond to both length and RATE of change (dynamic response, from nuclear bagl fibres)," secondary (11) endings signal length only (static).

mcqs.subject: Physiology
mcqs.question: A physiology student asks how the Golgi tendon reflex relaxes a contracting muscle. What mediates the Golgi tendon reflex. [HITEC 26]

options.A: Inhibitory interneurons in the spinal cord

mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Ib afferents 4 inhibitory interneurons (disynaptic) 4 inhibit a-motor neurons of the same muscle (and excite antagonists) 4 autogenic inhibition.

mcqs.subject: Physiology
mcqs.question: A man steps on a nail and immediately withdraws his foot before feeling pain. Which reflex is this? [Prof 24. BWP 26]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Flexor (withdrawal/nociceptive) reflex." polysynaptic, triggered by pain receptors, flexes the limb away from the stimulus; begins -0.2-0.5 s after the stimulus in the opposite limb (crossed extensor).

mcqs.subject: Physiology
mcqs.question: When a man steps on a nail, the injured leg withdraws while the opposite leg extends to support his body. Which reflex explains this response of the opposite limb? [Prof 24]

options.A: Reciprocal inhibition in the same limb

mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Crossed extensor reflex: interneurons cross the cord 4 extensors of the opposite limb contract to support body weight. It has a long after-discharge (reverberating circuits).

mcqs.subject: Physiology
mcqs.question: A neurologist explains that corticospinal, rubrospinal and reflex inputs all act on the anterior horn cell to produce contraction. On which neurons do all motor pathways ultimately converge. [AMC 25]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Sherrington: the alpha motor neuron is the "final common path" Renshaw cells give recurrent inhibition," gamma neurons set spindle sensitivity.

mcqs.subject: Physiology
mcqs.question: A neurologist taps the patellar tendon to test the L3-L4 segments. Through which muscle is the knee jerk mediated? [BWP 25]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Knee jerk: patellar tendon 4 quadriceps spindles 4 la ￿ L3, L4 4 femoral nerve ￿ quadriceps contraction. Ankle jerk Sl; biceps C5-6.. triceps C7.

mcqs.subject: Physiology
mcqs.question: A man walks with alternate f lexion and extension of each leg; when flexors contract, extensors of the same joint relax. Which mechanism explains this. [BWP 25]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Reciprocal innervation: la afferents excite the agonist and, via inhibitory interneurons, inhibit the antagonist," underlies stepping and alternating movements.

mcqs.subject: Physiology
mcqs.question: A 13-year-old boy has flaccid legs with absent stretch and inverse stretch reflexes after a spinal injury. What is the most important role of motor neurons. [QIMS 25]

options.B: Prevent muscle from producing too much force
options.C: Stimulate skeletal muscle fibres to contract

mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Alpha motor neurons are the final common path to extrafusal fibres," loss 4 flaccid paralysis and areflexia. GTO prevents excess force; spindles detect length.

mcqs.subject: Physiology
mcqs.question: A woman with pyramidal tract disease has brisk knee jerks. When the patellar tendon is tapped, which event occurs. [QIMS 25]

options.A: Ib afferents from GTO increase f iring first
options.D: la afferents from muscle spindles increase their firing

mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Tap stretches the quadriceps 4 spindle la firing t 4 monosynaptic excitation of a-motor neurons. UMN lesions remove descending inhibition hyperreflexia.

mcqs.subject: Physiology
mcqs.question: A child with tetanus has spasms because a toxin blocks transmitter release from inhibitory interneurons in the anterior horn. Which transmitter do Renshaw cells release. [LHR 26]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Renshaw cells (excited by a-motor neuron collaterals via Ach) release glycine ￿ recurrent inhibition. Tetanus toxin blocks glycine/GABA release; strychnine blocks glycine receptors.

mcqs.subject: Physiology
mcqs.question: A stroke patient has increased tone in the arm that is greatest at the start of passive stretch and then suddenly gives way. Which sign of an upper motor neuron lesion is this? [Prof 25. BWP 25]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: UMN lesion: spasticity (clasp-knife - sudden release due to Golgi tendon organ inhibition), hyperreflexia, clonus, positive Babinski, minimal wasting. LMN: flaccidity, wasting. fasciculations, areflexia.

mcqs.subject: Physiology
mcqs.question: A man with a C5-C6 root avulsion has a weak, wasted biceps with an absent biceps jerk. What type of paralysis does a lower motor neuron lesion cause. [Prof 25. KIMS 25]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: LMN lesion = flaccid paralysis with hypotonia, early marked wasting, fasciculations, absent reflexes and a flexor (normal) plantar response.

mcqs.subject: Physiology
mcqs.question: A physiology student is told that pyramidal fibres act mainly on distal limb muscles. What is a primary action of the corticospinal tract? [AMC 25]

options.D: Excites flexor motor neurons for fine distal movements

mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Lateral corticospinal tract (crossed, 80-900A) mainly excites motor neurons of distal flexor muscles for skilled movements; it is facilitatory to flexors, while vestibulospinal and pontine reticulospinal favour extensors.

mcqs.subject: Physiology
mcqs.question: A man with motor neuron disease has a brisk jaw jerk and emotional lability. An exaggerated jaw-jerk indicates a lesion of which pathway. [CKMC 26. CKMC 25]

options.A: Bilateral corticobulbar (UMN) fibres to the trigeminal motor nucleus

mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Jaw jerk." afferent mesencephalic nucleus of V, efferent trigeminal motor nucleus (pons). Brisk jaw jerk = bilateral UMN lesion ABOVE the pons (pseudobulbar palsy). distinguishing it from cervical cord lesions.

mcqs.subject: Physiology
mcqs.question: A man with traumatic damage to the motor cortex has a positive Babinski sign. Which other finding is most consistent with this lesion? [KIMS 25]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: UMN lesion: spasticity ( t tone), hyperreflexia, clonus, extensor plantar. Acute cortical lesions may be initially flaccid (shock) before spasticity develops.

mcqs.subject: Physiology
mcqs.question: A 55-year-old man wakes up with weakness of his left arm and leg. Which corticospinal tract in his brain is most likely damaged? [KIMS 25]

options.C: Right lateral (fibres destined for the lateral CST)

mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Above the decussation, fibres for the left limbs run in the RIGHT hemisphere/brainstem; _85% cross to form the lateral CST supplying limb muscles.

mcqs.subject: Physiology
mcqs.question: A 65-year-old man has a unilateral internal capsule infarct. What does a typical unilateral cerebral stroke cause? [CKMC 26]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Internal capsule lesion 4 contralateral face, arm, leg (dense) hemiplegia because fibres are tightly packed; cortical lesions more often cause monoplegia (e.g. ACA 4 leg).

mcqs.subject: Physiology
mcqs.question: A man with motor neuron disease has spastic legs with brisk reflexes. Which is a characteristic feature of an upper motor neuron lesion? [CKMC 26]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: UMN: spasticity, hyperreflexia, clonus, Babinski sign. disuse atrophy only. LMN: flaccidity, areflexia. fasciculations, early marked atrophy.

mcqs.subject: Physiology
mcqs.question: A patient cannot imitate gestures or plan sequences of movements, though power is normal. Which area plans movements and contains mirror neurons for imitation. [MUL 26. KIMS 26]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Premotor cortex (lateral area 6) programs patterns of movement and contains mirror neurons," supplementary motor area (medial 6) plans bilateral and sequential movements," area 4 executes.

mcqs.subject: Physiology
mcqs.question: A neurologist explains which area finally drives the anterior horn cells for voluntary movement. Which area executes voluntary movement? [MUL 26]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Primary motor cortex (precentral gyrus) has the lowest threshold for evoking movement," somatotopic (motor homunculus) with large hand and face areas.

mcqs.subject: Physiology
mcqs.question: A small infarct injures corticospinal fibres in the medullary pyramid above the decussation. Which type of paralysis results. [HITEC 26]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Pyramid lesions above the decussation 4 contralateral weakness. Pure pyramidal lesions cause weakness with less spasticity (other descending tracts spared).

mcqs.subject: Physiology
mcqs.question: A student defines the types of motor neuron lesions. What does an upper motor neuron lesion involve. [BWP 26]

options.D: Motor pathways descending from the brain to the spinal cord/brainstem nuclei

mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: UMN = cortex, corona radiata. internal capsule, brainstem and spinal tracts above the anterior horn/cranial motor nuclei. LMN = anterior horn cell, root, plexus, peripheral nerve.

mcqs.subject: Physiology
mcqs.question: A patient has paralysis of the left limbs and weakness of the lower left face, with the forehead spared. Where is the lesion. [BWP 26]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: UMN facial weakness (lower face only, contralateral) + contralateral hemiplegia = lesion of the opposite cerebral hemisphere/internal capsule. BRAIN STEM

mcqs.subject: Physiology
mcqs.question: An unconscious man after a pontine haemorrhage has all four limbs extended and the arms internally rotated. What is this posture. [MUL 25]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Decerebrate (lesion between superior and inferior colliculi/upper pons): extension of all limbs unopposed vestibular and pontine reticular facilitation. Decorticate (above red nucleus): flexed arms, extended legs.

mcqs.subject: Physiology
mcqs.question: A man feels the upward and downward movement of a lift. Which receptor detects vertical linear acceleration of the head? [WMC 25]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Saccule macula is vertical 4 vertical linear acceleration (lift). Utricle macula is horizontal 4 horizontal linear acceleration and head tilt. Canals angular (rotational) acceleration.

mcqs.subject: Physiology
mcqs.question: A decerebrate cat shows severe extensor rigidity. The rigidity is abolished by cutting which structures. [BWP 25]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Decerebrate rigidity is mainly y-rigidity (excess gamma drive 4 spindle 4 la 4 alpha)," cutting dorsal roots removes the la loop and abolishes it. Key note: source keyed gamma efferents - also logical, but the classic answer is deafferentation (dorsal root section).

mcqs.subject: Physiology
mcqs.question: A 65-year-old man with a left lateral medullary lesion has loss of balance with a tendency to fall to the left. Which motor pathway is most likely affected? [KIMS 25]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Lateral vestibular (Deiters) nucleus ￿ uncrossed lateral vestibulospinal tract ￿ ipsilateral extensor (antigravity) tone and balance. Lesion ipsilateral postural instability.

mcqs.subject: Physiology
mcqs.question: A man with a cerebellopontine angle tumour has unilateral tinnitus and deafness with unsteadiness. What does damage to the vestibulocochlear nerve cause. [CKMC 26]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: CN Vlll has cochlear (hearing) and vestibular (balance) divisions; vestibular schwannoma presents with sensorineural deafness, tinnitus and imbalance.

mcqs.subject: Physiology
mcqs.question: A student draws the cross-section of the cochlea. Which compartment contains the organ of Corti. [MUL 26]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Scala media (endolymph, high K,) rests on the basilar membrane carrying the organ of Corti; scala vestibuli and tympani contain perilymph and communicate at the helicotrema.

mcqs.subject: Physiology
mcqs.question: An elderly man exposed to loud machinery has progressive hearing loss; Weber test lateralizes to the better ear and Rinne is positive bilaterally. What type of hearing loss is this? [MUL 26]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Noise damages outer hair cells (4 kHz notch) 4 SNHL: Weber to the good ear, Rinne positive (AC > BC). Conductive: Weber to the bad ear, Rinne negative.

mcqs.subject: Physiology
