mcqs.question: Light is shone into a patient's right eye during examination. Which muscle contracts in response? [MUL 26]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Direct and consensual light reflex: pretectal nuclei project bilaterally to EW nuclei ￿ both sphincter pupillae contract.

mcqs.subject: Physiology
mcqs.question: A man feels dizzy when spun on a rotating chair. Which receptors detect angular acceleration of the head? [WMC 26]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Cristae (with gelatinous cupula) in the ampullae respond to rotational acceleration by endolymph inertia; maculae (otoliths) respond to linear acceleration and gravity (head tilt).

mcqs.subject: Physiology
mcqs.question: A pilot misjudges head tilt during acceleration. Which receptors detect linear acceleration and head tilt? [WMC 26]

options.B: Maculae of utricle and saccule (otolith organs)

mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Otoliths (CaCO3 Crystals) on the otolithic membrane bend hair-cell stereocilia when the head tilts or accelerates linearly," displaced otoconia cause BPPV.

mcqs.subject: Physiology
mcqs.question: A vestibular physiologist rotates a subject's head rapidly. Which movement produces maximal excitation of hair cells in the right horizontal semicircular canal? [HITEC 26]

options.A: Rapid rotation of the head to the right
options.D: Rapid rotation of the head to the left

mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Turning the head to the right moves endolymph (by inertia) toward the right utricle (ampullopetal) ￿ excites the right horizontal canal and inhibits the left. Elevators stimulate the saccule. Source gave no key.

mcqs.subject: Physiology
mcqs.question: A physiologist lesions the medullary reticular formation in an experimental animal. Which finding may result? [HITEC 26]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Medullary reticulospinal system inhibits antigravity muscles (facilitated by cortex/basal ganglia); pontine RF excites them. Losing medullary inhibition 4 extensor hypertonia. Source gave no key.

mcqs.subject: Physiology
mcqs.question: A man after a severe brainstem haemorrhage has all limbs extended. Where is the lesion that causes decerebrate posturing. [BWP 26]

options.B: At or below the red nucleus, in the brainstem (above vestibular nuclei)

mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Decorticate (flexor) posture: lesion above the red nucleus (rubrospinal flexor drive preserved). Decerebrate (extensor): lesion between red and vestibular nuclei. Decerebrate has worse prognosis.

mcqs.subject: Physiology
mcqs.question: A 50-year-old man with a cerebellar tumour cannot perform rapid alternating pronation and supination of the forearm. Which sign is positive? [Prof 24. CKMC 26. KIMS 26. LHR 25. CKMC 25. MUL 25]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Dysdiadochokinesia = inability to perform rapid alternating movements (cerebellar hemisphere lesion, ipsilateral). Dysmetria = past-pointing; both reflect loss of predictive timing by the cerebellum.

mcqs.subject: Physiology
mcqs.question: A 60-year-old man has a tremor that appears only when he reaches for a cup and worsens as his hand approaches it. Which disease causes this intention tremor. [Prof 24]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Intention (action) tremor = cerebellar lesion (dentate/cerebrocerebellum), lost "damping" Parkinsonian tremor is a resting pill-rolling" tremor that disappears on movement.

mcqs.subject: Physiology
mcqs.question: A man with a cerebellar lesion overshoots when reaching for objects and cannot judge how far or fast to move. Which structure controls the range, rate and timing of movement? [CKMC 26. CKMC 25]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: The cerebellum compares intended and actual movement (comparator function) and sets the onset of antagonist "braking" controlling range, rate, force and timing. Lesion ￿ dysmetria, past-pointing.

mcqs.subject: Physiology
mcqs.question: A neuroscientist notes that only one type of cerebellar cortical neuron uses glutamate. Which cells of the cerebellar cortex are excitatory. [MUL 25]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Granule cells (glutamate) are the only excitatory cerebellar cortical neurons; their axons form parallel fibres. Purkinje (sole output), basket, stellate and Golgi cells are GABAergic inhibitory.

mcqs.subject: Physiology
mcqs.question: A 45-year-old alcoholic performs the finger-nose test: his f inger overshoots and oscillates more as it nears the target. What does this show? [MUL 25]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Cerebellar signs (DANISH): Dysdiadochokinesia. Ataxia, Nystagmus. Intention tremor, Slurred (scanning) speech, Hypotonia. Dysmetria = past-pointing from lost predictive braking.

mcqs.subject: Physiology
mcqs.question: In a monkey experiment, the animal learns to adjust a motor response to a changing load; learning fails after a specific lesion. Which brain area is essential for this motor learning. [WMC 25]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Climbing fibres (inferior olive) signal errors and modify parallel-fibre-Purkinje synapses (LTD) 4 motor learning and adaptation (e.g. VOR adaptation).

mcqs.subject: Physiology
mcqs.question: A child has vertigo, nausea, vomiting and nystagmus; limb coordination tests are normal. MRI shows a midline tumour of the caudal cerebellum. Which part of the cerebellum is involved? [WMC 25]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Flocculonodular lobe ￿ vestibular nuclei: equilibrium and eye movements. Lesion 4 nystagmus, vertigo, truncal ataxia with normal limb coordination. Source stem said "normal gait"; limb coordination is the spared function.

mcqs.subject: Physiology
mcqs.question: A 50-year-old man has a tremor that worsens as his finger approaches his nose. Lesion of which division of the cerebellum causes intention tremor? [KIMS 26. BWP 25]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Intention tremor = failure of damping in the dentate-thalamic loop (cerebrocerebellum, superior peduncle). Key note: source keyed spinocerebellum.

mcqs.subject: Physiology
mcqs.question: A student compares the roles of motor structures in planning and executing complex patterns of movement. Which structure is most important for smooth, coordinated complex patterns of movement? [QIMS 25]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: The cerebellum (with cortex) sequences and times complex multi-joint movements; basal ganglia (putamen circuit) execute learned patterns, caudate circuit cognitively plans sequences.

mcqs.subject: Physiology
mcqs.question: A 55-year-old woman has a drunken gait and jerky movements that worsen as her limb approaches a target. Which neuronal network is most likely affected? [KIMS 25]

options.A: Corticospinal tract and basal ganglia neurons
options.C: Climbing f ibres and Purkinje cells
options.D: Mossy fibres and cortical pyramidal cells

mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Climbing fibres (inferior olive) produce complex spikes in Purkinje cells, providing error signals for correction; Purkinje output via deep nuclei damps and corrects movement.

mcqs.subject: Physiology
mcqs.question: A 60-year-old man with an unsteady gait has a lesion of the flocculonodular lobe. Which function is impaired? [KIMS 25]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Vestibulocerebellum uses vestibular input to control equilibrium, axial posture and eye movements (VOR). Spinocerebellum." proprioceptive limb coordination,. cerebrocerebellum." planning.

mcqs.subject: Physiology
mcqs.question: A 45-year-old sportsman cannot perform rapid alternating movements. Which physiological function is impaired? [KIMS 25]

options.B: Coordination and timing of muscle activity
options.C: Integration of motor and sensory signals in spinal cord

mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Dysdiadochokinesia reflects failure of the cerebellum to time the switch between agonist and antagonist (loss of predictive turn-off" signals).

mcqs.subject: Physiology
mcqs.question: A patient can initiate movement but has lost smooth, fine control of distal limb movements. Which structure is most likely affected? [AMC 26]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Intermediate (paravermal) spinocerebellum ￿ interposed nuclei ￿ red nucleus and motor cortex: corrects ongoing distal limb movements using proprioceptive feedback.

mcqs.subject: Physiology
mcqs.question: A student summarizes cerebellar function for a viva. What is a major function of the cerebellum? [AMC 26]

options.D: Real-time correction and coordination of movement

mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: The cerebellum compares intended (corticopontine) and actual (spinocerebellar) movement and sends corrections - it does not initiate movement,. lesions cause no paralysis.

mcqs.subject: Physiology
mcqs.question: A patient with a cerebellar tumour has frequent falls. Which finding best explains the falls. [HITEC 26]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Gait/truncal ataxia (vermis, flocculonodular lobe) causes falls; DDK and past-pointing are limb signs that do not themselves cause falls. Source gave no key.

mcqs.subject: Physiology
mcqs.question: During the finger-to-nose test, a patient consistently overshoots and touches his ear. What is the defect? [BWP 26]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Dysmetria (hypermetria = overshoot) - cerebellum fails to predict and initiate the braking (antagonist) contraction in time.

mcqs.subject: Physiology
mcqs.question: A 45-year-old man has choreiform movements and progressive memory loss and personality change. Which statement about Huntington chorea is correct? [QIMS 25]

options.C: Severe dementia accompanies the motor dysfunction

mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Huntington: AD, CAG repeats, loss of striatal GABA neurons 4 chorea + dementia + psychiatric change, onset 30-50 years. Copper deposition = Wilson disease.

mcqs.subject: Physiology
mcqs.question: A pianist executes a well-rehearsed piece "automatically" without thinking of individual movements. Which circuit executes learned patterns of movement? [QIMS 25]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Guyton: putamen circuit (premotor/sensory cortex 4 putamen 4 GPI 4 VA/VL 4 motor cortex) executes learned patterns (writing. cutting paper); caudate circuit provides cognitive control of sequences.

mcqs.subject: Physiology
mcqs.question: A 45-year-old woman has involuntary jerky movements of her limbs (hyperkinetic disorder). What best explains its pathophysiology. [KIMS 25]

options.C: Hypoactivity of thalamus from excess inhibition
options.D: Degeneration of the putamen-globus pallidus (indirect pathway) axis

mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Hyperkinetic (Huntington): loss of striatal indirect-pathway neurons 4 GPe disinhibited 4 STN inhibited ￿ l GPI output 4 thalamus disinhibited excess movement. Hypokinetic (Parkinson): the reverse.

mcqs.subject: Physiology
mcqs.question: A 63-year-old woman suddenly develops violent f linging movements of the left arm and leg f rom an infarct of the right subthalamic nucleus. What is the effect on the basal ganglia circuit? [KIMS 25]

options.A: Decreased excitatory input from STN to GPI
options.C: Increased inhibitory output from GPI to thalamus
options.D: Enhanced GABAergic input from GPe to STN

mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: STN (glutamate) normally excites GPI," its loss reduces GPI inhibition of VA/VL thalamus ￿ excessive thalamocortical drive 4 contralateral ballism.

mcqs.subject: Physiology
mcqs.question: A child with cerebral palsy has slow, writhing movements of the hands. Athetosis is classically associated with dysfunction of which structure. [CKMC 26. KIMS 26]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Guyton: athetosis - globus pallidus/putamen lesions; hemiballismus - STN; chorea - caudate/putamen; Parkinson - SN. Kernicterus damages the globus pallidus 4 athetoid CP.

mcqs.subject: Physiology
mcqs.question: A 70-year-old man has rigidity, bradykinesia, postural instability and a resting tremor. What is the most likely diagnosis. [MUL 26]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: TRAP = Tremor at rest, Rigidity (cogwheel/lead-pipe). Akinesia/bradykinesia, Postural instability. Essential tremor is postural/action tremor improved by alcohol.

mcqs.subject: Physiology
mcqs.question: A patient develops severe involuntary choreiform movements, later behavioural change and aggression; his father had a similar illness. Damage to which structure is most characteristic. [HITEC 26]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Huntington disease = striatal (caudate > putamen) degeneration. Source said "flinging" (ballism, STN), but the familial course with behavioural change fits Huntington.

mcqs.subject: Physiology
mcqs.question: A 68-year-old man has a 4-6 Hz tremor of the hand at rest that disappears when he reaches for objects. Which tremor is classically seen in Parkinson disease. [HITEC 26]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Parkinsonian tremor: resting, 4-6 Hz. pill-rolling. often asymmetric, reduced by movement and sleep, worse with stress. Intention tremor = cerebellar.

mcqs.subject: Physiology
mcqs.question: A neurologist flexes and extends a patient's wrist and feels a ratchet-like resistance. Which feature is characteristic of Parkinson disease? [BWP 26]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Parkinsonian rigidity." lead-pipe (uniform throughout movement) or cogwheel (tremor superimposed); reflexes normal. Spasticity (UMN) is velocity-dependent clasp-knife.

mcqs.subject: Physiology
mcqs.question: A 65-year-old man has uniform resistance throughout the range of passive elbow movement. Lead-pipe rigidity is classically seen in which disease. [BWP 26]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Lead-pipe rigidity (also in neuroleptic malignant syndrome) results from increased tonic stretch reflexes; equal in flexors and extensors, unlike spasticity.

mcqs.subject: Physiology
mcqs.question: A child has slow, writhing, flicking movements of the fingers and hands. Which movement disorder is this. [BWP 26]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Athetosis: slow, continuous, writhing distal movements (globus pallidus/putamen, kernicterus)," chorea." brief, rapid, dance-like; ballismus: violent proximal flinging (STN).

mcqs.subject: Physiology
mcqs.question: A 66-year-old man with Parkinson disease has great difficulty starting to walk and very slow movements. What is the mechanism of akinesia in Parkinson disease. [HITEC 26]

options.A: Destruction of the cerebellar dentate nucleus
options.B: Loss of nigrostriatal dopamine 4 excess GPI inhibition of the motor thalamus

mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Stem created: the source recall was incomplete (HITEC 26 Physiology QIO). Dopamine loss reduces the direct pathway (DI) and disinhibits the indirect pathway (D2) 4 GPi/SNr overactive ￿ thalamocortical drive l 4 bradykinesia; DBS of STN/GPi reduces it.

mcqs.subject: Physiology
mcqs.question: A 25-year-old man has a generalized tonic-clonic seizure. An hour later he is drowsy, confused and depressed. In which type of epilepsy does this postictal depression occur? [Prof 24. CKMC 26 . MUL 26]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Grand mal: tonic then clonic phase, followed by postictal depression (stupor, fatigue) lasting minutes to a day. Absence: 3/s spike-and-wave, no postictal state.

mcqs.subject: Physiology
mcqs.question: An EEG is recorded during a seizure in a patient with grand mal epilepsy. What does it show. [Prof 24]

options.C: High-voltage synchronous discharges over the entire cortex

mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Grand mal: high-voltage, high-frequency synchronous discharges over the whole cortex. Petit mal (absence): 3 Hz spike-and-dome. Psychomotor (temporal lobe): low-frequency rectangular waves 2-4/s.

mcqs.subject: Physiology
mcqs.question: The parents of a 5-year-old boy report that he walks and utters words during sleep but does not remember it in the morning. In which stage of sleep does this occur. [Prof 24]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Sleepwalking, sleep-talking, night terrors and bed-wetting occur in NREM stage 3 (slow-wave, delta) sleep. Nightmares and vivid recalled dreams occur in REM sleep.

mcqs.subject: Physiology
mcqs.question: After a head injury, a man cannot recall events from before the accident, although he forms new memories normally. Lesions of which structure are classically associated with retrograde amnesia. [Prof 24]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Guyton: lesions of the thalamus (dorsomedial) can cause retrograde amnesia, as the thalamus helps "search" memory stores. Hippocampal (medial temporal) lesions cause anterograde amnesia.

mcqs.subject: Physiology
mcqs.question: A man wakes up frightened from vivid nightmares that he remembers in detail. In which type of sleep do nightmares occur. [Prof 24]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: REM (paradoxical) sleep: vivid recalled dreams, rapid eye movements, muscle atonia. irregular HR/RR. beta-like EEG. Night terrors (not remembered) occur in slow-wave sleep.

mcqs.subject: Physiology
mcqs.question: A neuropathologist sees a white stripe (line of Gennari) in the cortex along the calcarine sulcus. The primary visual cortex is thick because of increased fibres in which layer. [AMC 25]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Area 17 (striate cortex): greatly expanded layer IV (internal granular) receiving geniculocalcarine fibres; stria of Gennari = myelinated fibres in layer IVB.

mcqs.subject: Physiology
mcqs.question: A sleep study shows rapid eye movements, a desynchronized EEG and absent chin EMG activity. What characterizes REM sleep? [AMC 25]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: REM: atonia (except eyes and respiratory muscles), active brain (beta-like EEG, t metabolism), vivid dreams, irregular HR and BP, penile erection; ~25% of adult sleep, recurs every 90 min.

mcqs.subject: Physiology
mcqs.question: A patient with bilateral hippocampal damage after cardiac arrest cannot form new long-term memories. What is the main function of the hippocampus. [CKMC 25]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Hippocampus converts short-term into long-term declarative memory (consolidation, LTP),. bilateral lesion ￿ anterograde amnesia (H.M.). Procedural memory remains intact.

mcqs.subject: Physiology
mcqs.question: A man has episodes of a strange burning smell followed by lip-smacking and impaired awareness, without falling. Which type of seizure is this. [CKMC 25. BWP 25]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Uncinate (temporal lobe) fits: olfactory/gustatory aura (uncus), automatisms, impaired consciousness, deja vu. EEG.. low-frequency rectangular waves.

mcqs.subject: Physiology
mcqs.question: A sleep study records high-amplitude 0.5-3 Hz waves during deep sleep. Which waves are associated with deep sleep. [CKMC 25]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Beta (>14 Hz) = alert; alpha (8- 13 Hz) = relaxed, eyes closed (occipital); theta (4-7 Hz) = drowsy/children; delta (<3.5 Hz) = deep slow-wave sleep, infancy, organic brain disease, anaesthesia.

mcqs.subject: Physiology
mcqs.question: A neurologist stimulates the postcentral gyrus and notes that a very large area represents one body region. Which region has the largest representation on the sensory homunculus. [MUL 25]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Cortical representation is proportional to receptor density: lips, face, tongue and thumb/fingers occupy most of area 3, 1,2; trunk and leg occupy small areas (leg on the medial surface).

mcqs.subject: Physiology
mcqs.question: During the first minutes of sleep, the EEG shows slowing from alpha to low-voltage 4-7 Hz waves. Which waves are seen in early (stage l) non-REM sleep. [MUL 25]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Stage Nl: theta; N2: sleep spindles (12-14 Hz) and K complexes: N3: delta (slow-wave). REM: low-voltage mixed (beta-like) "sawtooth" waves.

mcqs.subject: Physiology
mcqs.question: During deep general anaesthesia, the anaesthetist monitors the EEG. Which waves predominate. [WMC 25]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Delta waves (<3.5 Hz, high amplitude) appear in deep sleep, deep anaesthesia, infancy and organic brain disease; they persist in the cortex even after cortex is isolated from the thalamus.

mcqs.subject: Physiology
mcqs.question: After a head injury, a footballer cannot recall the match or the week before it, but remembers everything after waking in hospital. What type of amnesia is this. [WMC 25]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Retrograde: loss of memories formed BEFORE the injury (recent ones most affected). Anterograde: inability to form new memories after the event (hippocampal damage).

mcqs.subject: Physiology
mcqs.question: Guyton describes the thalamus as part of the memory system. What is the role of the thalamus in memory. [BWP 25]

options.C: Searching and retrieval of stored memories

mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Guyton: thalamic lesions cause retrograde amnesia because the thalamus "searches the memory storehouses and reads out memories" The hippocampus provides codification (short 4 long term). Key note: source keyed codification.

mcqs.subject: Physiology
mcqs.question: A patient with damage to the primary somatosensory cortex can feel pain but cannot judge shape, texture or weight of objects. What does damage to the somatosensory cortex cause? [QIMS 25]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: After S-I lesions, pain and temperature remain crudely perceived (thalamus), but discrimination. localization, two-point discrimination and stereognosis are lost. Amorphosynthesis = parietal association lesion.

mcqs.subject: Physiology
mcqs.question: A woman has zig-zag lights in her vision for 20 minutes, followed by a throbbing unilateral headache with nausea. What is believed to cause the aura (Guyton)? IQIMS 25]

options.C: Vasospasm causing ischaemia of the relevant cortex
options.D: Increased blood flow to sensory cortex

mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Classic vascular theory: prodromal vasospasm 4 cortical ischaemia (aura), then reactive vasodilation with stretch of arterial walls 4 headache. Current view: cortical spreading depression + trigeminovascular activation.

mcqs.subject: Physiology
mcqs.question: A man with chronic back pain cannot sleep and is prescribed a benzodiazepine. Why can he not sleep without medication. IQIMS 25]

options.B: Excitation of the reticular activating system by pain

mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Pain signals (paleospinothalamic) strongly excite the reticular activating system, keeping the cortex awake," benzodiazepines (GABA-A) depress it. Key note: source keyed depression of RF (the drug's action, not the cause of insomnia).

mcqs.subject: Physiology
mcqs.question: A 15-year-old girl with epilepsy undergoes EEG with provocation tests. Which condition produces the greatest increase in brain activity. IQIMS 25]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Activation procedures: hyperventilation (alkalosis) + photic stimulation are combined to provoke epileptiform discharges.

mcqs.subject: Physiology
mcqs.question: After a concussion, a 16-year-old understands and repeats speech but has difficulty reading, writing, spelling and naming. Which area is most likely affected? [KIMS 25]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Angular gyrus (area 39, dominant inferior parietal lobule) links visual word forms to language: lesion 4 alexia with agraphia, anomia; Gerstmann syndrome (finger agnosia, acalculia, R-L confusion, agraphia).

mcqs.subject: Physiology
mcqs.question: A 20-year-old student wakes unrefreshed; polysomnography shows reduced delta (slow-wave) activity. Which consequence is most likely. [KIMS 25]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Slow-wave sleep is restorative ( t GH secretion. I metabolism) and supports consolidation of declarative memory; REM supports procedural/emotional memory.

mcqs.subject: Physiology
mcqs.question: A 65-year-old has intact immediate recall but impaired delayed recall and recognition; he misplaces items frequently. Which structure is most likely affected? [KIMS 25]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Immediate (working) memory depends on prefrontal cortex,. transfer to long-term memory (delayed recall) depends on the hippocampus - the earliest site of Alzheimer pathology.

mcqs.subject: Physiology
mcqs.question: A 55-year-old alcoholic has anterograde amnesia and confabulation; MRI shows damage to the mammillary bodies and medial thalamus. Which type of memory is most impaired? [KIMS 25]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Korsakoff syndrome (thiamine deficiency) damages the Papez circuit 4 loss of episodic memory for recent events, confabulation," procedural memory preserved.

mcqs.subject: Physiology
mcqs.question: A man with bilateral hippocampal damage after head injury cannot recall recent events. Which finding is expected on neuropsychological testing. [KIMS 25]

options.A: Intact procedural memory but impaired episodic memory
options.B: Impaired working but intact procedural memory
options.C: Impaired semantic but intact working memory
options.D: Impaired procedural but intact episodic memory

mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Hippocampus." explicit (declarative) memory. Procedural (skills) memory." cerebellum, basal ganglia - preserved in amnesics (e.g. patient H.M. learnt mirror drawing).

mcqs.subject: Physiology
mcqs.question: A violinist with Alzheimer disease forgets recent events but still plays well. Playing a musical instrument is an example of which type of memory. [AMC 26]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Procedural (implicit, skill) memory depends on basal ganglia, cerebellum and motor cortex, not on the hippocampus.

mcqs.subject: Physiology
mcqs.question: A 7-year-old girl has brief staring spells many times a day; EEG shows 3-Hz spike-and-wave discharges. Which seizure type is this. [AMC 26. HITEC 26]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Absence (petit mal): thalamocortical T-type Ca" channel oscillation," 5- 15 s lapses, no postictal state, provoked by hyperventilation; treat with ethosuximide or valproate.

mcqs.subject: Physiology
mcqs.question: A neurosurgeon stimulates a gyrus and the awake patient reports tingling in the opposite hand. In which gyrus is the primary somatosensory cortex. [CKMC 26]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Postcentral gyrus = areas 3, 1, 2 (S-l)," S-11 lies in the wall of the lateral sulcus. Precentral gyrus = primary motor cortex (area 4).

mcqs.subject: Physiology
mcqs.question: A patient cannot form new memories after bilateral medial temporal lobe resection. Which structure is most likely damaged? [CKMC 26. HITEC 26]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Bilateral hippocampal loss (H.M., hypoxia, HSV) 4 profound anterograde amnesia for declarative memory: old memories and skills are preserved.

mcqs.subject: Physiology
mcqs.question: An ophthalmology student traces the path of light through the retina. Through which layers does light pass before reaching the photoreceptors. [MUL 26]

options.A: Outer nuclear and photoreceptor layers only
options.C: Inner retinal layers (nerve fibre, ganglion cell, plexiform, nuclear)

mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: The retina is "inverted": light crosses the nerve fibre, ganglion, inner plexiform, inner nuclear, outer plexiform and outer nuclear layers before reaching rods/cones; at the fovea these are displaced.

mcqs.subject: Physiology
mcqs.question: A physiologist studies rod responses to a flash of light. What happens to CGMP and cGMP-gated Na. channels during phototransduction. [MUL 26]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Light ￿ rhodopsin ￿ transducin 4 phosphodiesterase I CGMP ￿ Na. channels close ￿ hyperpolarization ￿ less glutamate release. In darkness the "dark current" keeps rods depolarized.

mcqs.subject: Physiology
mcqs.question: A student writes the visual pathway for an exam. Which is the correct sequence from retina to cortex. [MUL 26]

options.A: Retina 4 Optic nerve 4 chiasma 4 Optic tract 4 LGB 4 Optic radiation
options.B: Retina 4 Optic nerve 4 MGB 4 Optic radiation 4 cortex area 17
options.C: Retina 4 Optic tract 4 Optic nerve ￿ chiasma 4 superior colliculus
options.D: Retina 4 chiasma ￿ Optic nerve 4 LGB 4 cortex cortex

mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Lesions." optic nerve 4 monocular blindness; chiasma 4 bitemporal hemianopia; tract/radiation ￿ contralateral homonymous hemianopia; Meyer loop ￿ superior quadrantanopia.

mcqs.subject: Physiology
mcqs.question: A man cannot distinguish red from green. Which photoreceptors are responsible for colour vision. [WMC 26]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Three cone types (S-blue, M-green, L-red) mediate photopic colour vision and acuity at the fovea; rods (rhodopsin) mediate scotopic night vision. Red-green colour blindness is X-linked.

mcqs.subject: Physiology
mcqs.question: Polysomnography shows low-amplitude high-frequency EEG, rapid eye movements and marked skeletal muscle atonia. Which sleep stage is this. [HITEC 26]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: REM sleep ("paradoxical"): EEG resembles wakefulness, atonia (pontine inhibition of motor neurons via medullary RF), PGO waves," REM behaviour disorder = loss of atonia (early synucleinopathy).

mcqs.subject: Physiology
mcqs.question: A schoolgirl has brief spells of staring with loss of awareness but no convulsions or falls. Which seizure type causes unconsciousness without convulsions. [BWP 26]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Absence." sudden 5-20 s loss of awareness, eyelid fluttering, immediate recovery; 3-Hz spike-and-wave; begins in childhood.

mcqs.subject: Physiology
mcqs.question: A man has jerking of his left hand that spreads up the arm (Jacksonian march) without loss of consciousness. What characterizes focal epilepsy. [BWP 26]

options.B: Seizure activity beginning in a localized area of one hemisphere

mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Focal (partial) seizures arise from a localized cortical focus (scar, tumour); symptoms reflect the area (motor, sensory, psychic); may secondarily generalize.

mcqs.subject: Physiology
mcqs.question: A labourer works in a hot, very humid environment and develops heat exhaustion despite profuse sweating. Which heat-loss mechanism is least effective in hot humid air? [AMC 25]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Evaporation depends on the vapour-pressure gradient: in humid air sweat drips off without evaporating. When air temperature exceeds skin temperature, radiation and conduction add heat. Key note: source keyed decreased BMR.

mcqs.subject: Physiology
mcqs.question: A girl with a hypothalamic lesion develops obesity and delayed puberty. Which hypothalamic nucleus controls both feeding and reproduction (GnRH, POMC/NPY neurons)? [AMC 25]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Arcuate nucleus: NPY/AgRP (orexigenic) and POMC/CART (anorexigenic) neurons respond to leptin; also releases GnRH, dopamine (PIH) and GHRH into the portal system.

mcqs.subject: Physiology
mcqs.question: A woman develops hyperphagia and obesity after a hypothalamic tumour. In which nucleus is the satiety centre located? [CKMC 25]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Ventromedial nucleus = satiety centre (lesion 4 hyperphagia, obesity, rage). Lateral hypothalamus = feeding (hunger) centre (lesion 4 aphagia. starvation). Key note: source keyed dorsomedial.

mcqs.subject: Physiology
mcqs.question: A man after pituitary surgery passes 8 L of dilute urine daily. Which hypothalamic nucleus mainly regulates plasma osmolality through ADH? [CKMC 25]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Osmoreceptors (OVLT/anterior hypothalamus) drive the supraoptic (mainlyADH) and paraventricular (mainly oxytocin) magnocellular neurons posterior pituitary. Lesion 4 central diabetes insipidus.

mcqs.subject: Physiology
mcqs.question: A rat with bilateral lesions of a hypothalamic area refuses food and water and starves to death. Which nucleus is the feeding (appetite) centre. [MUL 26. HITEC 26. MUL 25]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Lateral hypothalamus = hunger/feeding centre (orexin, MCH); lesion ￿ aphagia, adipsia. Ventromedial = satiety; lesion ￿ hyperphagia, obesity.

mcqs.subject: Physiology
mcqs.question: A labourer collapses unconscious in the summer sun with a body temperature of 42°C and hot, dry skin. What is the cause. [MUL 25]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Heat stroke: core temperature >40.5 °C. absent sweating. CNS dysfunction - hypothalamic thermoregulation fails. Heat exhaustion: profuse sweating, salt/water depletion, normal mental state.

mcqs.subject: Physiology
mcqs.question: A man exposed to severe cold starts shivering and his skin vessels constrict. Which hypothalamic area controls heat production and conservation. [WMC 25]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Posterior hypothalamus (dorsomedial part) = primary motor centre for shivering and sympathetic vasoconstriction, piloerection and thyroid stimulation. Anterior/preoptic = heat loss.

mcqs.subject: Physiology
mcqs.question: A hypothalamic lesion disturbs both body temperature and water balance. Which nuclei regulate temperature and water osmolality respectively. [WMC 25]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Preoptic area: thermostat (warm-sensitive neurons). Supraoptic: ADH for osmolality. OVLT osmoreceptors drive thirst and ADH.

mcqs.subject: Physiology
mcqs.question: A neurology resident sees damage to the VPL nucleus on CT. Which function is chiefly affected? [KIMS 25]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: VPL relays medial lemniscus and spinothalamic input from the body to S-I," VL/VA relay motor (cerebellum/basal ganglia)," anterior/dorsomedial relay limbic.

mcqs.subject: Physiology
mcqs.question: A student summarizes the role of the thalamus. What is its primary function. [CKMC 26. KIMS 25]

options.D: Relaying sensory (and motor) information to the cortex

mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Thalamus = "gateway to the cortex": all sensory pathways except olfaction relay here (VPL. VPM, LGB, MGB): motor relays VA/VL; limbic anterior/DM," it also regulates arousal (intralaminar).

mcqs.subject: Physiology
mcqs.question: A 28-year-old man with an acute infection has a core temperature of 39°C, felt chills earlier and is now sweating. What is the cause of the raised temperature. [KIMS 25]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Pyrogens (IL-I, IL-6, TNF) 4 PGE2 in the preoptic area (OVLT) 4 set point t 4 shivering and vasoconstriction until body temperature reaches it (chills); antipyretics block COX.

mcqs.subject: Physiology
mcqs.question: A woman develops diabetes insipidus after hypothalamic surgery, though her posterior pituitary is intact. Where are ADH and oxytocin synthesized? [CKMC 26]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: ADH and oxytocin are made in hypothalamic magnocellular neurons and only stored/released in the posterior pituitary (neurohypophysis).

mcqs.subject: Physiology
mcqs.question: A man with a hypothalamic lesion never feels thirsty and develops hypernatraemia. Where is the thirst centre located? [CKMC 26]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Thirst: OVLT and subfornical organ (lack BBB, sense osmolality and angiotensin11) ￿ lateral preoptic hypothalamus. Thirst is stimulated by t osmolality (1-2%), I volume and dry mouth.

mcqs.subject: Physiology
mcqs.question: A student lists sensory pathways and their thalamic relays. Which sensory pathway reaches the cerebral cortex without first relaying in the thalamus? [CKMC 26]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Olfactory tract 4 piriform cortex, amygdala, entorhinal cortex directly; thalamic (dorsomedial) relay is secondary. Taste relays in VPM, vision in LGB, hearing in MGB.

mcqs.subject: Physiology
mcqs.question: A patient has degenerative changes in the ventral posterior nucleus of the thalamus and loses position sense on one side. Which deficit may result? [MUL 26]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Loss of proprioceptive relay (VPL) 4 contralateral sensory ataxia (pseudoathetosis); VL lesions (cerebellar relay) also cause contralateral ataxia.

mcqs.subject: Physiology
mcqs.question: A student traces the olfactory pathway to the orbitofrontal cortex. Which thalamic nucleus relays olfactory information toward the orbitofrontal cortex. [MUL 26]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Olfactory cortex 4 mediodorsal thalamus 4 orbitofrontal cortex (conscious discrimination of odours); direct path to cortex also exists without thalamic relay.

mcqs.subject: Physiology
mcqs.question: A child with tonsillitis develops a fever. Which substance acts directly in the hypothalamus to raise the temperature set point? [HITEC 26]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Endogenous pyrogens (IL-I, IL-6, TNF-a) induce COX-2 in OVLT endothelium ￿ PGE2 4 EP3 receptors on preoptic neurons 4 set point t. Aspirin/paracetamol block PGE2 synthesis.

mcqs.subject: Physiology
mcqs.question: A patient has retrograde amnesia attributed to thalamic damage. Which function is a principal role of the thalamus? [BWP 26]

options.B: Initiation of voluntary movement at lower motor neurons
options.C: Regulation of muscle tone at the neuromuscular junction
options.D: Relay of sensory information to the cerebral cortex

mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Besides relaying sensation (and motor loops), the thalamus helps retrieve memories; thalamic lesions can produce retrograde amnesia. Source stem was incomplete.

mcqs.subject: Physiology
mcqs.question: A patient has lost the whole somatosensory cortex on one side but still crudely perceives painful stimuli on the opposite side. Which sensation can be perceived at the thalamic level without the cortex. [BWP 26]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Stem created: the source recall was incomplete (thalamus stimulation/fMRI question had no options). Guyton: pain is perceived crudely at the thalamus and reticular formation,. the cortex is needed for localization and discrimination.

mcqs.subject: Physiology
mcqs.question: A 55-year-old man with a chronic subdural haematoma has headache, vomiting and bilateral papilloedema. What is the mechanism of the papilloedema. [Prof 24]

options.A: Raised ICP transmitted along the optic nerve sheath, causing
options.B: Direct infarction of the optic nerve axoplasmic stasis

mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: The subarachnoid space extends along the optic nerve to the globe; raised CSF pressure compresses the central retinal vein and blocks axoplasmic flow 4 swollen optic disc.

mcqs.subject: Physiology
mcqs.question: A patient with meningitis develops communicating hydrocephalus because of scarring of the sites where CSF returns to blood. Through which structures is CSF absorbed? [WMC 26. AMC 25. CKMC 25]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Arachnoid villi project into the dural venous sinuses (mainly superior sagittal) and act as one-way valves opening when CSF pressure exceeds venous pressure by~1.5 mmHg.

mcqs.subject: Physiology
mcqs.question: A lumbar puncture is done on a healthy volunteer for comparison with plasma. Which constituent is present in the least concentration in CSF relative to plasma. [KIMS 26. WMC 25]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: CSF protein -20-40 mg/dL vs plasma 6-8 g/dL (=0.5A) because of the blood-CSF barrier. Glucose -60A of plasma. t protein: bacterial meningitis, Guillain-Barre (albuminocytological dissociation).

mcqs.subject: Physiology
mcqs.question: A physiology lab compares CSF with plasma composition. Which electrolyte is higher in CSF than in plasma. [WMC 25]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: CSF has higher Cl- and Mg" (and slightly higher Na. in some texts) but lower K., Ca, , glucose, protein, HCO3 and pH (7.33) than plasma.

mcqs.subject: Physiology
mcqs.question: A lumbar puncture is performed on a healthy adult lying on his side. What is the normal CSF pressure? [CKMC 26]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Source note: this question slot was blank in the CKMC 26 recall; a high-yield question on the same block topic has been added. Normal CSF pressure (lying) = 10 mmHg (70- 180 mm H,0). It rises with tumours, haemorrhage, meningitis (absorption blocked) and causes papilloedema.

mcqs.subject: Physiology
mcqs.question: A patient with intestinal colic feels poorly localized cramping pain. Visceral afferent fibres mainly innervate which tissue? [AMC 25]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Visceral afferents supply smooth muscle and mucosa of hollow organs.. they respond to distension, spasm, ischaemia and chemicals, travelling with sympathetic (pain) and parasympathetic (reflex) nerves.

mcqs.subject: Physiology
mcqs.question: A man with hyperhidrosis is treated by blocking the sympathetic supply to his sweat glands. Which glands receive sympathetic cholinergic innervation. [KIMS 26. LHR 25 . BWP 25]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Sympathetic postganglionic fibres to most eccrine sweat glands release acetylcholine (muscarinic). Adrenal medulla receives preganglionic cholinergic fibres directly (nicotinic).

mcqs.subject: Physiology
mcqs.question: A student faces a sudden threat: his heart races, pupils dilate and blood glucose rises. Which system mediates this emergency response? [CKMC 25]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Cannon: sympathetic "fight or flight" with mass discharge and adrenal medullary adrenaline. Parasympathetic = "rest and digest" discrete discharge.

mcqs.subject: Physiology
mcqs.question: A physiology student classifies nerve f ibres by size. Preganglionic autonomic fibres belong to which type. [CKMC 25]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: B fibres: thinly myelinated preganglionic autonomic. 3-15 m/s, most sensitive to hypoxia. C fibres: unmyelinated postganglionic sympathetic and slow pain, most sensitive to local anaesthetics.

mcqs.subject: Physiology
mcqs.question: A student under acute stress before an exam has sympathetic activation. Which effect consistently occurs in the stress response? [WMC 25]

options.D: Ciliary muscle relaxation for near vision

mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Sympathetic/adrenaline response: t metabolic rate, glycogenolysis, HR, BP, bronchodilation, mydriasis. Ciliary relaxation (far vision) occurs but is not the consistent metabolic effect asked.

mcqs.subject: Physiology
mcqs.question: A patient is given dobutamine to increase cardiac output. Which receptor increases heart rate. [WMC 25]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Fl (Gs, t CAMP) on SA node, AV node and myocardium 4 t HR, contractility, conduction. M2 (Gi) from vagus ￿ l HR. F2 4 bronchodilation, vasodilation.

mcqs.subject: Physiology
mcqs.question: A student sweats on the palms before public speaking. Which neurotransmitter acts on the sweat glands? [BWP 26. BWP 25]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Thermoregulatory and emotional sweating are mediated by sympathetic cholinergic fibres (Ach on M3). Palmar/apocrine sweating may also respond to circulating adrenaline.

mcqs.subject: Physiology
mcqs.question: A young woman faints after standing for a long time in a hot church; her pulse is slow during the episode. What causes vasovagal syncope. [BWP 25]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Vasovagal (neurocardiogenic) syncope." Bezold-jarisch reflex ￿ bradycardia (vagal) + vasodilation (sympathetic withdrawal) 4 cerebral hypoperfusion.

mcqs.subject: Physiology
mcqs.question: A man is sitting quietly in a chair after lunch reading a newspaper. Which part of the autonomic nervous system is predominantly active? [QIMS 25]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: "Rest and digest": parasympathetic activity (vagus) T Gl motility and secretion, l HR, pupillary constriction, accommodation for near (reading).

mcqs.subject: Physiology
mcqs.question: A medical student studies the craniosacral outflow. How do parasympathetic fibres leave the CNS? [QIMS 25]

options.C: Through cranial nerves111, VII, IX, X and sacral S2-S4

mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Parasympathetic.. long preganglionic fibres in CN111, VII, IX, X and pelvic splanchnics (S2-S4), short postganglionic fibres, Ach at both synapses.

mcqs.subject: Physiology
mcqs.question: A patient with bradycardia is given atropine. How does atropine increase heart rate. [KIMS 25]

options.B: Blockade of muscarinic (M2) receptors in the SA node
options.C: Activation of nicotinic receptors in ganglia

mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Vagal Ach on M2 receptors opens K, (IKACh) channels and reduces If at the SA node; atropine removes vagal tone (resting HR is normally under vagal dominance).

mcqs.subject: Physiology
mcqs.question: A hypertensive man is started on atenolol. What do P-blockers commonly do to the heart? [AMC 26]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Fl blockade 4 l HR, contractility, AV conduction and renin release (JG cells); non-selective agents can cause bronchospasm (F2).

mcqs.subject: Physiology
mcqs.question: A pharmacology student blocks transmission at autonomic ganglia with hexamethonium. Which receptor is activated by Ach from preganglionic fibres at autonomic ganglia? [AMC 26. MUL 26]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: All autonomic ganglia (sympathetic and parasympathetic) and the adrenal medulla use nicotinic NN receptors." target organs use muscarinic (parasympathetic) or adrenergic (sympathetic) receptors.

mcqs.subject: Physiology
mcqs.question: A student explains the effects of vagal stimulation after a meal. What does vagal parasympathetic stimulation primarily promote? [CKMC 26]

options.B: Digestion ( t Gl motility and secretion)

mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Vagus: t gastric acid, pancreatic secretion, gut motility; l HR,. bronchoconstriction. Pupillary constriction is via CN111.

mcqs.subject: Physiology
mcqs.question: An ophthalmologist uses pilocarpine to constrict the pupil in glaucoma. Which receptors mediate pupillary constriction. [MUL 26]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Sphincter pupillae and ciliary muscle: M3 (parasympathetic) - pilocarpine constricts. atropine dilates and paralyses accommodation (cycloplegia).

mcqs.subject: Physiology
mcqs.question: Phenylephrine eye drops dilate the pupil without affecting accommodation. Which receptors mediate pupillary dilatation. [MUL 26]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Dilator pupillae (radial muscle) has al receptors (sympathetic)," al agonists cause mydriasis without cycloplegia.

mcqs.subject: Physiology
mcqs.question: A man with phaeochromocytoma has paroxysmal hypertension, sweating, palpitations and anxiety. Excess of which neurotransmitter is responsible. [HITEC 26]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Phaeochromocytoma: chromaffin cell tumour of adrenal medulla secreting NE/E; "rule of IOS"; diagnose with plasma/urine metanephrines; treat with a-blocker (phenoxybenzamine) before F-blocker.

mcqs.subject: Physiology
mcqs.question: A diabetic man with autonomic neuropathy feels dizzy and his BP falls by 30 mmHg on standing. Which autonomic response is impaired? [BWP 26]

options.A: Reduced vagal activity to the heart only

mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Standing pools -500 ML blood in the legs 4 baroreceptor unloading ￿ sympathetic vasoconstriction and tachycardia. Autonomic failure (diabetes, Parkinson, MSA) ￿ orthostatic hypotension.

mcqs.subject: Physiology
mcqs.question: A child collapses in a garden sprayed with insecticide; he has pinpoint pupils, salivation, sweating, bradycardia and muscle twitching. Which neurotransmitter is in excess. [KIMS 26]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Organophosphates irreversibly inhibit acetylcholinesterase ￿ muscarinic (DUMBELS) and nicotinic (fasciculations, paralysis) effects; treat with atropine + pralidoxime.

mcqs.subject: Physiology
mcqs.question: A student narrowly escapes a road accident. His heart pounds and his mouth becomes dry. Which set of autonomic changes occurs during acute stress? [HITEC 26]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Stem created: the source recall was incomplete (stress question was incomplete). Sympathetic mass discharge + adrenal adrenaline: t HR and BP, mydriasis, bronchodilation, glycogenolysis, l Gl motility, redistribution of blood to muscles. BIOCHEMISTRY NEUROTRANSMirrERS

mcqs.subject: Biochemistry
mcqs.question: A medical student learns that a pigmented pontine nucleus projects widely to the cortex, promotes wakefulness and is overactive in panic states. Which neurotransmitter does the locus coeruleus release. [Prof 24]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Locus coeruleus (pons) ￿ norepinephrine (arousal, REM-off). Raphe nuclei 4 serotonin. Substantia nigra/wfA ￿ dopamine. Nucleus basalis of Meynert 4 acetylcholine (lost in Alzheimer).

mcqs.subject: Biochemistry
mcqs.question: Brain biopsy of a 65-year-old man with resting tremor and rigidity shows eosinophilic intracytoplasmic Lewy bodies in nigral neurons. Which protein accumulates in Parkinson disease. [Prof 24]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Lewy bodies = a-synuclein aggregates. Alzheimer: F-amyloid plaques (extracellular) + hyperphosphorylated tau tangles (intracellular). Pick disease." tau (Pick bodies).

mcqs.subject: Biochemistry
mcqs.question: Autopsy of a 78-year-old woman with progressive memory loss shows cortical atrophy and extracellular plaques. Which is the characteristic histological finding in Alzheimer disease. [Prof 24 . KIMS 26]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Alzheimer hallmarks: extracellular senile (F-amyloid) plaques + intracellular neurofibrillary tangles (hyperphosphorylated tau). Loss of cholinergic neurons of nucleus basalis of Meynert.

mcqs.subject: Biochemistry
mcqs.question: A neurology resident explains that excitotoxic neuronal death after stroke is caused by excess release of the main excitatory transmitter acting on NMDA receptors. Which is the major excitatory neurotransmitter of the CNS? [Prof 24]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Glutamate = main excitatory CNS transmitter (AMPA, NMDA, kainate receptors). GABA = main inhibitory transmitter in the brain," glycine = main inhibitory in the spinal cord.

mcqs.subject: Biochemistry
mcqs.question: A 45-year-old man with Huntington disease has atrophy of the caudate nucleus. Which neurotransmitter is mainly lost in Huntington disease. [CKMC 25]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Huntington: loss of striatal GABA/enkephalin and cholinergic neurons; dopamine is relatively preserved ￿ hyperkinesia. Parkinson: dopamine loss. Glutamate excitotoxicity contributes to death.

mcqs.subject: Biochemistry
mcqs.question: A woman with depression is started on fluoxetine. How do selective serotonin reuptake inhibitors act? [MUL 26. CKMC 25]

options.B: Prolong serotonin action in the synaptic cleft by blocking SERT

mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: SSRIS block the serotonin transporter (SERT) on presynaptic terminals," MAO inhibitors block degradation. Serotonin is removed mainly by reuptake, then degraded by MAO-A to 5-HIAA.

mcqs.subject: Biochemistry
mcqs.question: A 75-year-old man with Alzheimer disease is started on donepezil to improve recent memory. Which neurotransmitter is most important for recent memory. [AMC 26. MUL 25. KIMS 25]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Cholinergic neurons of nucleus basalis of Meynert project to cortex and hippocampus; their loss in Alzheimer disease is treated with cholinesterase inhibitors (donepezil, rivastigmine).

mcqs.subject: Biochemistry
mcqs.question: A woman with depression responds to drugs that increase brain serotonin. Which nucleus is the main source of serotonin in the brain. [MUL 25]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Raphe nuclei (midline brainstem) 4 serotonin: mood, sleep (NREM), pain inhibition (nucleus raphe magnus 4 spinal cord enkephalinergic interneurons).

mcqs.subject: Biochemistry
mcqs.question: A 40-year-old man with Down syndrome develops progressive memory loss. Brain imaging and biopsy show amyloid plaques. Which disease is this: [MUL 25]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: APP gene is on chromosome 21, so Down syndrome causes early Alzheimer disease. Early-onset familial AD.. APP, presenilin-l, presenilin-2; late-onset risk: ApoE4.

mcqs.subject: Biochemistry
mcqs.question: A man with resistant depression is given phenelzine and is warned to avoid cheese. How do MAO inhibitors act? [MUL 25]

options.D: Increase monoamine levels in the synaptic cleft by blocking their breakdown

mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: MAO (outer mitochondrial membrane) degrades NE, serotonin. dopamine. MAOIS T monoamines," tyramine (cheese, wine) then causes hypertensive crisis. MAO-B inhibitors (selegiline) for Parkinson disease.

mcqs.subject: Biochemistry
mcqs.question: A man with angina is given glyceryl trinitrate, which releases a gaseous transmitter. What is the main effect of nitric oxide. [MUL 25]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: NO (from arginine by NO synthase: needs NADPH. BH4) activates soluble guanylyl cyclase 4 CGMP 4 PKG 4 smooth muscle relaxation. In brain, NO acts as a retrograde messenger in LTP.

mcqs.subject: Biochemistry
mcqs.question: A patient with urticaria has histamine release. In which cells is histamine synthesized? [BWP 25]

options.D: Mast cells, basophils and gastric ECL cells

mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Histamine is formed from histidine by histidine decarboxylase (PLP-dependent) in mast cells, basophils, ECL cells and tuberomammillary neurons (wakefulness).

mcqs.subject: Biochemistry
mcqs.question: A patient with carcinoid syndrome develops pellagra because tryptophan is diverted. From which amino acid is serotonin synthesized? [BWP 25]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Tryptophan 4 (tryptophan hydroxylase, BH4) 5-hydroxytryptophan ￿ (aromatic L-amino acid decarboxylase, PLP) serotonin 4 melatonin (pineal). Carcinoid diverts tryptophan from niacin synthesis.

mcqs.subject: Biochemistry
mcqs.question: A 40-year-old woman with jet lag is prescribed melatonin. From which amino acid is melatonin derived? [QIMS 25]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Pineal: tryptophan 4 serotonin ￿ N-acetylserotonin (N-acetyltransferase, rate-limiting, t at night) ￿ melatonin (HIOMT). Light inhibits via SCN-sympathetic pathway.

mcqs.subject: Biochemistry
mcqs.question: A patient with phaeochromocytoma is given metyrosine to inhibit catecholamine synthesis at the rate-limiting step. Which enzyme is targeted? [CKMC 26. WMC 26. QIMS 25]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Tyrosine 4 DOPA (tyrosine hydroxylase, BH4, Fe", rate-limiting, inhibited by catecholamines) 4 dopamine (decarboxylase, PLP) ￿ NE (F-hydroxylase, vitamin C, Cu) ￿ E (PNMT, SAM," induced by cortisol).

mcqs.subject: Biochemistry
mcqs.question: A patient with early Parkinson disease is started on selegiline. Which neurotransmitter's breakdown does MAO-B inhibition mainly prevent? [QIMS 25]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: MAO-B preferentially degrades dopamine (selegiline, rasagiline)," MAO-A degrades serotonin and NE (and tyramine in the gut). COMT inhibitors (entacapone) also prolong levodopa.

mcqs.subject: Biochemistry
mcqs.question: A 70-year-old man with bradykinesia and rigidity improves on levodopa. Which neurotransmitter is deficient in the nigrostriatal pathway in Parkinson disease. [AMC 26. CKMC 26. WMC 26. BWP 26. KIMS 25]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Loss of SNC dopamine ￿ relative excess of striatal Ach (hence anticholinergics such as benzhexol help tremor). Levodopa crosses the BBB," carbidopa blocks peripheral decarboxylation.

mcqs.subject: Biochemistry
mcqs.question: A 35-year-old woman has episodic headaches, sweating, palpitations and hypertension. Which urinary metabolite is elevated in phaeochromocytoma. [CKMC 26]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: NE/E ￿ (COMT, MAO) metanephrines 4 VMA. Dopamine ￿ homovanillic acid (HVA, neuroblastoma). Serotonin ￿ 5-HIAA (carcinoid). Homogentisic acid 4 alkaptonuria.

mcqs.subject: Biochemistry
mcqs.question: A woman has urticaria after a bee sting due to histamine release. How is histamine synthesized? [MUL 26]

options.B: Decarboxylation of histidine by histidine decarboxylase

mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Biogenic amines are formed by PLP-dependent decarboxylation: histidine ￿ histamine," tryptophan (5-HTP) 4 serotonin; glutamate ￿ GABA; DOPA dopamine.

mcqs.subject: Biochemistry
mcqs.question: A biochemistry student traces catecholamine synthesis. Which amino acid is the precursor of dopamine. [WMC 26]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Phenylalanine ￿ tyrosine (phenylalanine hydroxylase) 4 DOPA ￿ dopamine 4 NE 4 E. In PKU, tyrosine becomes essential.

mcqs.subject: Biochemistry
mcqs.question: A 30-year-old woman has persistent sadness, anhedonia, insomnia, poor appetite and suicidal thoughts. Deficiency of which neurotransmitter is most classically associated with depression. [HITEC 26]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Monoamine hypothesis." I serotonin and norepinephrine in depression." treatments (SSRIS, SNRIS, TCAS, MAOIS) increase synaptic monoamines.

mcqs.subject: Biochemistry
mcqs.question: A patient with Parkinson disease is given levodopa with carbidopa. Which enzyme converts levodopa into dopamine? [BWP 26]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: DOPA decarboxylase (PLP-dependent); carbidopa inhibits it peripherally (does not cross BBB) so more levodopa reaches the brain and nausea is reduced. Pyridoxine supplements accelerate peripheral conversion.

mcqs.subject: Biochemistry
mcqs.question: A student lists neurotransmitters derived from amino acids. Which is formed from an amino acid (or amino-acid-derived) precursor. [BWP 26]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Dopamine è tyrosine," NO è arginine (NOS); acetylcholine é- choline (derived from serine/diet) + acetyl-CoA. Also serotonin è tryptophan, GABA glutamate, histamine &- histidine, glycine itself.

mcqs.subject: Biochemistry
mcqs.question: A student writes the sequence of catecholamine synthesis in the adrenal medulla. What is the correct sequence. [CKMC 26]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Stem created: the source recall was incomplete (handwritten note DopT (sequence)" read as the dopamine synthesis sequence). Enzymes: tyrosine hydroxylase (rate-limiting, BH4) ￿ DOPA decarboxylase (PLP) ￿ dopamine F-hydroxylase (vitamin C, Cu") ￿ PNMT (SAM," induced by cortisol).

mcqs.subject: Biochemistry
mcqs.question: A biochemist studies a small cloverleaf-shaped RNA containing pseudouridine and ribothymidine in its TWC arm and CCA at the 3 end. Which RNA is this? [Prof 24]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: tRNA: cloverleaf with acceptor arm (CCA-3), D arm (dihydrouridine), anticodon arm, TWC arm (binds ribosome). Contains the most unusual (modified) bases of all RNAS.

mcqs.subject: Biochemistry
mcqs.question: A student draws a nucleoside and labels the bond joining C-l of deoxyribose to N-9 of adenine. Between which components is the N-glycosidic bond in DNA? [AMC 25]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: N-glycosidic bond: Cl of pentose to N9 of purine or Nl of pyrimidine. 3.5-phosphodiester bonds link sugars through phosphate to form the backbone.

mcqs.subject: Biochemistry
mcqs.question: A muscle biopsy from a patient with mitochondrial myopathy shows low ATP content. What is the main role of ATP in cells. [AMC 25. QIMS 25]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: ATP is the energy currency (high-energy phosphoanhydride bonds, AG ~ _7.3 kcal/mol); dATP (not ATP) is used for DNA; NAD/FAD carry electrons: CAMP is a second messenger.

mcqs.subject: Biochemistry
mcqs.question: A student builds a DNA strand model joining the 3-OH of one nucleotide to the 5-phosphate of the next. What is the bond between phosphate and sugar called? [CKMC 26. BWP 26. CKMC 25]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: 3,5-phosphodiester bonds form the sugar-phosphate backbone (negatively charged at pH 7). Bases pair by hydrogen bonds (A=T two, G-C three).

mcqs.subject: Biochemistry
mcqs.question: An electron micrograph shows chromatin as beads on a string". Which histones form the nucleosome core octamer? [CKMC 25]

options.C: Two each of H2A, H2B, H3, H4

mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Core octamer: (H2A, H2B, H3, H4) x2 with -146 bp DNA wrapped 1.7 turns. HI is the linker histone binding linker DNA. Histones are rich in lysine and arginine (positive).

mcqs.subject: Biochemistry
mcqs.question: A biophysicist finds a left-handed DNA helix with a zigzag backbone in a sequence of alternating purines and pyrimidines. Z-DNA forms in which sequences. [CKMC 25]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: B-DNA: right-handed, 10.5 bp/turn (physiological). A-DNA: right-handed. dehydrated, 11 bp/turn. Z-DNA: left-handed, 12 bp/turn, alternating GC. high salt/methylation.

mcqs.subject: Biochemistry
mcqs.question: A student explains why DNA strands separate at 95°C during PCR. Which bonds hold complementary DNA strands together. [WMC 25. KIMS 25]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: A=T (2 H-bonds), G=C (3 H-bonds) - Gc-rich DNA has a higher melting temperature (Tm). Base stacking (hydrophobic, van der Waals) also stabilizes the helix.

mcqs.subject: Biochemistry
mcqs.question: A student combines the base uracil with ribose via an N-glycosidic bond. What is the product? [BWP 25]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Base + sugar = nucleoside (uridine. adenosine, guanosine, cytidine, thymidine)," + phosphate = nucleotide (UMP).

mcqs.subject: Biochemistry
mcqs.question: A student is given an unlabelled nucleic acid and finds it is hydrolysed by alkali. Which structural feature uniquely identifies RNA? [HITEC 26. QIMS 25]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: The 2-OH of ribose makes RNA susceptible to alkaline hydrolysis (DNA is resistant). RNA has uracil instead of thymine and is usually single-stranded.

mcqs.subject: Biochemistry
mcqs.question: A student lists the functions of nucleotides. What is a primary function of nucleotides in the body. [KIMS 25]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Nucleotides." building blocks of DNA/RNA. energy currency (ATP, GTP), coenzymes (NAD, FAD, COA). second messengers (CAMP, CGMP). activated intermediates (UDP-glucose, CDP-choline, SAM).

mcqs.subject: Biochemistry
mcqs.question: A biochemist distinguishes nucleotides A, T, G, C and U. Which part of a nucleotide determines its identity. [KIMS 25]

options.D: Pentose sugar C, U. T are pyrimidines.

mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Purines." adenine, guanine (double ring). Pyrimidines: cytosine, thymine. uracil (single ring). "CUT the Pye"

mcqs.subject: Biochemistry
mcqs.question: A forensic student lists the bases found in DNA from a blood stain. Which nitrogenous bases are found in DNA? [KIMS 25]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: DNA: A, G, C, T. RNA." A, G, C, U. Thymine = 5-methyluracil.

mcqs.subject: Biochemistry
mcqs.question: A lab technician measures the concentration of extracted DNA by UV spectrophotometry. At which wavelength is DNA absorbance measured? [AMC 26]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Nucleic acids absorb at 260 nm (aromatic bases)." proteins at 280 nm (Trp. Tyr). A260/A280 = 1.8 indicates pure DNA. Hyperchromicity: absorbance rises on denaturation. NADH absorbs at 340 nm.

mcqs.subject: Biochemistry
mcqs.question: Watson and Crick described the double helix. What is the relationship between the two strands of DNA? [CKMC 26]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Strands run 543 in opposite directions and pair by complementary bases (Chargaff.. A = T, G = C," purines = pyrimidines).

mcqs.subject: Biochemistry
mcqs.question: A student adds a phosphate group to adenosine. What is formed when a nucleoside is combined with phosphate. [CKMC 26]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Base + pentose = nucleoside; nucleoside + phosphate (ester at 5-OH) = nucleotide; polymer of nucleotides = nucleic acid; DNA + histone octamer = nucleosome.

mcqs.subject: Biochemistry
mcqs.question: A single DNA strand contains A 20%, T 25%, G 30% and C 25%. What is the composition of the complementary strand? [MUL 26]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: In the complementary strand, A = T of the template, T= A, G = C, C= G. Chargaff's rules (A = T, G = C) apply only to double-stranded DNA as a whole.

mcqs.subject: Biochemistry
mcqs.question: A student draws the bond linking adenine to ribose in adenosine. Which bond connects the nitrogenous base to the sugar in a nucleoside. [HITEC 26]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: F-N-glycosidic bond: Cl of the pentose to N9 (purines) or Nl (pyrimidines). Pseudouridine is an exception with a C-C glycosidic bond.

mcqs.subject: Biochemistry
mcqs.question: A student classifies ATP. ATP is classified as which of the following? [HITEC 26]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: ATP = adenine (purine) + ribose + three phosphates (a, F, y)," the F and y phosphoanhydride bonds are "high-energy"

mcqs.subject: Biochemistry
mcqs.question: DNA from a thermophilic bacterium living in hot springs has an unusually high melting temperature. Which feature explains this. [HITEC 26]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: G-C pairs have three hydrogen bonds and stronger stacking than A=T (two), so Gc-rich DNA has a higher Tm. Tm also rises with ionic strength and length.

mcqs.subject: Biochemistry
mcqs.question: A biophysicist examines DNA in transcriptionally active regions of a living cell. Which form of DNA is most common under physiological conditions. [HITEC 26]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: B-DNA (Watson-crick)." right-handed, 10.5 bp/turn, 3.4 nm pitch, major and minor grooves; the predominant form in aqueous physiological conditions.

mcqs.subject: Biochemistry
mcqs.question: A student models DNA for a practical exam. The DNA backbone is formed by alternating units of what? [BWP 26]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Sugar-phosphate backbone on the outside (hydrophilic, negatively charged); bases stacked inside, perpendicular to the helix axis.

mcqs.subject: Biochemistry
mcqs.question: An electron micrograph shows chromatin compacted into a 30-nm fibre. Which histone links adjacent nucleosomes and stabilizes DNA entry and exit? [BWP 26]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: HI (linker histone) binds linker DNA and promotes the 30-nm solenoid," it is the least conserved histone and is not part of the octamer.

mcqs.subject: Biochemistry
mcqs.question: A hepatocyte synthesizes glycogen after a meal. Which nucleoside triphosphate activates glucose for glycogen synthesis. [KIMS 26]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Glucose-l-phosphate + UTP 4 UDP-glucose (UDP-glucose pyrophosphorylase). Other activated carriers: CDP (phospholipids). SAM (methyl). GTP (protein synthesis, gluconeogenesis).

mcqs.subject: Biochemistry
mcqs.question: A hormone binds a Gs-coupled receptor and activates adenylyl cyclase in its target cell. Which nucleotide acts as the second messenger? [CKMC 26]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Source note: this question slot was blank in the CKMC 26 recall; a high-yield question on the same block topic has been added. Adenylyl cyclase converts ATP 4 CAMP (3,5-cyclic) 4 protein kinase A; degraded by phosphodiesterase (inhibited by caffeine/theophylline). CGMP is the messenger for NO and ANP.

mcqs.subject: Biochemistry
mcqs.question: A DNA strand has the sequence 5-ATGCGT-3. What is the sequence of its complementary strand written 543? [BWP 26]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Stem created: the source recall was incomplete (the DNA sequence was missing). The complement of 5-ATGCGT-3 is 3-TACGCA-5; written by convention 543 it is 5-ACGCAT-3 (antiparallel).

mcqs.subject: Biochemistry
mcqs.question: An infant has recurrent severe infections, oral thrush and a very low lymphocyte count. Red cell dATP levels are very high. Deficiency of which enzyme causes this SCID? [Prof 24. KIMS 26. AMC 25 . CKMC 25]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: ADA deficiency ￿ dATP accumulates 4 inhibits ribonucleotide reductase 4 no DNA synthesis in lymphocytes 4 SCID (autosomal recessive). First disease treated by gene therapy.

mcqs.subject: Biochemistry
mcqs.question: A 7-year-old boy bites his lips and f ingers, has intellectual disability, gouty arthritis and orange crystals in his diapers. Which enzyme is deficient? [Prof 24. CKMC 26. HITEC 26. AMC 25. CKMC 25. MUL 25. QIMS 25. KIMS 25]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Lesch-Nyhan: X-linked recessive HGPRT deficiency ￿ failed purine salvage, T PRPP, t de novo synthesis, hyperuricaemia. HGPRT: Hyperuricaemia, Gout, Pissed off (aggression, self-mutilation), Retardation, dysTonia.

mcqs.subject: Biochemistry
mcqs.question: A 50-year-old man with recurrent gout and uric acid stones is started on allopurinol. Which enzyme does it inhibit? [CKMC 26. HITEC 26. AMC 25 . QIMS 25]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Allopurinol (hypoxanthine analogue) 4 oxypurinol, a suicide inhibitor of xanthine oxidase (hypoxanthine 4 xanthine ￿ uric acid). Febuxostat is non-purine inhibitor.

mcqs.subject: Biochemistry
mcqs.question: A child on a drug that depletes folate develops megaloblastic anaemia because thymidylate cannot be made. Which cofactor is needed to convert dUMP to dTMP? [AMC 25]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Thymidylate synthase transfers a methylene group from N',N"_methylene-THF to dUMP, producing DHF, which DHFR must reduce back to THF. 5-FU inhibits thymidylate synthase.

mcqs.subject: Biochemistry
mcqs.question: A patient with rheumatoid arthritis on methotrexate develops mouth ulcers and pancytopenia, which improve with folinic acid. Which enzyme does methotrexate inhibit? [AMC 25. CKMC 25. QIMS 25]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Methotrexate, trimethoprim (bacterial) and pyrimethamine (protozoal) inhibit DHFR ￿ no THF 4 I dTMP and purines. Leucovorin (folinic acid) bypasses the block.

mcqs.subject: Biochemistry
mcqs.question: A patient on S-f luorouracil for colon cancer has reduced DNA synthesis. Which reaction does thymidylate synthase catalyse? [LHR 25]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Thymidylate synthase methylates dUMP to dTMP using N',N'°_methylene-THF; inhibited by 5-FU (as FdUMP, suicide inhibitor).

mcqs.subject: Biochemistry
mcqs.question: In E. coli, the f irst committed enzyme of pyrimidine synthesis is allosterically controlled by the end product. By which nucleotide is aspartate transcarbamoylase inhibited? [LHR 25]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Bacterial ATCase: inhibited by CTP, activated by ATP. In humans the regulated step is CPS-11 (cytosolic)." inhibited by UTP, activated by PRPP and ATP.

mcqs.subject: Biochemistry
mcqs.question: A child has megaloblastic anaemia unresponsive to B12 and folate, poor growth and orotic acid crystals in urine, with normal blood ammonia. Which enzyme is defective in hereditary orotic aciduria? [AMC 26 . HITEC 26. KIMS 26. CKMC 25 . QIMS 25. KIMS 25]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: UMP synthase (orotate phosphoribosyltransferase + OMP decarboxylase) deficiency ￿ orotic aciduria; treat with uridine. OTC deficiency also raises orotic acid but with hyperammonaemia and no anaemia.

mcqs.subject: Biochemistry
mcqs.question: A kidney transplant recipient is given mycophenolate mofetil to suppress lymphocyte proliferation. What is its mechanism? [MUL 25]

options.A: Inhibits IMP dehydrogenase ( I GMP synthesis) I

mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: IMP ￿ XMP (IMP dehydrogenase) 4 GMP. Lymphocytes depend on de novo purine synthesis. so MPA and ribavirin (IMPDH inhibitors) are selectively antiproliferative.

mcqs.subject: Biochemistry
mcqs.question: A biochemistry student traces the atoms of the pyrimidine ring. What are the sources of nitrogen in pyrimidine synthesis. [MUL 25]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Pyrimidine ring." N3 from glutamine (via carbamoyl phosphate), Nl + C4-C6 from aspartate. C2 from CO,. Purine ring." glycine, aspartate, glutamine, CO,, N"_formyl-THF.

mcqs.subject: Biochemistry
mcqs.question: A biochemist studies the committed step of de novo purine synthesis, which is inhibited by AMP, GMP and IMP. Which enzyme catalyses this regulated step. [MUL 25 . QIMS 25]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: PRPP + glutamine 4 5-phosphoribosylamine (glutamine:PRPP amidotransferase) - the committed, rate-limiting step," feedback inhibited by purine nucleotides, activated by PRPP.

mcqs.subject: Biochemistry
mcqs.question: A hypertensive man on hydrochlorothiazide develops his first attack of gout. How do thiazides cause gout? [MUL 25]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Thiazides and loop diuretics compete for tubular organic acid secretion and cause volume contraction 4 t urate reabsorption. Underexcretion causes~900A of primary gout.

mcqs.subject: Biochemistry
mcqs.question: A patient with chronic myeloid leukaemia is given hydroxyurea to reduce DNA synthesis in tumour cells. Which enzyme is inhibited? [MUL 25 . WMC 25]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Ribonucleotide reductase converts NDPS to dNDPs (needs thioredoxin); inhibited by hydroxyurea and high dATP. Hydroxyurea also raises HbF in sickle cell disease.

mcqs.subject: Biochemistry
mcqs.question: A leukaemic patient's cells become resistant to methotrexate after months of treatment. What is the commonest mechanism of resistance. [WMC 25]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Tumour cells amplify the DHFR gene (homogeneously staining regions, double minutes) 4 more enzyme than drug can inhibit. Reduced uptake (RFC) and polyglutamation also contribute.

mcqs.subject: Biochemistry
mcqs.question: A child with hereditary orotic aciduria has megaloblastic anaemia and failure to thrive. What is the treatment? [WMC 25 . BWP 25]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Oral uridine is converted by salvage to UMP ￿ bypasses UMP synthase and feedback-inhibits CPS-II, reducing orotic acid production.

mcqs.subject: Biochemistry
mcqs.question: A biochemist labels the amide nitrogen of an amino acid and finds it in two positions of the purine ring. Which amino acid supplies N3 and N9 of the purine ring? [WMC 25. QIMS 25]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Purine ring: Nl aspartate; C2, C8 formyl-THF; N3, N9 glutamine; C4, C5, N7 glycine; C6 CO,. Key note: source answer "glutamine and glycine"; glycine supplies N7, not N3/N9.

mcqs.subject: Biochemistry
mcqs.question: A student traces glycine incorporation into the purine ring. Which nitrogen of the purine ring comes from glycine. [WMC 25]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Glycine is incorporated whole, contributing C4, C5 and N7. Aspartate gives Nl only. Key note: source keyed aspartate for the "position 7" nitrogen.

mcqs.subject: Biochemistry
mcqs.question: A child with HGPRT deficiency has hyperuricaemia. In which pathway is HGPRT involved? [BWP 26. BWP 25]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: HGPRT: hypoxanthine + PRPP 4 IMP,. guanine + PRPP 4 GMP. APRT: adenine 4 AMP. Salvage saves energy and is the main route in brain and RBCS.

mcqs.subject: Biochemistry
mcqs.question: A 55-year-old man has an acutely swollen first MTP joint with negatively birefringent needle-shaped crystals. Gout is a disorder of which metabolism. [CKMC 26. BWP 25]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Gout = monosodium urate deposition from hyperuricaemia (end product of purine catabolism); pseudogout = calcium pyrophosphate (positively birefringent, rhomboid).

mcqs.subject: Biochemistry
mcqs.question: A biochemist compares purine catabolism in humans and dogs. What is the end product of purine catabolism in humans. [CKMC 26. BWP 25. KIMS 25]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Humans and higher primates lack uricase, so uric acid is excreted,. other mammals convert it to allantoin. Pyrimidine catabolism gives soluble products (F-alanine. F-aminoisobutyrate. CO,, NH,).

mcqs.subject: Biochemistry
mcqs.question: A student traces which nucleosides are degraded to uric acid. Uric acid is formed from the degradation of which nucleoside. [BWP 25]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Purine nucleosides (adenosine via inosine/hypoxanthine, guanosine via guanine) 4 xanthine ￿ uric acid. Pyrimidines (cytidine, uridine, thymidine) do not form uric acid.

mcqs.subject: Biochemistry
mcqs.question: A child on methotrexate for ALL has impaired DNA synthesis. Synthesis of which nucleotide is most directly decreased? [BWP 25]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Without THF regeneration, N',N'°_methylene-THF is unavailable for thymidylate synthase 4 I dTMP ("thymineless death")," purine synthesis (formyl-THF steps) is also reduced.

mcqs.subject: Biochemistry
mcqs.question: In the branch from IMP to GMP, the end product feeds back on its own synthesis. Which nucleotide allosterically inhibits IMP dehydrogenase. [BWP 25]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Cross-regulation: GMP inhibits IMP dehydrogenase (IMP 4 XMP), AMP inhibits adenylosuccinate synthetase," GTP is needed for AMP synthesis and ATP for GMP synthesis (balance).

mcqs.subject: Biochemistry
mcqs.question: A biochemist traces aspartate into the purine ring. Aspartate provides nitrogen at which position of the purine ring? [BWP 25]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Aspartate gives Nl of purines (and Nl + C4-C6 of pyrimidines); also donates the amino group converting IMP to AMP. Key note: source keyed "Nl, N7" N7 comes from glycine.

mcqs.subject: Biochemistry
mcqs.question: A patient on 5~f luorouracil for colorectal cancer develops anaemia and mucositis. Synthesis of which nucleotide does 5-FU inhibit? [MUL 26. QIMS 25]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: 5-FU ￿ FdUMP forms a covalent ternary complex with thymidylate synthase and methylene-THF (suicide inhibition); leucovorin ENHANCES 5-FU toxicity (opposite of methotrexate rescue).

mcqs.subject: Biochemistry
mcqs.question: A man with an acute gout attack is given colchicine. What is its mechanism? [AMC 26. QIMS 25]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Colchicine binds tubulin ￿ inhibits neutrophil chemotaxis and phagocytosis of urate crystals. Probenecid t excretion," allopurinol/febuxostat I production.

mcqs.subject: Biochemistry
mcqs.question: A 3-month-old with recurrent infections is found to have adenosine deaminase deficiency. Which pathway is affected? [KIMS 25]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: ADA (adenosine 4 inosine) and PNP (inosine 4 hypoxanthine) are enzymes of purine catabolism; deficiency of either ￿ immunodeficiency (ADA: T + B,. PNP: T only).

mcqs.subject: Biochemistry
mcqs.question: A biochemistry student identifies the regulated first step of pyrimidine synthesis in the cytosol of human cells. Which is the rate-limiting enzyme of de novo pyrimidine synthesis in humans. [AMC 26]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: CPS11 (cytosol, glutamine as N donor, part of CAD) - inhibited by UTP, activated by PRPP/ATP. CPS I (mitochondria, NH,, needs N-acetylglutamate) is for urea synthesis.

mcqs.subject: Biochemistry
mcqs.question: A man with early gout and uric acid stones has very high intracellular PRPP levels with normal HGPRT activity. Increased activity of which enzyme explains this. [AMC 26]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: X-linked PRPP synthetase superactivity 4 t PRPP 4 t de novo purine synthesis 4 hyperuricaemia and gout. PRPP synthetase is inhibited by purine nucleotides.

mcqs.subject: Biochemistry
mcqs.question: A child has recurrent viral and fungal infections; T-cell numbers are very low but B and NK cells are normal; uric acid is low. Deficiency of which enzyme is suggested? [AMC 26]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: PNP deficiency 4 dGTP accumulates in T cells ￿ selective T-cell immunodeficiency, neurological problems, LOW uric acid. ADA deficiency affects T and B cells (SCID).

mcqs.subject: Biochemistry
mcqs.question: A child with ADA deficiency has very high dATP in lymphocytes. How does excess dATP impair DNA synthesis. [MUL 26]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: dATP binds the activity site of ribonucleotide reductase ￿ inhibits reduction of all NDPS 4 no dNTPs 4 lymphocyte apoptosis.

mcqs.subject: Biochemistry
mcqs.question: A man with gout asks which foods to avoid; organ meats and seafood are rich in nucleic acids. Which base should be restricted in gout? [MUL 26]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Purines (adenine. guanine) are catabolized to uric acid." pyrimidines are degraded to soluble products. Low-purine diet: avoid red/organ meat, seafood, beer.

mcqs.subject: Biochemistry
mcqs.question: A man with gout starts allopurinol; urinary uric acid falls. Which purine metabolite accumulates during allopurinol treatment? [MUL 26]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Blocking xanthine oxidase raises hypoxanthine and xanthine, which are more soluble and partly reused by HGPRT salvage (feedback reduces de novo synthesis). Rare xanthine stones.

mcqs.subject: Biochemistry
mcqs.question: In a dividing cell, dGTP levels rise markedly. Which deoxyribonucleotide synthesis is stimulated by allosteric regulation of ribonucleotide reductase. [MUL 26]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Specificity site: ATP/dATP 4 reduction of CDP. UDP,. dTTP 4 GDP," dGTP 4 ADP. This balances dNTP pools. dATP at the activity site inhibits the enzyme overall.

mcqs.subject: Biochemistry
