mcqs.question: A child has growth retardation and megaloblastic anaemia unresponsive to B12 and folate with high urinary orotic acid. Which pathway is affected? [HITEC 26]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Orotate 4 OMP 4 UMP is the final part of de novo pyrimidine synthesis,. block 4 low pyrimidines (megaloblastosis) and orotic acid excess.

mcqs.subject: Biochemistry
mcqs.question: A man develops sudden severe pain, swelling and redness of the great toe after a feast with red meat and alcohol. What is the underlying cause. [HITEC 26]

options.A: Bacterial infection of the MTP joint

mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Acute gout (podagra): urate crystals precipitate in the cool first MTP joint; alcohol (lactate competes for urate excretion, t ATP turnover) and purine-rich foods trigger attacks.

mcqs.subject: Biochemistry
mcqs.question: A student compares de novo pyrimidine synthesis with pyrimidine salvage. Which substrate is used in both pathways. [BWP 261
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: De novo." orotate + PRPP 4 OMP (orotate phosphoribosyltransferase). Salvage: uracil + PRPP 4 UMP (uracil phosphoribosyltransferase). PRPP is also needed for purine de novo and salvage. Source key was not confirmed.

mcqs.subject: Biochemistry
mcqs.question: A biochemist labels aspartate and finds the label in both purine and pyrimidine rings. Which substance contributes atoms to both purine and pyrimidine rings. [BWP 26]

options.B: Glutamine (also both, but via amide N only)

mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Aspartate: Nl of purines; Nl, C4, C5, C6 of pyrimidines. Glutamine also donates N to both (N3, N9 purine; N3 pyrimidine via CPS11) - but aspartate contributes ring atoms directly in both. Glycine is purine-only.

mcqs.subject: Biochemistry
mcqs.question: A 50-year-old man has an acutely painful, swollen f irst metatarsophalangeal joint. Joint aspirate is examined under polarized light. Which finding confirms gout? [CKMC 26]

options.B: Rhomboid, positively birefringent calcium pyrophosphate crystals
options.D: Needle-shaped, negatively birefringent monosodium urate crystals

mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Stem created: the source recall was incomplete (note said only "Gout ). Gout: urate, needle-shaped, negatively birefringent (yellow when parallel to the compensator). Pseudogout: CPPD, rhomboid, weakly positive (blue).

mcqs.subject: Biochemistry
mcqs.question: Rapidly dividing cells must make deoxyribonucleotides for DNA synthesis. Which enzyme converts ribonucleoside diphosphates to deoxyribonucleotides? [CKMC 26]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Source note: this question slot was blank in the CKMC 26 recall; a high-yield question on the same block topic has been added. Ribonucleotide reductase (NDP 4 dNDP) uses thioredoxin/NADPH; it is inhibited by hydroxyurea and allosterically by dATP,' activity is highest in S phase. 14 15

mcqs.subject: Biochemistry
mcqs.question: Glycine labelled with C and N is given to a culture of dividing cells. Which atoms of the purine ring become labelled? [MUL 26]

options.A: One nitrogen and two carbons (N7, C4, C5)

mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Stem created: the source recall was incomplete (the precursor was not named). Glycine is incorporated whole into the purine ring: C4, C5 and N7. Aspartate gives Nl,. glutamine N3, N9; formyl-THF C2, C8,. CO, C6.

mcqs.subject: Biochemistry
mcqs.question: A child has severe sunburn after minimal exposure, freckling and multiple skin cancers by age 8. Which DNA lesion is not repaired in xeroderma pigmentosum? [Prof24. CKMC 26. HITEC 26. BWP 26. CKMC 25. QIMS 25. KIMS 25]

options.A: Thymine dimers by nucleotide excision repair
options.C: Deaminated bases by base excision repair

mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: UV light ￿ pyrimidine (thymine) dimers ￿ repaired by nucleotide excision repair (Uv-specific endonuclease). Defect = xeroderma pigmentosum. Mismatch repair defect = Lynch syndrome (HNPCC).

mcqs.subject: Biochemistry
mcqs.question: A man with a chest infection is allergic to penicillin and is given erythromycin. On which ribosomal subunit does it act? [Prof 24. KIMS 26. MUL 25]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Macrolides bind 50S and block translocation. "Buy AT 30, CCEL at 50": Aminoglycosides, Tetracyclines on 30S; Chloramphenicol, Clindamycin, Erythromycin, Linezolid on 50S.

mcqs.subject: Biochemistry
mcqs.question: During DNA replication in a rapidly dividing tumour cell, positive supercoils build up ahead of the replication fork. How do topoisomerases solve this. [Prof 24. WMC 26. KIMS 26]

options.A: Seal nicks in the lagging strand
options.C: Unwind the double helix by breaking hydrogen bonds
options.D: Make transient breaks in DNA to relieve supercoiling

mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Topoisomerase I cuts one strand (no ATP); topoisomerase11 (DNA gyrase in bacteria) cuts both strands (ATP) to relieve supercoils. Helicase breaks H-bonds." ligase seals nicks.

mcqs.subject: Biochemistry
mcqs.question: A researcher silences a gene by RNA interference. Double-stranded RNA is processed into SIRNA, which guides the RISC complex to cleave the target MRNA. Which enzyme of RISC cleaves the MRNA? [Prof 24]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Dicer chops dsRNA into 21-23 nt siRNA/miRNA; Argonaute ("slicer") within RISC cleaves the complementary MRNA. MIRNA with imperfect pairing blocks translation instead.

mcqs.subject: Biochemistry
mcqs.question: During protein synthesis in a hepatocyte, the ribosome reads nucleotide triplets. On which molecule are codons present? [Prof 24]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Codons are on MRNA (read 543)," anticodons are on tRNA. 64 codons: 61 sense, 3 stop (UAA, UAG, UGA),. AUG = start (methionine).

mcqs.subject: Biochemistry
mcqs.question: A baby born to an HIV-positive mother is given zidovudine (AZT) prophylaxis. What is the mechanism of action of this drug. [Prof 24]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Azf= thymidine analogue lacking 3-OH ￿ chain termination of viral DNA made by reverse transcriptase. Main toxicity: bone marrow suppression (anaemia).

mcqs.subject: Biochemistry
mcqs.question: A 28-year-old man is newly diagnosed with HIV infection. Which treatment should he start? [Prof 24]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: HIV is treated with combination ART (usually 2 NRTIS + an integrase inhibitor/NNRTl/protease inhibitor) to prevent resistance from the error-prone reverse transcriptase.

mcqs.subject: Biochemistry
mcqs.question: In E. coli, after Okazaki fragments are made on the lagging strand, the RNA primers must be removed and replaced with DNA. Which enzyme does this. [Prof 24. CKMC 26. AMC 25]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: DNA polymerase I has 543 exonuclease activity 4 removes RNA primers and fills gaps. Pol111 = main replicative enzyme. Ligase seals the remaining nick. In eukaryotes RNase H/FENI remove primers.

mcqs.subject: Biochemistry
mcqs.question: A family develops liver failure after eating wild Amanita mushrooms. Which enzyme does a-amanitin inhibit? [AMC 26. BWP 26. AMC 25. WMC 25]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: a-Amanitin strongly inhibits RNA Pol11 (MRNA, snRNA, MIRNA); Pol111 (tRNA, 5S rRNA) only at high concentration," Pol l (28S. 18S, 5.8S rRNA) is resistant.

mcqs.subject: Biochemistry
mcqs.question: A child with a grey pharyngeal membrane develops myocarditis. The toxin ADP-ribosylates a host protein. What does diphtheria toxin inhibit? [AMC 25]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Diphtheria toxin (and Pseudomonas exotoxin A) ADP-ribosylates eEF-2 ￿ blocks translocation ￿ stops protein synthesis.

mcqs.subject: Biochemistry
mcqs.question: A patient with sepsis on gentamicin develops hearing loss. How do aminoglycosides inhibit bacterial protein synthesis. [AMC 25]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Aminoglycosides bind 30S ￿ block initiation complex and cause misreading of MRNA codons. Toxicity: nephro- and ototoxicity, neuromuscular blockade.

mcqs.subject: Biochemistry
mcqs.question: A blood donor has a positive HIV ELISA; a conf irmatory test detects antibodies to separated viral proteins. Which technique is used to detect proteins. [AMC 25. BWP 25]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: SNOW DROP: Southern = DNA, Northern = RNA, Western = Protein. Western blot was the classic HIV confirmatory test; Southwestern = DNA-binding proteins.

mcqs.subject: Biochemistry
mcqs.question: A 40-year-old man has right~sided colon cancer; his mother had endometrial cancer at 45. Tumour shows microsatellite instability. Hereditary nonpolyposis colorectal cancer results from a defect in which repair system. [MUL 26. HITEC 26. AMC 25]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Lynch syndrome: germline MLHI/MSH2 mutations 4 mismatch repair defect ￿ microsatellite instability. BRCA1/2 = homologous recombination; ataxia-telangiectasia (ATM) = DSB sensing.

mcqs.subject: Biochemistry
mcqs.question: A patient on warfarin has a prolonged PT; his clotting factors are synthesized but inactive. Which post-translational modification is impaired in vitamin K deficiency. [AMC 25. CKMC 25. QIMS 25]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Vitamin K is a cofactor for y-glutamyl carboxylase ￿ Gla residues bind Ca" (factors11, VII, IX, X, protein C, S). Vitamin C 4 hydroxylation of proline/lysine in collagen.

mcqs.subject: Biochemistry
mcqs.question: Cancer cells divide indef initely without the chromosome shortening that occurs in normal somatic cells. Which enzyme prevents chromosome shortening during replication. [WMC 26. AMC 25. CKMC 25. MUL 25]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Telomerase = ribonucleoprotein reverse transcriptase that adds TtAGGG repeats to 3 ends using its own RNA template; active in germ cells. stem cells and ~90% of cancers.

mcqs.subject: Biochemistry
mcqs.question: A newborn of an HIV-positive mother needs testing; maternal antibodies make serology unreliable. What is the best method to detect HIV infection in this situation. [MUL 26 . AMC 25]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: HIV RNA by RT-PCR detects infection in infants (<18 months) and in the window period; ELISA is the screening test in adults, and viral load monitors therapy.

mcqs.subject: Biochemistry
mcqs.question: A patient's abnormal haemoglobin chain (Hb Constant Spring) is 31 amino acids longer than normal because of a mutation in the termination codon. What results from loss of a stop codon? [LHR 25]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Stop-loss (non-stop) mutation converts UAA/UAG/UGA into a sense codon ￿ translation continues into the 3 UTR 4 elongated protein. Nonsense mutation does the opposite.

mcqs.subject: Biochemistry
mcqs.question: E. coli grown on lactose with no glucose strongly expresses F-galactosidase. Maximal function of the lac operon depends on what? [AMC 26. LHR 25]

options.A: RNA polymerase binding without any regulation
options.C: CAP-CAMP binding plus presence of lactose (allolactose)

mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Lac operon is maximally ON when lactose present (allolactose removes repressor) AND glucose absent ( t CAMP 4 CAP-CAMP enhances RNA polymerase binding). Glucose present ￿ catabolite repression.

mcqs.subject: Biochemistry
mcqs.question: E. coli is grown in a medium containing both glucose and lactose. What is the state of the lac operon. [CKMC 25]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Glucose I CAMP 4 no CAP-CAMP 4 only basal transcription even if lactose is present (catabolite repression). Bacteria use glucose first (diauxic growth).

mcqs.subject: Biochemistry
mcqs.question: A boy with Duchenne muscular dystrophy has a point mutation changing a CAG codon to UAG. What does a nonsense mutation cause. [KIMS 26. CKMC 25. MUL 25]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Nonsense = sense codon 4 stop codon; missense = different amino acid (e.g. sickle cell Glu6Val); silent = same amino acid (wobble)," frameshift = insertion/deletion not a multiple of 3.

mcqs.subject: Biochemistry
mcqs.question: A patient with tuberculosis develops vertigo on streptomycin. Which ribosomal subunit does streptomycin bind? [AMC 26. CKMC 25. QIMS 25]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Streptomycin binds the 30S subunit (16S rRNA, S12 protein) ￿ inhibits initiation complex and causes misreading. Ototoxic (vestibular) and nephrotoxic.

mcqs.subject: Biochemistry
mcqs.question: A forensic lab digests DNA with a restriction enzyme and compares fragment patterns between a suspect and a crime scene. What does RFLP analysis detect? [CKMC 25]

options.B: Variation in restriction fragment lengths (due to SNPS or VNTRS at restriction sites)

mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: RFLP: inherited sequence differences that create/abolish restriction sites or vary the number of tandem repeats (VNTR) ￿ different fragment sizes on Southern blot," used in paternity. forensics, sickle cell (Mstll).

mcqs.subject: Biochemistry
mcqs.question: A molecular biologist notes that MRNA lacking a poly-A tail is rapidly degraded in the cytoplasm. What is the function of the poly-A tail? [CKMC 25 . QIMS 25]

options.C: MRNA stability and nuclear export (and translation)

mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Poly(A) polymerase adds -200 A residues after the AAUAAA signal; poly-A tail protects from 3 exonucleases, aids export and translation initiation. Histone MRNAS lack poly-A tails.

mcqs.subject: Biochemistry
mcqs.question: A child with Wilms tumour receives dactinomycin. What is its mechanism of action? [CKMC 25]

options.B: Intercalates between GC base pairs of DNA, blocking transcription

mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Actinomycin D intercalates into DNA at G-C pairs and blocks RNA polymerase elongation (inhibits transcription in both prokaryotes and eukaryotes).

mcqs.subject: Biochemistry
mcqs.question: A technician performs a Southern blot to detect a gene deletion. What is the correct sequence of steps. [CKMC 25]

options.D: Restriction digestion and electrophoresis 4 blotting 4 hybridization with probe

mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Southern: digest DNA 4 agarose gel electrophoresis 4 denature and transfer (blot) to nitrocellulose/nylon 4 hybridize labelled probe autoradiography.

mcqs.subject: Biochemistry
mcqs.question: A neuroscientist shows that cAMP-dependent PKA phosphorylates a nuclear protein that binds the CRE element and enhances gene expression. What is the action of CREB? [CKMC 25]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: CAMP 4 PKA 4 phosphorylated CREB binds CAMP response elements and recruits CBP/p300 4 gene transcription; underlies long-term memory formation.

mcqs.subject: Biochemistry
mcqs.question: A lab uses a labelled single-stranded DNA fragment to locate the sickle cell gene on a blot. What does a probe do. [CKMC 25]

options.B: Binds a complementary nucleic acid sequence (hybridization)

mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Probe: labelled (radioactive/fluorescent) SSDNA or RNA that base-pairs with its complementary target: allele-specific oligonucleotide probes detect point mutations.

mcqs.subject: Biochemistry
mcqs.question: A child with transfusion-dependent anaemia has a point mutation at an intron-exon junction that creates abnormal MRNA. Splice-site mutations are classically associated with which disease? [CKMC 25]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Splice-site mutations: F-thalassaemia (classic), also some cases of DMD, Tay-sachs, Gaucher. Key note: source answered Duchenne muscular dystrophy," F-thalassaemia is the textbook example.

mcqs.subject: Biochemistry
mcqs.question: A biochemist shows that E. coli DNA polymerase I can remove nucleotides ahead of it while synthesizing new DNA (nick translation). Which activity of Pol I removes RNA primers? [WMC 26. CKMC 25]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Poll: 543 polymerase, 345 exonuclease (proofreading), 543 exonuclease (primer removal, nick translation). Klenow fragment lacks the 543 exonuclease.

mcqs.subject: Biochemistry
mcqs.question: A virologist notes that a DNA virus uses host RNA polymerase11 to make its messenger RNA. What does RNA polymerase11 synthesize. [CKMC 25 . KIMS 25]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Eukaryotic RNA polymerases: l = rRNA (28S, 18S, 5.8S) in nucleolus; 11 = MRNA, snRNA, miRNA;111 = tRNA, 5S rRNA. "1-2-3 = R-M-T

mcqs.subject: Biochemistry
mcqs.question: A 38-year-old woman with chorea and a family history of the same disease undergoes genetic testing showing expanded CAG repeats. On which chromosome is the Huntington gene located? [MUL 25]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Huntingtin gene (HTT) on 4p16.3, autosomal dominant, CAG (glutamine) repeats >36, anticipation especially with paternal transmission.

mcqs.subject: Biochemistry
mcqs.question: An E. coli MRNA lacking a purine-rich sequence -8 bases upstream of AUG is not translated. Which sequence is recognized by the 30S subunit for initiation. [MUL 25 . QIMS 25]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Shine-Dalgarno sequence pairs with 16S rRNA of the 30S subunit. Eukaryotes use the 5 cap and Kozak sequence. TATA (Hogness) and Pribnow boxes are DNA promoter elements.

mcqs.subject: Biochemistry
mcqs.question: A child is tested for a gene deletion by transferring digested DNA from gel to membrane and probing it. Which blotting technique detects DNA sequences. [MUL 25. KIMS 25]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Southern (E.M. Southern) = DNA; Northern = RNA (gene expression): Western = protein (antibody): Eastern = post-translational modifications.

mcqs.subject: Biochemistry
mcqs.question: A lab analyses RFLPS to establish paternity. Which enzyme is used to generate the fragments. [MUL 25]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Restriction endonucleases (molecular scissors) cut at palindromic sequences (e.g. ECORI GAArrc), giving sticky or blunt ends.

mcqs.subject: Biochemistry
mcqs.question: A genetic engineer chooses a plasmid as the vector for cloning the insulin gene. Which property of plasmids makes them useful? [MUL 25. WMC 25]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Plasmids." small circular extrachromosomal dsDNA with their own origin of replication, multiple cloning sites and antibiotic-resistance genes for selection.

mcqs.subject: Biochemistry
mcqs.question: A microbiologist identifies a cluster of genes (lacz, lacy, lacA) transcribed together when lactose is available. What is this set of genes called? [MUL 25]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Lac operon (inducible): lacz (F-galactosidase), lacy (permease), lacA (transacetylase) under one promoter/operator, controlled by lacl repressor. Trp operon is repressible.

mcqs.subject: Biochemistry
mcqs.question: A tRNA with anticodon 3-CGI-5 can read GCU, GCC and GCA. How can one tRNA recognize several codons. [MUL 25]

options.B: Wobble base pairing at the third codon base J

mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl. Crick wobble hypothesis: the 5 base of the anticodon (often inosine) pairs loosely with the 3 base of the codon; explains code degeneracy and why only-45 tRNAs are needed for 61 codons.

mcqs.subject: Biochemistry
mcqs.question: A woman with iron-deficiency anaemia has increased transferrin receptor expression on her erythroid precursors. How does iron deficiency affect the transferrin receptor. [MUL 25]

options.B: Increased receptor expression (IRP stabilizes its MRNA)

mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Low iron 4 iron-regulatory protein binds IRES: at 3 UTR of transferrin-receptor MRNA (stabilizes 4 t TfR) and 5 UTR of ferritin MRNA (blocks translation 4 I ferritin).

mcqs.subject: Biochemistry
mcqs.question: During PCR to detect a viral gene, the temperature is lowered to about 55°C. What happens in the annealing step. [MUL 25]

options.C: Primers bind to the template DNA

mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: PCR cycle." denaturation (94-96 f) 4 annealing of primers (50-65 °C) 4 extension by Taq polymerase (72 °C); 25-35 cycles ￿ exponential amplification.

mcqs.subject: Biochemistry
mcqs.question: A primary transcript of 8 kb is processed into a 2 kb mature MRNA in the nucleus. What does splicing remove. [MUL 25. KIMS 25]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Spliceosome (snRNPs." Ul, U2, U4. U5, U6) removes introns (GU at 5, AG at 3) as lariats and joins exons. Anti-snRNP (anti-smith) antibodies in SLE.

mcqs.subject: Biochemistry
mcqs.question: A replicating bacterium makes fewer than one error per IO, bases because its main replicative enzyme corrects mismatches immediately. Which enzyme proofreads during replication. [WMC 26. MUL 25]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Proofreading = 345 exonuclease activity of Pol111 (E subunit) and Pol l in prokaryotes." Pol 6 and E in eukaryotes. Errors escaping it are corrected by mismatch repair.

mcqs.subject: Biochemistry
mcqs.question: During translation elongation, EF-TU (eEF-I) delivers aminoacyl-tRNA and EF-G (eEF-2) moves the ribosome. What is the energy source for elongation. [MUL 25]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Elongation uses 2 GTP per peptide bond (binding + translocation); amino acid activation uses ATP (4 AMP, = 2 high-energy bonds). Total = high-energy bonds per amino acid.

mcqs.subject: Biochemistry
mcqs.question: A lab performs PCR for COVID-19; the polymerase survives repeated heating to 95°C. Which enzyme is used at high temperature in PCR? [WMC 25 . QIMS 25]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Taq polymerase (Thermus aquaticus) is heat-stable (optimum 72 °C) but lacks 345 proofreading; Pfu polymerase has proofreading.

mcqs.subject: Biochemistry
mcqs.question: A cell line accumulates many short DNA fragments of 100-200 nucleotides on the lagging strand that are never joined. Deficiency of which enzyme causes this. [WMC 25]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: DNA ligase seals nicks between Okazaki fragments by forming a phosphodiester bond (ATP in eukaryotes, NAD. in E. coli). Bloom syndrome involves a helicase; DNA ligase I deficiency causes immunodeficiency.

mcqs.subject: Biochemistry
mcqs.question: A diabetic is prescribed insulin lispro, in which two amino acids at B28 and B29 are swapped to make it act faster. Which technique was used to produce it? [WMC 25. BWP 25]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Site-directed mutagenesis changes specific codons in a cloned gene (lispro: Pro B28 ￿ Lys B29) ￿ less hexamer formation, faster absorption.

mcqs.subject: Biochemistry
mcqs.question: A technician transfers DNA fragments separated by electrophoresis onto a membrane by capillary action. Which is the characteristic step of Southern blotting. [WMC 25]

options.B: Transfer of DNA fragments from gel to nitrocellulose/nylon

mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: The "blot" _ transfer from gel to membrane, preserving the separation pattern; denatured DNA then hybridizes with a labelled probe.

mcqs.subject: Biochemistry
mcqs.question: A 20-year-old with cystic f ibrosis enrolls in a gene therapy trial; only lung epithelial cells are targeted. In which cells is gene therapy currently performed in humans. [WMC 25]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Only somatic gene therapy is permitted," germline therapy is banned for ethical reasons (inheritable changes). First success: ADA-SCID (1990). Source item "best age = early adulthood" merged here.

mcqs.subject: Biochemistry
mcqs.question: A child with a single-gene disorder (ADA-SCID) is treated by inserting a normal copy of the gene into his own lymphocytes. Which treatment approach is this? [WMC 25]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Gene therapy replaces/adds a functional gene using viral (retro/lenti/AAV) or non-viral vectors; best suited for monogenic recessive disorders.

mcqs.subject: Biochemistry
mcqs.question: A biochemist lists the stages of protein synthesis in a hepatocyte. What is the first step of translation. [WMC 25]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Steps: (l) activation aminoacyl-tRNA synthetase charges tRNA using ATP; (2) initiation; (3) elongation; (4) termination. Key note." source keyed initiation (assembly), which follows amino acid activation.

mcqs.subject: Biochemistry
mcqs.question: A researcher studies the nucleoplasmic polymerase that transcribes tRNA genes and 5S rRNA. Which enzyme synthesizes 5S rRNA? [WMC 25]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: 5S rRNA is the only rRNA made by Pol111 (outside the nucleolus)," 28S, 18S, 5.8S rRNA by Pol l in the nucleolus.

mcqs.subject: Biochemistry
mcqs.question: A geneticist designing degenerate PCR primers prefers amino acids encoded by a single codon. Which amino acid is best for this purpose. [WMC 25]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Only methionine (AUG) and tryptophan (UGG) have a single codon," using them reduces primer degeneracy. Leucine, serine, arginine have six codons each.

mcqs.subject: Biochemistry
mcqs.question: A new drug (patisiran) silences the transthyretin gene in the liver. Which molecule inhibits translation of a specific MRNA? [BWP 25]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: SIRNA (perfectly complementary) 4 RISC cleaves target MRNA," MIRNA (partly complementary) ￿ translational repression. Both are ~21-23 nt.

mcqs.subject: Biochemistry
mcqs.question: A researcher uses a labelled CDNA probe to measure how much of a specific MRNA a tumour expresses. Which blot uses a CDNA probe to detect RNA? [BWP 25]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Northern blot: RNA separated by electrophoresis, transferred and hybridized with a labelled DNA (CDNA) probe 4 shows gene expression and transcript size.

mcqs.subject: Biochemistry
mcqs.question: A lab uses ECORI to cut a plasmid. What do restriction endonucleases cut? [BWP 25]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Bacterial restriction enzymes cut foreign dsDNA at palindromic sites; the bacterium protects its own DNA by methylation (restriction-modification system).

mcqs.subject: Biochemistry
mcqs.question: A microbiologist isolates extrachromosomal genetic elements carrying antibiotic resistance from E. coli. What is a plasmid? [BWP 25]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Plasmids." small, circular, double-stranded, self-replicating DNA; carry R factors, F factor and toxin genes; used as cloning vectors (insert up to -10 kb).

mcqs.subject: Biochemistry
mcqs.question: A single DNA template undergoes 20 cycles of PCR with perfect efficiency. About how many copies are produced? [BWP 25]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Each cycle doubles the product: 2, 1.05 x 10,; 30 cycles = IO, copies.

mcqs.subject: Biochemistry
mcqs.question: A student asks about the size limit of standard PCR products. Up to what length can routine PCR amplify DNA? [BWP 25]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Standard Taq PCR reliably amplifies up to -5- 10 kb; long-range PCR with enzyme mixtures can reach ~30-40 kb.

mcqs.subject: Biochemistry
mcqs.question: In PCR, after primer annealing the temperature is raised for strand extension. At what temperature does Taq polymerase work optimally. [BWP 25]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Denaturation 94- 96 °C, annealing 50-65 °C, extension 72 °C (Taq optimum).

mcqs.subject: Biochemistry
mcqs.question: A cell line has a mutation in primase. Which step of DNA replication is directly affected? [HITEC 26. KIMS 26 . QIMS 25]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: DNA polymerases cannot start de novo: primase (DNA-dependent RNA polymerase, part of Pol a in eukaryotes) lays down-10-nt RNA primers - one on the leading strand, one per Okazaki fragment.

mcqs.subject: Biochemistry
mcqs.question: A toxin selectively blocks RNA polymerase l in the nucleolus. Synthesis of which RNA is directly prevented? [QIMS 25]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Pol I transcribes the 45S pre-rRNA in the nucleolus, which is cleaved to 28S. 18S and 5.8S rRNA.

mcqs.subject: Biochemistry
mcqs.question: A student explains why ordinary E. coli polymerase cannot be used in automated PCR. Which step requires a thermostable DNA polymerase. [QIMS 25]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Polymerase acts during extension. but must survive every 95 °C denaturation step; Taq avoids adding fresh enzyme each cycle.

mcqs.subject: Biochemistry
mcqs.question: A teenager has early colorectal cancer; tumour testing shows defective mismatch repair genes. Which mutations accumulate. [QIMS 25]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Without MMR, slippage errors in repetitive sequences persist 4 small insertions/deletions (frameshifts) 4 microsatellite instability (Msl-high tumours).

mcqs.subject: Biochemistry
mcqs.question: A molecular biologist studies the E. coli Muts, MutL and MutH proteins. Which repair pathway uses Mut proteins. [CKMC 26. QIMS 25]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Muts recognizes the mismatch, MutL links, MutH nicks the unmethylated (new) strand at GATC: human homologues MSH2, MLHI (Lynch syndrome).

mcqs.subject: Biochemistry
mcqs.question: A sailor with bleeding gums and poor wound healing has scurvy. Collagen is unstable. Hydroxylation of proline and lysine residues in collagen requires which vitamin? [QIMS 25]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Prolyl and lysyl hydroxylases need ascorbate (keeps Fe" reduced) and O,, a-ketoglutarate; hydroxylation allows interchain H-bonds and triple-helix stability.

mcqs.subject: Biochemistry
mcqs.question: During elongation in a bacterial ribosome, the peptide bond is formed between the P-site and A-site amino acids. Which component joins the amino acids. [CKMC 26. QIMS 25]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Peptidyl transferase activity resides in 23S rRNA (28S in eukaryotes) of the large subunit - a ribozyme," inhibited by chloramphenicol.

mcqs.subject: Biochemistry
mcqs.question: A virologist detects an enzyme in HIV particles that copies the viral RNA genome into DNA. Which enzyme synthesizes DNA from RNA? [QIMS 25]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Reverse transcriptase (RNA-dependent DNA polymerase) of retroviruses,. also used to make CDNA in the lab (RT-PCR). Telomerase is a cellular reverse transcriptase.

mcqs.subject: Biochemistry
mcqs.question: A student compares the bacterial DNA polymerases. Which polymerase is mainly responsible for leading-strand synthesis in prokaryotes. [KIMS 25]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Pol111 holoenzyme (with F-clamp, highly processive) synthesizes both leading and lagging strands,. Pol I removes primers; Pol11, IV, V are repair polymerases.

mcqs.subject: Biochemistry
mcqs.question: A student compares replication in human cells and E. coli. Which feature is unique to eukaryotic replication. [KIMS 25]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Bacteria: single origin (oric); eukaryotes: thousands of origins (ARS) to replicate long chromosomes in S phase,. telomeres and histone assembly are also eukaryotic features.

mcqs.subject: Biochemistry
mcqs.question: A microbiologist studies the promoter of a bacterial gene recognized by the u factor of RNA polymerase. Which promoter element is recognized in prokaryotes. [KIMS 25]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Prokaryotic promoter: _IO Pribnow box + -35 TTGACA. Eukaryotic: TATA box (-25), CAAT box (-70), GC boxes, enhancers.

mcqs.subject: Biochemistry
mcqs.question: In a cell-free translation system, ribosomes assemble on MRNA and amino acids are added one by one. Which molecule brings amino acids to the ribosome? [KIMS 25]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Each aminoacyl-tRNA carries its amino acid on the 3-CCA end and pairs via its anticodon with the MRNA codon at the A site.

mcqs.subject: Biochemistry
mcqs.question: A child with sickle cell anaemia has GAG 4 GTG in the F-globin gene. Which type of point mutation produces a single amino acid change. [MUL 26 . KIMS 25]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Missense." one amino acid replaced (Hbs: Glu6Val). Conservative missense may have little effect; non-conservative changes charge or shape.

mcqs.subject: Biochemistry
mcqs.question: A molecular biologist notes that a newly made transcript receives a 7-methylguanosine at its 5 end. Which post-transcriptional modification protects MRNA from degradation and aids ribosome binding. [AMC 26. HITEC 26. KIMS 25]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: 5 cap: 7-methylguanosine linked 5-5 by triphosphate (methyl from SAM) 4 protects from 5 exonucleases. needed for splicing, export and translation initiation.

mcqs.subject: Biochemistry
mcqs.question: A family with @-thalassaemia has a mutation in the TATA box upstream of the P-globin gene. What does a promoter mutation cause. [KIMS 25]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Promoter mutations reduce RNA polymerase binding 4 less MRNA but normal protein structure (F'_thalassaemia).

mcqs.subject: Biochemistry
mcqs.question: A 40-year-old man with chorea has anticipation in his family, with earlier onset in each generation. Which disorder results from trinucleotide repeat expansion. [KIMS 25]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Trinucleotide repeat disorders: Huntington (CAG), myotonic dystrophy (CTG), fragile X (CGG), Friedreich ataxia (GAA), spinocerebellar ataxias (CAG). Anticipation = expansion across generations.

mcqs.subject: Biochemistry
mcqs.question: A lab must detect a point mutation in a child with recurrent infections and first makes millions of copies of the gene segment. Which technique is used? [KIMS 25]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: PCR amplifies a defined DNA segment exponentially using two flanking primers, dNTPs and thermostable polymerase; products are then sequenced or probed.

mcqs.subject: Biochemistry
mcqs.question: A forensic laboratory identifies remains using DNA inherited only from the mother, which has a high copy number and mutation rate. Which DNA is used? [KIMS 25]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: mtDNA: circular. 16.5 kb. 37genes, maternally inherited, no histones, poor repair 4 high mutation rate,. many copies per cell survive degradation. Diseases show heteroplasmy (MELAS, LHON).

mcqs.subject: Biochemistry
mcqs.question: A gene therapy vector carries a normal copy of a gene designed to replace a faulty one. Which property of DNA makes gene therapy (and probe detection) possible? [KIMS 25]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Complementary base pairing allows accurate replication, transcription, hybridization of probes/primers and homologous recombination of introduced genes.

mcqs.subject: Biochemistry
mcqs.question: A pharmaceutical company produces human insulin by inserting the gene into E. coli. Which is an example of recombinant DNA technology. [KIMS 25]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Recombinant DNA: cut gene and vector with the same restriction enzyme, ligate, transform host, select and express (insulin, GH, hepatitis B vaccine, factor Vlll).

mcqs.subject: Biochemistry
mcqs.question: During replication the double helix must be opened ahead of the fork using energy. Which replication protein requires ATP hydrolysis to unwind DNA? [AMC 26]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Helicase (DnaB in E. coli; MCM in eukaryotes) breaks H-bonds using ATP. SSB proteins keep strands apart without ATP. Defects: Bloom, Werner syndromes (RecQ helicases).

mcqs.subject: Biochemistry
mcqs.question: A student compares eukaryotic DNA polymerases. Which eukaryotic polymerase synthesizes the RNA-DNA primer. [AMC 26]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Pol a (with primase) initiates," Pol E elongates the leading strand; Pol 6 the lagging strand; Pol y replicates mitochondrial DNA: Pol F repairs.

mcqs.subject: Biochemistry
mcqs.question: Adenine in DNA is deaminated to hypoxanthine and the lesion escapes repair. What mutation results after replication. [AMC 26]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Hypoxanthine pairs with cytosine 4 next round G pairs with C ￿ A~T becomes G-C (transition). Cytosine deamination to uracil ￿ G-C to A-T. Repaired by base excision repair.

mcqs.subject: Biochemistry
mcqs.question: A patient on antituberculous therapy notices orange urine. Which part of bacterial RNA polymerase does rifampicin inhibit? [AMC 26. MUL 26 . KIMS 26]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Rifampicin binds the F subunit of DNA-dependent RNA polymerase 4 inhibits transcription (prokaryotic). Resistance from rpoB mutations. Induces cytochrome P450.

mcqs.subject: Biochemistry
mcqs.question: A researcher finds that a microRNA reduces translation of its target MRNA in a tumour cell line. Which complex mediates microRNA-associated silencing. [AMC 26]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: MIRNA genes 4 pri-miRNA (Drosha) 4 pre-miRNA (exported) 4 Dicer 4 mature MIRNA loaded onto Argonaute in RISC ￿ repression/degradation of target MRNA.

mcqs.subject: Biochemistry
mcqs.question: A student explains how the ribosome moves along MRNA after each peptide bond. In eukaryotes, which factor mediates translocation. [AMC 26. BWP 26]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: eEF-la (EF-TU) brings aminoacyl-tRNA to the A site," eEF-2 (EF-G) translocates the ribosome (target of diphtheria toxin). elF-2 brings Met-tRNAi,' eRF-I recognizes stop codons.

mcqs.subject: Biochemistry
mcqs.question: Two DNA samples have identical restriction sites f lanking a VNTR region, but one gives a longer fragment on Southern blot. What explains this. [AMC 26 . BWP 26]

options.A: A longer VNTR repeat region (more repeats)

mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: VNTRS (minisatellites) vary in repeat number between individuals ￿ fragment-length polymorphism used in DNA fingerprinting (Jeffreys). STRS (microsatellites) are used in modern forensics by PCR.

mcqs.subject: Biochemistry
mcqs.question: A paternity laboratory performs RFLP analysis. Which blotting technique detects the specific DNA sequences? [AMC 26]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: RFLP analysis." digest genomic DNA 4 electrophoresis 4 Southern blot ￿ probe for the polymorphic locus.

mcqs.subject: Biochemistry
mcqs.question: A lab tests a nasal swab for SARS-CoV-2 RNA. What is the first step in detecting viral RNA by RT-PCR? [AMC 26]

options.D: Convert RNA into complementary DNA with reverse transcriptase

mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Taq cannot copy RNA,. reverse transcriptase first makes CDNA, which is then amplified (qRT-PCR measures viral load).

mcqs.subject: Biochemistry
mcqs.question: A DNA regulatory sequence is moved several kilobases upstream of a promoter and still increases transcription in either orientation. What is the sequence. [AMC 26. BWP 26]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Enhancers bind activator proteins and act at a distance, in either orientation, upstream or downstream (via DNA looping and Mediator). Silencers bind repressors.

mcqs.subject: Biochemistry
mcqs.question: A molecular biologist notes that histone MRNAS lack a tail added after cleavage at AAUAAA. Which enzyme adds the poly-A tail to eukaryotic MRNA? [CKMC 26]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Poly(A) polymerase adds -200 adenylates without a template after endonucleolytic cleavage 10-30 nt downstream of A4UAAA.

mcqs.subject: Biochemistry
mcqs.question: A haematologist orders a blot to detect a deleted a-globin gene. What does Southern blotting detect? [CKMC 26]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Southern = DNA (deletions, RFLP, gene rearrangements); Northern = RNA; Western = protein.

mcqs.subject: Biochemistry
mcqs.question: In agarose gel electrophoresis, small DNA fragments migrate further than large ones. By what property does electrophoresis separate DNA fragments. [CKMC 26. KIMS 26]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: DNA has uniform negative charge per unit length (phosphates). so in a gel matrix it migrates towards the anode by size," smaller fragments move faster.

mcqs.subject: Biochemistry
mcqs.question: A cloning procedure joins a gene insert into a cut plasmid. Which enzyme joins DNA fragments by forming phosphodiester bonds? [CKMC 26]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: DNA ligase (T4 ligase in labs) seals 3-OH and 5-phosphate ends; joins Okazaki fragments in vivo and inserts into vectors in vitro.

mcqs.subject: Biochemistry
mcqs.question: A geneticist explains why two people's DNA yields different fragment patterns after digestion with the same enzyme. On what is RFLP analysis based? [CKMC 26]

options.A: Differences in number or position of restriction sites

mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: A SNP may create or abolish a restriction site (e.g. Mstll site lost in sickle cell mutation), or repeat number may vary between sites 4 fragments of different lengths.

mcqs.subject: Biochemistry
mcqs.question: A biotech student clones the human insulin gene in bacteria. In recombinant DNA technology, plasmids are commonly used as what? [CKMC 26]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Vectors: plasmids (< 10 kb), bacteriophage A (<20 kb), cosmids (<45 kb), BACs/YACs (100 kb- l Mb); they carry ori, selectable markers and cloning sites.

mcqs.subject: Biochemistry
mcqs.question: A student matches codons with their complementary triplets during translation. On which molecule is the anticodon present? [CKMC 26]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: The anticodon loop of tRNA pairs antiparallel with the MRNA codon (e.g. codon 5-AUG-3, anticodon 3-UAC-5).

mcqs.subject: Biochemistry
mcqs.question: A research team corrects a sickle cell mutation in a patient's stem cells by cutting the DNA at a guide-RNA-specified site. Which tool is used for targeted gene editing. [CKMC 26]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: CRISPR-Cas9: guide RNA directs the Cas9 nuclease to a matching sequence next to a PAM (NGG) ￿ double-strand break 4 repaired by NHEJ (knock-out) or HDR (precise correction).

mcqs.subject: Biochemistry
mcqs.question: A polymerase mutant lacking 345 exonuclease activity has a 100-fold higher mutation rate. What is the 345 exonuclease activity responsible for. [CKMC 26]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Proofreading removes a mismatched nucleotide immediately after insertion (backspace function),. primer removal needs 543 exonuclease (Pol l).

mcqs.subject: Biochemistry
mcqs.question: A student digests plasmid DNA with BamHI. What do restriction endonucleases do. [CKMC 26]

options.C: Cut DNA at specific recognition sequences

mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Type11 restriction enzymes recognize 4-8 bp palindromes and cleave within them; methylases (not endonucleases) protect host DNA.

mcqs.subject: Biochemistry
mcqs.question: A student lists processing steps of eukaryotic pre-mRNA. Which is NOT a post~transcriptional modification of MRNA? [CKMC 26]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Histone acetylation (HATS) is an epigenetic chromatin modification that loosens chromatin and increases transcription - it acts on DNA packaging, not on MRNA.

mcqs.subject: Biochemistry
mcqs.question: A patient with SLE has anti-smith antibodies directed against proteins required for MRNA processing. Which statement about intron removal is correct? [MUL 26]

options.A: 5 and 3 splice sites have identical sequences
options.B: The branch-point adenosine is removed first
options.C: Exons are joined before the intron is cut

mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Splicing: Ul binds 5 GU, U2 binds branch-pointA, which attacks the 5 site forming a lariat; exons are then joined. The 3 site is AG.

mcqs.subject: Biochemistry
mcqs.question: A promoter mutation 25 bp upstream of the transcription start site reduces initiation. What is the normal function of this sequence. [MUL 26]

options.C: Binds basal transcription factors (TFIIDnBP) for initiation

mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: TATA (Hogness) box at -25 binds TBP of TFIID. positioning RNA polymerase11; CAAT box (-70) and GC box bind other transcription factors.

mcqs.subject: Biochemistry
mcqs.question: A cell that normally maintains telomeres loses the RNA component of telomerase. What happens. [MUL 26]

options.A: Progressive shortening of telomeres with each division

mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Telomerase uses its own RNA (TERC) as template for TTAGGG repeats; without it, telomeres shorten (end-replication problem) ￿ senescence (Hayflick limit). Dyskeratosis congenita.

mcqs.subject: Biochemistry
mcqs.question: A student compares prokaryotic and eukaryotic translation. Which process occurs in both? [MUL 26]

options.A: Peptidyl-tRNA moves from the A site to the P site (translocation)

mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Shine-Dalgarno and fMet-tRNA are prokaryotic; 5 cap scanning is eukaryotic; translocation (EF-G / eEF-2 with GTP) is common to both.

mcqs.subject: Biochemistry
mcqs.question: Intestinal cells make apoB-48 while hepatocytes make apoB-100 from the same gene. How is apoB-48 produced? [MUL 26. HITEC 26]

options.D: RNA editing (C4U creates a stop codon)

mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: APOBEC-I deaminates C to U at codon 2153 of apoB MRNA in enterocytes 4 UAA stop codon ￿ truncated apoB-48 (48% of apoB-100).

mcqs.subject: Biochemistry
mcqs.question: A mutant E. coli cannot express the lac operon even when lactose is present (lacl super~repressor). Why. [MUL 26]

options.A: The repressor cannot bind the operator
options.C: The repressor cannot bind the inducer (allolactose)
options.D: RNA polymerase cannot bind any promoter

mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: lacl.: repressor binds the operator but not the inducer 4 permanently OFF (non-inducible). lacl- or operator (O,) mutations 4 constitutive expression.

mcqs.subject: Biochemistry
mcqs.question: A child with Prader-willi syndrome has a normal DNA sequence but abnormal silencing of genes on chromosome 15. Which is an epigenetic alteration that affects gene expression. [MUL 26]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Epigenetics = heritable changes in expression without sequence change: CpG methylation (silencing), histone modifications, imprinting (Prader-willi, Angelman), X-inactivation.

mcqs.subject: Biochemistry
mcqs.question: A student identifies the recognition site of ECORI. Which sequence shows perfect dyad symmetry (palindrome)? [MUL 26]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: A palindrome reads the same 543 on both strands: GAAThC/ complement C￿AAG read backwards = GAATTC. ECORI cuts G"AATTC giving sticky ends.

mcqs.subject: Biochemistry
mcqs.question: A gene~chip (microarray) experiment suggests a gene is overexpressed in breast cancer. Which technique can confirm the change in gene expression. [MUL 26]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Microarrays measure MRNA levels; confirmation is by Northern blot or quantitative R T-PCR (also MRNA). Western blot would confirm protein, a different level.

mcqs.subject: Biochemistry
mcqs.question: After transformation, bacteria are grown on ampicillin plates to find those that took up the plasmid. Which plasmid component allows this selection. [MUL 26]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Selection: antibiotic-resistance gene (only transformed cells grow). Screening for inserts: insertional inactivation of lacz (white colonies) or of a second resistance gene.

mcqs.subject: Biochemistry
mcqs.question: A geneticist describes regulatory elements controlling a gene. Which combination correctly describes cis- and trans-acting elements? [MUL 26]

options.C: DNA sequence cis-acting; regulatory protein trans-acting

mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Cis-acting elements (promoter, operator, enhancer) act only on the DNA molecule they lie on: trans-acting factors (repressor, CAP, transcription factors) are diffusible proteins acting on any copy.

mcqs.subject: Biochemistry
mcqs.question: When lactose enters E. coli, the lac operon is switched on. Which molecule binds the lac repressor and inactivates it? [WMC 26]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: F-galactosidase converts some lactose to allolactose (the natural inducer), which changes repressor shape so it leaves the operator. IPTG is a non-metabolizable inducer used in labs.

mcqs.subject: Biochemistry
mcqs.question: A boy with Becker muscular dystrophy has a mutation in the promoter of the dystrophin gene. Which process is most directly impaired? [HITEC 26]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: The promoter is the binding site for RNA polymerase and general transcription factors,. mutations reduce transcription initiation and the amount of normal protein.

mcqs.subject: Biochemistry
mcqs.question: A student asks which protein f irst recognizes the promoter of protein-coding genes in human cells. Which factor recognizes eukaryotic promoters. [HITEC 26]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: TFIID (TBP + TAFS) binds the TATA box, then TFIIB, Pol11-TFIIF, TFIIE and TFIIH (helicase, kinase phosphorylates CTD) assemble. Sigma factor is prokaryotic," rho is a termination factor.

mcqs.subject: Biochemistry
mcqs.question: A patient with acne takes doxycycline. Tetracyclines bind the 30S subunit and block aminoacyl-tRNA attachment. Which step is inhibited? [HITEC 26. BWP 26]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Tetracyclines block the A site 4 aminoacyl-tRNA cannot bind 4 elongation stops (bacteriostatic). Avoid in children (teeth staining) and with milk/antacids (chelation).

mcqs.subject: Biochemistry
mcqs.question: A ribosome reaches a UGA codon in the A site. Which molecule recognizes a stop codon. [HITEC 26]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: No tRNA reads stop codons; release factors (RFI, RF2 in bacteria; eRFI in eukaryotes, with GTP-bound RF3/eRF3) cause peptidyl transferase to hydrolyse the peptide from tRNA.

mcqs.subject: Biochemistry
mcqs.question: A man with scurvy has defective collagen. Vitamin C def iciency impairs hydroxylation of which amino acids in collagen? [HITEC 26]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Prolyl and lysyl hydroxylases (ascorbate-dependent) form hydroxyproline (helix stability) and hydroxylysine (glycosylation and cross-links).

mcqs.subject: Biochemistry
mcqs.question: A woman with ER-positive breast cancer is treated with tamoxifen, which binds the oestrogen receptor without activating it in breast tissue. What is its effect? [HITEC 26]

options.D: Inhibition of transcription of oestrogen-responsive genes

mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Steroid receptors are ligand-activated transcription factors (zinc-finger DNA-binding domain). Tamoxifen-ER complex recruits co-repressors in breast (antagonist) but acts as agonist in endometrium (cancer risk).

mcqs.subject: Biochemistry
mcqs.question: A child with suspected cystic fibrosis is tested for the common ￿F508 mutation. Which technique amplifies the CFfR gene segment for mutation detection? [HITEC 26]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: PCR amplifies the target region, then mutations are detected by sequencing, allele-specific primers/probes or fragment size (AF508 = 3-bp deletion). PCR also detects M. tuberculosis DNA (Genexpert).

mcqs.subject: Biochemistry
mcqs.question: Genomic DNA is digested with a restriction enzyme and probed to detect the sickle mutation, which abolishes an Mstll site. Which technique is used? [HITEC 26]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: The sickle mutation (A4T in codon 6) destroys an Mstll (CCTNAGG) site. so FS gives a larger fragment (1.35 kb vs 1.15 kb) on Southern blot.

mcqs.subject: Biochemistry
mcqs.question: A family asks what gene therapy aims to do for their child with a single-gene disorder. What is the primary goal of gene therapy. [HITEC 26]

options.B: Permanently delete the mutant gene in every case
options.C: Replace or supplement a defective gene with a functional one

mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Gene addition (most common), gene editing (CRISPR) or gene silencing (siRNA/antisense for dominant-negative alleles). Vectors: retro/lentivirus (integrating), AAV, adenovirus, liposomes.

mcqs.subject: Biochemistry
mcqs.question: A researcher wants to label DNA specifically in the Hershey-chase style experiment. Which radioactive isotope is commonly used to label DNA? [BWP 26] 3S 14 32 12S
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: DNA contains phosphorus but no sulfur 4 "P labels DNA (backbone phosphates)," "S labels protein (methionine, cysteine). '1 labels proteins/antibodies.

mcqs.subject: Biochemistry
mcqs.question: A student labels the regions of a mature eukaryotic MRNA. Which sequence lies between the 5 cap and the AUG start codon. [BWP 26]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: MRNA: 5 cap - 5 UTR (Kozak sequence around AUG." IRES in ferritin MRNA) - coding region - stop codon - 3 UTR (AAUA44. MIRNA sites) - poly-A tail.

mcqs.subject: Biochemistry
mcqs.question: A laboratory sequences a gene by the Sanger chain-termination method. Which group is absent from the dideoxynucleotides used? [BWP 26]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: ddNTPs lack both 2 and 3 OH; without the 3-OH no phosphodiester bond can form 4 chain termination. (Deoxyribose already lacks the 2-0H. so the key missing group is the 3-OH.)

mcqs.subject: Biochemistry
mcqs.question: A man with HIV is started on tenofovir and lamivudine. Which drug class inhibits viral reverse transcriptase. [BWP 26]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: NRTIS (zidovudine. tenofovir, lamivudine) are chain terminators lacking 3-OH; NNRTIS (efavirenz, nevirapine) bind an allosteric site. Neuraminidase inhibitors (oseltamivir) treat influenza.

mcqs.subject: Biochemistry
mcqs.question: A virologist studies how HIV DNA becomes part of the host chromosome. Which enzyme facilitates HIV integration into the host genome. [BWP 26]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: HIV integrase inserts the proviral DNA (blocked by raltegravir, dolutegravir); protease cleaves Gag-Pol polyproteins (blocked by "_navir" drugs).

mcqs.subject: Biochemistry
mcqs.question: A student identifies the DNA site where RNA polymerase binds to start transcribing a bacterial operon. What is this sequence called? [BWP 26]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Promoter (-10 and -35 elements) binds RNA polymerase holoenzyme (u factor); operator overlaps it and binds the repressor,. terminators are rho-dependent or hairpin (rho-independent).

mcqs.subject: Biochemistry
mcqs.question: A newborn is screened for sickle cell disease using a DNA test. Which method can detect the sickle mutation. [BWP 26]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: PCR-RFLP: amplify the F-globin segment then digest - the FS mutation abolishes the restriction site," also allele-specific oligonucleotide probes or sequencing. Hb electrophoresis/HPLC detects the protein.

mcqs.subject: Biochemistry
mcqs.question: A cell repairs a uracil that arose from cytosine deamination; the first enzyme cleaves the abnormal base from its sugar. DNA glycosylase initiates which repair pathway. [KIMS 26]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: BER: glycosylase removes the damaged base 4 AP endonuclease 4 Pol F fills 4 ligase. Handles deamination, oxidation (8-oxoG), alkylation. Source had no options.

mcqs.subject: Biochemistry
mcqs.question: A patient with small-cell lung cancer receives etoposide, which traps the enzyme that cuts and reseals DNA ahead of the replication fork. Which enzyme does etoposide inhibit? [HITEC 26]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Stem created: the source recall was incomplete (chemotherapy/unwinding question was incomplete). Topoisomerase l inhibitors: irinotecan, topotecan,. topoisomerase11 inhibitors: etoposide, doxorubicin,. bacterial gyrase: fluoroquinolones.

mcqs.subject: Biochemistry
mcqs.question: The template (antisense) strand of a gene is 3-TACGGA-5. What is the MRNA transcribed from it? [BWP 26]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Stem created: the source recall was incomplete (the DNA sequence was missing). MRNA is complementary to the template strand and identical to the coding strand with U in place of T, synthesized 543.

mcqs.subject: Biochemistry
mcqs.question: A gene contains the template-strand DNA sequence 3-CGG CGG-5. What is the MRNA sequence transcribed from this region? [WMC 25]
mcqs.explanation: Exam Pearl: Stem created: the source recall was incomplete (original garbled: "CAG binds cytosine abnormally - resulting MRNA GCC GCC"). G pairs with C, so template 3-CGG CGG-5 gives MRNA 5-GCC GCC-3 (codons for alanine).
